title: Cantor’s Theorem
objects: 𝑉a vector space over a field 𝑘; 𝑉∗= Hom𝑘(𝑉, 𝑘) its algebraic dual.
structure: For infinite-dimensional 𝑉with basis 𝐵, dim 𝑉∗= |𝑘||𝐵| > |𝐵| = dim 𝑉. The dual is strictly larger, mirroring |𝐴| < |𝒫(𝐴)|.
reduction: Replace the power set by the dual space; the characteristic-function bijection 𝒫(𝐵) ≅{0, 1}𝐵becomes the coordinate description of 𝑉∗over 𝔽2.
status: Exact linear analogue. Over 𝔽2 the two statements coincide exactly.

title: Cantor–Schröder–Bernstein Theorem
objects: Injective linear maps between vector spaces.
structure: True for vector spaces, since dimension is a complete invariant and injectivity forces dim 𝑉≤dim 𝑊. Notably false for general modules, and false for Banach spaces under isomorphic embedding.
reduction: Injections of sets become injective linear maps; cardinality becomes dimension.
status: Exact linear analogue, in Vect only.

title: Cardinality of the Continuum
objects: ℝregarded as a vector space over ℚ.
structure: A Hamel basis has cardinality 𝔠, not ℵ0; its existence requires the axiom of choice and no explicit basis can be written down.
reduction: 2ℵ0 = |ℝ| becomes a statement about the dimension of a concrete infinite-dimensional space.

title: Continuum Hypothesis
objects: Vector spaces over ℚof intermediate dimension.
structure: CH is equivalent to the non-existence of such a space. Independent of ZFC, so this is undecidable as stated.
reduction: Cardinals become dimensions; every cardinal is the dimension of some space, so nothing is lost.

title: Generalised Continuum Hypothesis
objects: Dual space of an infinite-dimensional space.
structure: Under GCH the dual jumps exactly one cardinal. Without GCH the dual dimension is only bounded, not determined.
reduction: Cardinal exponentiation becomes the dimension of the dual.

title: Cardinal Arithmetic (Infinite Absorption)
objects: Direct sum and tensor product of infinite-dimensional spaces.
structure: Both bilinear constructions collapse to the maximum once either factor is infinite-dimensional. Only Hom(𝑉, 𝑊) — the exponential — grows.
reduction: Cardinal sum becomes ⊕, cardinal product becomes ⊗, exponentiation becomes Hom.

title: König’s Theorem (Cardinal Form)
objects: Direct sum versus direct product over an index set.
structure: The gap between ⊕and ∏is the whole content: they agree for finite 𝐼and diverge sharply for infinite 𝐼.
reduction: Cardinal sum and product become the two coproduct/product constructions in Vect.

title: Beth Numbers
objects: Iterated algebraic duals over 𝔽2.
structure: Each dual strictly increases dimension, so the canonical map 𝑉→𝑉∗∗is injective but never surjective in infinite dimensions.
reduction: Iterated power sets become iterated dual spaces.

title: Ordinal Successor and Limit
objects: A transfinite filtration of nested subspaces. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 10
structure: Successor steps adjoin one basis vector; limit steps take the directed colimit, which in Vect is the union of the chain.
reduction: Von Neumann’s 𝛼∪{𝛼} becomes adjoining a basis vector.

title: Cofinality
objects: Chains of subspaces exhausting 𝑉.
structure: A space is never the union of fewer than cf(dim 𝑉) proper subspaces. The finite case is the standard result that a vector space over an infinite field is never a finite union of proper subspaces. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 11
reduction: Cofinal subsets of a cardinal become exhausting chains of subspaces.

title: Russell’s Paradox
objects: None. The construction 𝑅= {𝑥∶𝑥∉𝑥} has no vector-space counterpart.
structure: Self-membership is not expressible for vectors; the closest linear phenomenon — a space isomorphic to its own dual or endomorphism algebra — is consistent, not paradoxical.
reduction: Not available.
status: No faithful linear form. The paradox is about unrestricted comprehension, which linear algebra never assumes.

title: Axiom Schema of Separation
objects: 𝐴a linear operator on 𝑉.
structure: Subspaces are carved from 𝑉by linear conditions only. Arbitrary subsets are not subspaces, exactly paralleling separation’s restriction to subsets of an existing set.
reduction: The predicate 𝜑becomes a linear condition; the resulting subset becomes a subspace.
status: Structural analogue rather than a theorem restatement.

title: Axiom Schema of Replacement
objects: 𝐴∶𝑉→𝑊linear; 𝑈≤𝑉a subspace.
structure: The image of a subspace under a linear map is a subspace, with dim 𝐴(𝑈) = dim 𝑈−dim(𝑈∩ker 𝐴).
reduction: Definable class functions become linear maps; images of sets become images of subspaces.

title: Axiom of Foundation
objects: 𝑁a nilpotent operator on a finite-dimensional space.
structure: Nilpotency gives a well-founded filtration 𝑉⊃𝑁𝑉⊃𝑁2𝑉⊃⋯⊃0 that terminates, mirroring the ban on infinite ∈-descent.
reduction: Membership descent becomes repeated application of a nilpotent operator.

title: Cumulative Hierarchy
objects: A complete flag or filtration of 𝑉.
structure: Each stage is a subspace; the associated graded object ⨁𝑉𝛼+1/𝑉𝛼recovers the whole space and is the linear analogue of rank.
reduction: Rank in the cumulative hierarchy becomes position in the filtration.

title: Axiom of Choice
objects: A spanning, linearly independent set 𝐵⊆𝑉.
structure: Equivalent to AC over ZF (Blass, 1984). Every short exact sequence of vector spaces splits, which is the same fact in different clothing.
reduction: Simultaneous choice from a family becomes the selection of a basis.
status: Exact linear analogue — and the single most-used consequence of AC in mathematics.

title: Zorn’s Lemma
objects: The poset of linearly independent subsets of 𝑉ordered by inclusion.
structure: The union of a chain of independent sets is independent, since independence is a finitary condition. A maximal independent set is a basis.
reduction: The abstract poset becomes the poset of independent subsets.
status: Exact linear analogue; this is the standard proof that bases exist.

title: Well-Ordering Theorem
objects: An ordinal-indexed basis.
structure: Permits transfinite Gram–Schmidt and construction of operators by transfinite recursion on coordi- nates.
reduction: Well-ordering a set becomes well-ordering a basis.

title: Transfinite Induction
objects: A property of subspaces along a filtration.
structure: The finite-dimensional case is ordinary induction on dimension — the workhorse proof technique for matrix normal forms.
reduction: Induction over ordinals becomes induction along a filtration or on dimension.

title: De Morgan’s Laws
objects: Subspaces 𝑈, 𝑊≤𝑉with 𝑉an inner product space; ⟂the orthogonal complement.
structure: ⟂is an order-reversing involution on the subspace lattice, exactly as complementation is on the Boolean lattice of sets. In matrix terms, ker(𝐴)⟂= im(𝐴⊤).
reduction: Union becomes sum, intersection stays intersection, complement becomes orthogonal complement.
status: Exact linear analogue. The subspace lattice is modular but not distributive, so not every Boolean identity survives.
also_in: Computer Science, Electrical Engineering. Logic and Foundations

title: Gödel’s First Incompleteness Theorem
objects: None. Provability is not a linear operator on any natural space of sentences.
structure: Encoding sentences as vectors over 𝔽2 makes the syntax linear but leaves derivability nonlinear and, worse, only semi-decidable.
reduction: Not available.
status: No faithful linear form. Incompleteness is about recursive enumerability, which linear structure does not capture.

title: Gödel’s Second Incompleteness Theorem
objects: None.
structure: As above; the derivability conditions are not preserved by any linearisation of provability.
reduction: Not available.

title: Diagonal (Fixed-Point) Lemma
objects: 𝐴a linear operator; 𝑣a fixed point up to scale. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 23
structure: The eigenvalue equation is the linear fixed-point statement. Existence over ℂfollows from the funda- mental theorem of algebra; over ℝit may fail, as for a rotation.
reduction: Self-reference 𝜑⟺𝜓(⌜𝜑⌝) becomes self-consistency 𝐴𝑣= 𝜆𝑣.
status: Analogy only. The eigenvalue equation shares the fixed-point form but none of the self-referential content.

title: Tarski’s Undefinability Theorem
objects: A hypothetical truth functional on the space of coded sentences. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 24
structure: No linear functional can decide truth, since the truth set is not a subspace — it is not closed under addition of sentence codes.
reduction: The truth predicate becomes a candidate linear functional; the obstruction is that truth is not linear.
status: Analogy only, though the failure of linearity is itself the honest point.

title: Compactness Theorem
objects: An infinite system of linear equations over a field. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 25
structure: True for linear systems: finite solvability implies solvability, by an inverse-limit or ultraproduct argu- ment. This is the linear-algebraic shadow of compactness.
reduction: Sentences become linear equations; satisfiability becomes solvability.
status: Exact linear analogue for systems over a field. Fails over general rings.

title: Löwenheim–Skolem Theorem
objects: Subspaces of prescribed dimension. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 26
structure: The theory of infinite-dimensional vector spaces over a fixed countable field is 𝜅-categorical for un- countable 𝜅— a textbook example of an uncountably categorical theory.
reduction: Model cardinality becomes dimension.
status: Exact linear analogue; vector spaces are the standard illustration of the theorem.

title: Gödel Completeness Theorem
objects: 𝐴a coeﬀicient matrix; b a right-hand side.
structure: Semantic consequence (solvability) equals syntactic consequence (no obstruction from the left null space). This is the Fredholm alternative, the linear completeness theorem. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 27
reduction: Entailment becomes membership in the column space; derivability becomes orthogonality to the cokernel.

title: Peano Induction Axiom
objects: A property of 𝑛-dimensional spaces.
structure: Induction on dimension is the standard proof scheme for Jordan form, Schur triangularisation, and the spectral theorem.
reduction: Induction on ℕbecomes induction on dimension. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 28

title: Modus Ponens
objects: 𝑃an idempotent projection, 𝑃2 = 𝑃.
structure: Detachment corresponds to applying an operator and retaining the image. Over 𝔽2, resolution and modus ponens become Gaussian elimination on a clause matrix.
reduction: Inference becomes operator application; the rule chain becomes a matrix product.
status: Analogy, exact for the 𝔽2 resolution encoding.

title: Cut Rule (Sequent Calculus)
objects: Derivations as linear maps between spaces of sequents.
structure: Cut is composition of matrices. Cut elimination says every composite factors through a normal form, at the cost of a possibly non-elementary blow-up in size — analogous to expressing a product explicitly rather than as a factorisation.
reduction: Lemma use becomes matrix multiplication.

title: Curry–Howard Correspondence
objects: Tensor–hom adjunction in Vect𝑘.
structure: This is currying, literally: implication becomes Hom, conjunction becomes ⊗. Linear logic was constructed to make this correspondence exact, with Vect a model.
reduction: Types become vector spaces; programs become linear maps.
status: Exact linear analogue for the multiplicative fragment. Contraction and weakening fail, which is precisely why the logic is called linear.
also_in: Computer Science. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 31

title: Beta Reduction (Lambda Calculus)
objects: The evaluation map, itself linear.
structure: Application is the counit of the tensor–hom adjunction. Substitution becomes composition, which is bilinear.
reduction: (𝜆𝑥.𝑀)𝑁→𝑀[𝑥∶= 𝑁] becomes evaluation of a linear map at a vector.
status: Exact linear analogue for the linear fragment; a variable used twice has no linear counterpart.
also_in: Computer Science. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 32

title: Y Combinator (Fixed-Point Combinator)
objects: 𝐴with spectral radius 𝜌(𝐴) < 1; x∗the unique fixed point.
structure: The Neumann series is the linear fixed-point combinator: it constructs the fixed point by unbounded self-application, converging exactly when 𝜌(𝐴) < 1.
reduction: 𝑌𝑓= 𝑓(𝑌𝑓) becomes x∗= 𝐴x∗+ b.
status: Exact linear analogue, with a convergence condition the untyped calculus does not need.

title: Church Numerals
objects: Powers of a fixed operator 𝐴.
structure: The map 𝑛↦𝐴𝑛is a monoid homomorphism (ℕ, +) →(End 𝑉, ∘). With 𝐴the nilpotent Jordan block, 𝐴𝑛shifts 𝑛places and 𝐴𝑑= 0 caps the arithmetic at dimension 𝑑.
reduction: 𝑛-fold composition of an abstract 𝑓becomes the 𝑛-th power of a matrix.

title: Kripke Forcing Relation
objects: 𝑅∈{0, 1}𝑛×𝑛the accessibility matrix; x ∈{0, 1}𝑛the valuation vector.
structure: Over the Boolean semiring, □𝜑is matrix-vector product with universal quantification, ♢𝜑with existential. Frame conditions become matrix conditions: reflexive ⟺ 𝐼≤𝑅, transitive ⟺ 𝑅2 ≤𝑅, symmetric ⟺𝑅= 𝑅⊤.
reduction: Possible worlds become basis vectors; accessibility becomes a matrix.
status: Exact linear analogue over the Boolean semiring, not over a field.

title: Heyting Algebra Implication
objects: Subspaces of 𝑉; the residual (𝑊∶𝑈′) the largest subspace whose intersection with 𝑈′ lies in 𝑊.
structure: Residuation makes the subspace lattice a quantale, giving an intuitionistic-style implication. Double negation fails, since 𝑈⟂⟂= 𝑈only in finite dimensions or for closed subspaces.
reduction: Lattice meet becomes intersection; relative pseudo-complement becomes residuation.
status: Structural analogue. The subspace lattice is orthomodular, not Heyting — this gap is the mathematical content of quantum logic.

title: Boolean Algebra Axioms
objects: 𝑃an orthogonal projection; 𝑃⟂= 𝐼−𝑃.
structure: Commuting projections form a Boolean algebra. Non-commuting projections do not, and 𝑃∧𝑄is then not 𝑃𝑄— the algebraic origin of quantum indeterminacy.
reduction: ∨, ∧, ¬ become +, ⋅, 𝐼−on projections.
status: Exact linear analogue for commuting families only.

title: Stone Representation
objects: A commutative algebra of projections; 𝑋its spectrum.
structure: The spectral theorem for commuting self-adjoint operators is Stone duality in analytic form: every such algebra is an algebra of functions on a space.
reduction: Ultrafilters become points of the spectrum; clopen sets become spectral projections.
status: Exact linear analogue — the spectral theorem is Stone duality.

title: Craig Interpolation
objects: Factorisation through a space of minimal dimension.
structure: Any linear map factors through its image, and the interpolating space has dimension exactly the rank. The shared vocabulary of the logical statement becomes the shared rank.
reduction: The interpolant 𝜃becomes the intermediate space in the rank factorisation 𝐴= 𝐶𝐷.
status: Exact linear analogue; rank factorisation is interpolation.

title: Skolem Normal Form
objects: 𝐵+ the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse.
structure: The existential witness becomes an explicit linear function of x, exactly as Skolemisation replaces ∃𝑦 by 𝑓(𝑥). Solvable for all x precisely when im 𝐴⊆im 𝐵.
reduction: The Skolem function becomes the pseudoinverse.

title: Composition and Identity Laws
objects: Matrices 𝐴∈𝑘𝑚×𝑛, 𝐵∈𝑘𝑝×𝑚, 𝐶∈𝑘𝑞×𝑝.
structure: Associativity of matrix multiplication and the identity matrix are exactly the category axioms; Mat𝑘 is the skeleton of Vectfd 𝑘.
reduction: Objects become dimensions, morphisms become matrices.
status: Exact linear analogue — matrices are the canonical example of a category.

title: Functor Laws
objects: 𝐹a representation, or a construction such as 𝑉↦𝑉⊗𝑊.
structure: A functor into Vect is precisely a representation. For a group 𝐺, 𝜌(𝑔ℎ) = 𝜌(𝑔)𝜌(ℎ) and 𝜌(𝑒) = 𝐼are the functor laws written out.
reduction: Structure-preserving maps of categories become representations by matrices.

title: Natural Transformation Square
objects: 𝜂a family of matrices, one per object.
structure: An intertwiner. For group representations, 𝜂𝜌1(𝑔) = 𝜌2(𝑔)𝜂for all 𝑔; Schur’s lemma says such an 𝜂 between irreducibles is zero or invertible.
reduction: Naturality becomes the intertwining relation.
status: Exact linear analogue — naturality is equivariance.

title: Yoneda Lemma
objects: The representable functor Hom(𝑉, −).
structure: Taking 𝑉= 𝑘gives Hom(𝑘, 𝑊) ≅𝑊: a vector is a linear map from the ground field. This is the everyday linear-algebra shadow of Yoneda.
reduction: Determination by hom-sets becomes determination by the action on the ground field.

title: Adjunction (Hom-Set Bijection)
objects: Tensor–hom adjunction, −⊗𝑉⊣Hom(𝑉, −).
structure: The universal property of the tensor product: bilinear maps 𝑈× 𝑉→𝑊correspond to linear maps 𝑈⊗𝑉→𝑊. Left adjoints preserve direct sums, right adjoints preserve products.
reduction: The abstract adjunction becomes the defining property of ⊗.
status: Exact linear analogue — the motivating example of an adjunction.

title: Triangle Identities
objects: coev ∶𝑘→𝑉⊗𝑉∗and ev ∶𝑉∗⊗𝑉→𝑘.
structure: In coordinates, coev(1) = ∑𝑖𝑒𝑖⊗𝑒𝑖and the identities reduce to ∑𝑖𝑒𝑖(𝑣)𝑒𝑖= 𝑣— the completeness relation. The trace is ev ∘coev, giving tr 𝐼= dim 𝑉.
reduction: Unit and counit become coevaluation and evaluation.
status: Exact linear analogue; these identities are why finite-dimensional spaces are dualisable.

title: Universal Property of the Product
objects: 𝜋𝑉, 𝜋𝑊the projection matrices; ⟨𝑓, 𝑔⟩the stacked matrix ( 𝑓 𝑔).
structure: The pairing is literally vertical concatenation of matrices; the projections are the block rows of the identity.
reduction: The universal cone becomes block matrix stacking.

title: Universal Property of the Coproduct
objects: [𝑓, 𝑔] the horizontally concatenated matrix ( 𝑓𝑔).
structure: In Vect finite products and coproducts coincide — ⊕is a biproduct. This self-duality is special to additive categories and fails in Set.
reduction: The universal cocone becomes horizontal block concatenation.
status: Exact linear analogue, with biproduct collapse as a bonus.

title: Limit as a Universal Cone
objects: Φ the block matrix assembling all compatibility conditions.
structure: Every finite limit in Vect is the kernel of an explicitly constructible block matrix; kernels, products, and pullbacks are all instances.
reduction: Universal cones become kernels of assembled block matrices.

title: Colimit as a Universal Cocone
objects: Ψ the block matrix of identification relations.
structure: Dual to the limit case: every finite colimit is a cokernel. Direct sums, pushouts, and coequalisers are all instances.
reduction: Gluing becomes quotienting by the image of a block matrix.

title: Pullback Square
objects: 𝐴∶𝑉→𝑋, 𝐵∶𝑊→𝑋; the pullback is the null space of the stacked map.
structure: dim(𝑉×𝑋𝑊) = dim 𝑉+ dim 𝑊−rank (𝐴 −𝐵). When both maps are surjective this equals dim 𝑉+ dim 𝑊−dim 𝑋.
reduction: The fibre product becomes a null space.

title: Equaliser
objects: Parallel maps 𝐴, 𝐵∶𝑉→𝑊.
structure: Equalisers are kernels of differences; in an additive category the two notions coincide, which is why Vect needs only kernels and cokernels.
reduction: The solution set of 𝐴𝑣= 𝐵𝑣becomes a null space. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 51

title: Monad Laws
objects: 𝑇(𝑉) = 𝑉⊗𝐴for 𝐴an associative unital algebra; 𝜇from multiplication, 𝜂from the unit.
structure: The monad laws become exactly associativity and unitality of 𝐴. Algebras over this monad are 𝐴-modules — that is, representations.
reduction: The abstract monad becomes an associative algebra; its algebras become modules.

title: Kan Extension
objects: Induced representation as a left Kan extension along 𝐻↪𝐺.
structure: Frobenius reciprocity Hom𝐺(Ind𝐺 𝐻𝑊, 𝑈) ≅Hom𝐻(𝑊, Res𝐺 𝐻𝑈) is the adjunction, and dim Ind𝐺 𝐻𝑊= [𝐺∶𝐻] dim 𝑊.
reduction: Left Kan extension becomes induction; restriction is the right adjoint.
status: Exact linear analogue — induced representations are the standard concrete Kan extension.

title: Subobject Classifier
objects: None. Vect𝑘has no subobject classifier.
structure: Subspaces of 𝑉are not classified by maps into a fixed object: the subspace lattice of 𝑘𝑛is the Grassmannian ⨆𝑟Gr(𝑟, 𝑛), a variety rather than a representing object. Vect is abelian but not a topos.
reduction: Not available.
status: No faithful linear form — and the obstruction is informative, since it is exactly why linear algebra is not a setting for internal logic.

title: Sheaf Gluing Axiom
objects: 𝑑the Čech differential, a block matrix of restriction maps with alternating signs.
structure: The sheaf condition is exactness at the first two spots: ℱ(𝑈) = ker 𝑑. Failure of exactness further along is measured by 𝐻𝑘= ker 𝑑𝑘/ im 𝑑𝑘−1, a quotient of vector spaces.
reduction: Gluing becomes a kernel; obstruction to gluing becomes cohomology.
status: Exact linear analogue for sheaves of vector spaces.

title: Exactness Condition
objects: 𝐴∶𝑈→𝑉, 𝐵∶𝑉→𝑊.
structure: Exactness is a rank condition. The homology ker 𝐵/ im 𝐴has dimension dim 𝑉−rank 𝐴−rank 𝐵, and vanishes exactly when the rank equation holds.
reduction: The image-equals-kernel condition becomes a rank identity.

title: Five Lemma
objects: A commutative ladder of matrices between two exact rows.
structure: Provable by rank counting alone in Vect: the alternating sum of dimensions in an exact sequence vanishes, so the middle rank is forced.
reduction: Diagram chase becomes dimension bookkeeping.
status: Exact linear analogue, and much easier in Vect than in general abelian categories.

title: Snake Lemma
objects: 𝜕the connecting map, constructed as 𝜕= 𝛾−1𝐵𝛽−1 on representatives.
structure: Exactness of the six-term sequence forces the alternating dimension sum to vanish, giving a rank identity relating the three columns.
reduction: The connecting homomorphism becomes a composite of a section, a matrix, and a quotient.

title: Euler’s Identity
objects: 𝐽the standard complex structure, 𝐽2 = −𝐼; exp the matrix exponential.
structure: 𝑒𝑖𝜃becomes exp(𝜃𝐽) = 𝑅(𝜃), the rotation group 𝑆𝑂(2) as a one-parameter subgroup with generator 𝐽. Setting 𝜃= 𝜋gives −𝐼.
reduction: The complex unit becomes a real 2×2 matrix; complex multiplication becomes matrix multiplication.
status: Exact linear analogue — and arguably the more revealing form, since it exhibits 𝑖as a rotation.

title: Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
objects: 𝐶𝑝the companion matrix of a monic polynomial 𝑝.
structure: Roots of 𝑝are eigenvalues of 𝐶𝑝, so the theorem says every complex matrix has an eigenvalue — equivalently, every complex matrix is triangularisable (Schur). Root-finding and eigenvalue computation are the same problem, and this is how modern root-finders actually work.
reduction: Polynomial factorisation becomes eigenvalue decomposition.

title: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
objects: The positive rationals as a free ℤ-module on the primes.
structure: Unique factorisation is exactly the statement that the primes form a basis. Multiplication becomes vector addition, gcd becomes componentwise minimum, and lcm componentwise maximum.
reduction: Prime exponents become coordinates.
status: Exact linear analogue over ℤ— a free module, not a vector space.

title: Binomial Theorem
objects: 𝑁nilpotent (or any matrix commuting with 𝐼); 𝑃the lower-triangular Pascal matrix.
structure: 𝑃= exp(𝑆) with 𝑆the subdiagonal matrix 𝑆𝑖,𝑖−1 = 𝑖, and 𝑃−1 has entries (−1)𝑖−𝑗(𝑖 𝑗) — binomial inversion. Requires commutativity: (𝐴+ 𝐵)𝑛has no such expansion when 𝐴𝐵≠𝐵𝐴.
reduction: Scalar binomial expansion becomes expansion of a matrix power, valid only for commuting terms.
status: Exact linear analogue under commutativity; the non-commuting case is the origin of the Baker–Campbell– Hausdorff formula.

title: Pigeonhole Principle
objects: A linear map from a larger to a smaller space.
structure: Rank–nullity gives dim ker 𝐴≥𝑛−𝑚> 0. More vectors than dimensions forces linear dependence — the pigeonhole principle of linear algebra, and the reason every homogeneous underdetermined system has a nontrivial solution.
reduction: Objects become vectors, boxes become dimensions, collision becomes linear dependence.

title: Galois Correspondence
objects: 𝐾as an 𝐹-vector space; Gal(𝐾/𝐹) acting by 𝐹-linear maps.
structure: Each 𝜎∈Gal(𝐾/𝐹) is an 𝐹-linear operator on 𝐾satisfying 𝜎𝑚= 𝐼, hence diagonalisable when char 𝐹∤𝑚. Artin’s linear independence of characters says distinct automorphisms are linearly independent in End𝐹(𝐾), which is what forces |Gal| ≤dim𝐹𝐾. Intermediate fields are the 𝐻-invariant subspaces.
reduction: Field extensions become vector spaces; automorphisms become commuting operators; intermediate fields become invariant subspaces.
status: Exact linear analogue — the whole correspondence is invariant-subspace theory for a finite group of operators.

title: Kolmogorov Axioms
objects: A probability vector on the simplex Δ𝑛−1.
structure: Probability is a non-negative linear functional of total mass one. Countable additivity is linearity extended to infinite sums; the simplex is the convex hull of the basis vectors, so every distribution is a convex combination of point masses.
reduction: The measure becomes a non-negative unit-sum vector.

title: Conditional Probability
objects: A diagonal projection followed by renormalisation.
structure: Conditioning is the projection 𝐷𝐴(idempotent, 𝐷2 𝐴= 𝐷𝐴) composed with rescaling. The projection is linear; the renormalisation is not, which is the sole nonlinearity in the whole of elementary probability.
reduction: Conditioning becomes a diagonal projection plus normalisation.

title: Chain Rule (Multiplication Rule)
objects: A product of conditional transition matrices.
structure: The joint distribution factorises as a product of stochastic matrices, one per variable — exactly the structure of a Bayesian network. The joint over 𝑛binary variables is a vector of length 2𝑛; factorisation is a low-rank tensor decomposition of it.
reduction: The joint becomes a product of conditional matrices.

title: Law of Total Probability
objects: 𝑇a column-stochastic transition matrix.
structure: Marginalisation is matrix–vector multiplication. Stochasticity (1⊤𝑇= 1⊤) guarantees the result stays on the simplex, so 𝑇maps the simplex into itself.
reduction: Total probability becomes a stochastic matrix product.

title: Bayes’ Theorem
objects: ℓthe likelihood vector; the update is diagonal scaling plus normalisation.
structure: Bayesian updating is componentwise multiplication followed by renormalisation — a diagonal operator on the simplex. Sequential updates compose as products of diagonal matrices, hence commute: the order of evidence does not matter.
reduction: The update becomes a diagonal rescaling.

title: Independence
objects: The joint distribution matrix 𝑃𝑖𝑗.
structure: Independence is exactly 𝑃= pq⊤— the joint is a rank-one outer product. Dependence is the departure from rank one, and the singular values beyond the first quantify how much dependence there is; mutual information is a function of that spectrum.
reduction: Independence becomes rank one.
status: Exact linear. One of the sharpest translations in the compendium.

title: Conditional Independence
objects: Each conditional slice of the joint tensor has rank one.
structure: The joint tensor 𝑃𝑖𝑗𝑘has every 𝑘-slice of rank one, so 𝑃has a rank-|𝐶| nonnegative tensor decomposi- tion. This is exactly the structure exploited by latent variable models and by nonnegative matrix factorisation.
reduction: Conditional independence becomes slicewise rank one.

title: Inclusion–Exclusion for Probabilities
objects: Möbius inversion on the subset lattice. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 9
structure: Identical to the combinatorial version: multiplication by 𝑍−1 where 𝑍is the unitriangular subset- containment matrix. The Bonferroni inequalities are truncations of this triangular solve, alternately over- and under-estimating.
reduction: The alternating sum becomes a triangular matrix inverse.

title: Borel–Cantelli Lemmas
objects: Summability of a sequence.
structure: The first lemma is subadditivity of a positive linear functional applied to tails — the union bound taken to the limit. The second requires independence, hence rank-one joints, and is not a consequence of linearity alone.
reduction: The first lemma is the union bound; the second needs independence. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 10

title: Kolmogorov Zero-One Law
objects: The tail 𝜎-algebra.
structure: Tail events are measurable with respect to a limit of 𝜎-algebras and independent of every finite prefix, forcing 𝑃(𝐴) = 𝑃(𝐴)2. The idempotence 𝑥= 𝑥2 is the same algebra as 𝑃2 = 𝑃for a projection — the eigenvalues of a projection are 0 and 1.
reduction: The dichotomy becomes idempotence.

title: Cumulative Distribution Function
objects: The cumulative-sum matrix.
structure: 𝐹is 𝑆p and p = 𝑆−1F with 𝑆−1 the bidiagonal difference matrix — the discrete fundamental theorem of calculus. Monotonicity of 𝐹is non-negativity of p.
reduction: Integration of the density becomes cumulative summation.

title: Probability Density Function
objects: The density as a non-negative vector against a quadrature weight vector.
structure: The continuous analogue of the probability vector; all linear functionals of the distribution are w⊤(g⊙f) for some g. Densities live in the positive cone of 𝐿1.
reduction: The density becomes a weighted non-negative vector.

title: Expectation
objects: Inner product of the distribution and the value vector.
structure: Linearity of expectation is bilinearity of the dot product, and it requires no independence whatsoever — that is why it is the most robust tool in probability. 𝔼[𝐴X] = 𝐴𝔼[X] for any matrix 𝐴.
reduction: Expectation is a dot product.

title: Variance and Standard Deviation
objects: A quadratic form in the centred value vector.
structure: Variance is 𝔼[𝑋2] −𝜇2, a difference of a quadratic and the square of a linear functional — hence a quadratic form. Non-negativity of variance is Cauchy–Schwarz, or equivalently positive semidefiniteness of the second-moment matrix.
reduction: Variance becomes a quadratic form.

title: Covariance and Correlation
objects: The covariance matrix, symmetric positive semidefinite.
structure: Σ ⪰0 always, since a⊤Σa = Var(a⊤X) ≥0. Its eigenvectors are the principal components and its eigenvalues the explained variances. The correlation matrix has unit diagonal and is again positive semidefinite, so not every symmetric matrix with unit diagonal is a valid correlation matrix.
reduction: Second-order dependence becomes a positive semidefinite matrix.
status: Exact linear. Central to statistics, machine learning, and finance alike.

title: Variance of a Sum
objects: A quadratic form in the weight vector.
structure: The single most-used identity in portfolio theory, error propagation, and experimental design. Inde- pendence makes Σ diagonal, reducing the form to ∑𝑎2 𝑖𝜎2 𝑖— the familiar addition-in-quadrature. Cross terms are exactly the off-diagonals.
reduction: Already a quadratic form.

title: Law of Total Expectation
objects: Conditional expectation as an orthogonal projection.
structure: 𝔼[𝑋∣𝑌] is the orthogonal projection of 𝑋onto the subspace of 𝑌-measurable functions in 𝐿2, so the tower property is idempotence of projections: 𝑃1𝑃2 = 𝑃1 for nested subspaces. Conditional expectation is a projection matrix.
reduction: Conditioning becomes projection onto a subspace.

title: Law of Total Variance
objects: Pythagorean decomposition in 𝐿2.
structure: ‖𝑋‖2 = ‖𝑃𝑋‖2 + ‖(𝐼−𝑃)𝑋‖2 for the conditional-expectation projection 𝑃. Total variance splits into explained (projected) and unexplained (residual) parts — this identity is the ANOVA decomposition and the 𝑅2 definition.
reduction: The decomposition is the Pythagorean theorem for a projection.

title: Moment Generating Function
objects: A linear functional of an exponentiated linear form.
structure: Moments are derivatives at zero: ∇2 ln 𝑀(0) = Σ, so the Hessian of the cumulant generating function is the covariance matrix. Convexity of ln 𝑀is positive semidefiniteness of that Hessian.
reduction: Moments become derivatives of a functional of a linear form.

title: Characteristic Function
objects: The Fourier transform of the distribution.
structure: 𝜑= 𝐹p with 𝐹the DFT matrix — the characteristic function is a unitary transform of the distribution vector. Convolution of independent variables becomes pointwise multiplication, which is the convolution theorem.
reduction: The transform is multiplication by the DFT matrix.

title: Bernoulli and Binomial Distributions
objects: An 𝑛-fold convolution, hence the 𝑛-th power of a 2 × 2-generated Toeplitz operator.
structure: The binomial vector is 𝑇𝑛e0 where 𝑇is the bidiagonal Toeplitz matrix with entries (1 −𝑝, 𝑝) — repeated convolution is a matrix power. Mean 𝑛𝑝and variance 𝑛𝑝(1 −𝑝) follow from linearity and independence.
reduction: The distribution becomes a Toeplitz matrix power.

title: Poisson Distribution
objects: p = 𝑒𝜆(𝑆−𝐼)e0 for the shift matrix 𝑆.
structure: The Poisson vector is a matrix exponential of the shift generator — it is the solution of the Kolmogorov forward equation for a pure birth process. Mean equals variance equals 𝜆, a consequence of the generator’s structure.
reduction: The distribution becomes a matrix exponential of a shift.

title: Geometric and Negative Binomial
objects: Powers of a scalar; a rank-one absorbing chain.
structure: The geometric distribution is the hitting-time distribution of a two-state Markov chain with one absorbing state, so 𝑃(𝑇> 𝑘) = (1 −𝑝)𝑘is a matrix power of the transient block. Negative binomial is the 𝑟-fold convolution, hence a larger triangular block.
reduction: The distribution becomes hitting times of a Markov chain.

title: Uniform Distribution
objects: The normalised all-ones vector.
structure: The maximum entropy distribution on a bounded set, and the stationary distribution of any doubly stochastic matrix. Projection onto constants is the rank-one matrix 11⊤/𝑛.
reduction: The distribution becomes the uniform vector.

title: Exponential Distribution
objects: The eigenfunction of the differentiation operator.
structure: Memorylessness is the semigroup property 𝑒−𝜆(𝑠+𝑡) = 𝑒−𝜆𝑠𝑒−𝜆𝑡, which is exactly the matrix exponen- tial’s defining property 𝑒𝐴(𝑠+𝑡) = 𝑒𝐴𝑠𝑒𝐴𝑡. Continuous-time Markov chains have exponential holding times for precisely this reason.
reduction: The distribution is the scalar case of a matrix exponential semigroup.

title: Normal (Gaussian) Distribution
objects: Exponential of a quadratic form; the 1 × 1 case of the next entry.
structure: Closed under linear transformations, convolution, and conditioning — the family is the linear-algebraic distribution family. Maximum entropy for fixed variance, and the fixed point of the convolution operator under normalisation (the CLT).
reduction: The exponent is a quadratic form.

title: Multivariate Normal Density
objects: Σ ≻0 the covariance; Σ−1 the precision matrix. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 27
structure: Entirely determined by a vector and a positive definite matrix. Marginals delete rows and columns of Σ; conditionals are Schur complements Σ11 −Σ12Σ−1 22 Σ21; linear maps give 𝐴Σ𝐴⊤; independence is a zero entry of Σ, and conditional independence a zero entry of Σ−1. Sampling is 𝜇+ 𝐿z with 𝐿the Cholesky factor.
reduction: The whole distribution is a mean vector and a covariance matrix.
status: Exact linear. The point where probability and linear algebra fully coincide.

title: Gamma Distribution
objects: Sum of 𝛼exponentials; a phase-type distribution.
structure: For integer 𝛼it is the hitting time of a chain of 𝛼exponential stages — a phase-type distribution with an explicit triangular generator matrix. Its density is 𝛼⊤𝑒𝑇𝑡t for that generator.
reduction: The distribution becomes a matrix-exponential (phase-type) form.

title: Beta Distribution
objects: The conjugate prior for the binomial; a point on the simplex’s boundary structure.
structure: Conjugacy means the Bayesian update is the aﬀine map (𝛼, 𝛽) ↦(𝛼+ 𝑘, 𝛽+ 𝑛−𝑘) — a translation in parameter space. Conjugate families are exactly those where updating is aﬀine in the natural parameters.
reduction: Bayesian updating becomes an aﬀine map on parameters.
status: Exact linear in the parameter update.

title: Chi-Squared Distribution
objects: The squared norm of a standard Gaussian vector.
structure: z⊤𝑃z ∼𝜒2 𝑟for any orthogonal projection 𝑃of rank 𝑟— Cochran’s theorem. Degrees of freedom are ranks of projections, which is why every 𝜒2 test’s df is a dimension count.
reduction: The distribution becomes a quadratic form in a Gaussian vector.

title: Student’s 𝑡Distribution
objects: Ratio of a Gaussian to an independent chi norm. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 31
structure: Independence of numerator and denominator follows from orthogonality of the corresponding projec- tions: ̄𝑋and 𝑠2 are independent because 1 and its orthogonal complement are orthogonal subspaces. The 𝑡 distribution exists because of a projection decomposition.
reduction: Independence becomes orthogonality of projections.

title: 𝐹Distribution
objects: Ratio of two quadratic forms in orthogonal subspaces.
structure: 𝑄1 = z⊤𝑃1z and 𝑄2 = z⊤𝑃2z with 𝑃1𝑃2 = 0, so they are independent. ANOVA is precisely this: decomposing ℝ𝑛into orthogonal subspaces and comparing the resulting quadratic forms.
reduction: The 𝐹ratio becomes a ratio of projected norms. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 32

title: Lognormal Distribution
objects: A Gaussian pushed through the exponential.
structure: Multiplicative processes become additive after taking logs, so a product of many independent factors is lognormal by the CLT applied in log space. The transformation is nonlinear, which is why the mean is 𝑒𝜇+𝜎2/2 rather than 𝑒𝜇.
reduction: Linear after a logarithmic change of variable.

title: Pareto (Power Law) Distribution
objects: Heavy tails; moments diverge for 𝑘≥𝛼.
structure: For 𝛼≤2 the variance is infinite, so the covariance matrix does not exist and every second-order linear method fails. This is the sharpest limitation on the linear-algebraic treatment of probability: no Σ, no PCA, no least squares, no CLT.
reduction: Not available at second order.
status: No faithful linear form when 𝛼≤2.

title: Transformation of Densities
objects: The Jacobian determinant as the density scaling factor.
structure: For a linear map Y = 𝐴X the factor is the constant | det 𝐴|−1, and Σ𝑌= 𝐴Σ𝑋𝐴⊤. Normalising flows in machine learning are built entirely on making det 𝐽cheap to compute.
reduction: The change of variables is a Jacobian determinant.

title: Convolution of Independent Variables
objects: 𝑇𝑋the Toeplitz matrix of p𝑋.
structure: Convolution is multiplication by a Toeplitz matrix, diagonalised by the DFT — which is why charac- teristic functions multiply. Sums of 𝑛iid variables are 𝑇𝑛e0, and the CLT is the statement that the normalised limit of this matrix power is Gaussian.
reduction: Convolution becomes a Toeplitz product.

title: Order Statistics Density
objects: Combinatorial weights times powers of the CDF.
structure: Uses the cumulative matrix 𝑆and binomial weights, so the whole family is a polynomial transformation of 𝑆p. The joint density of all order statistics is 𝑛! on the ordered simplex — a determinant-like volume factor.
reduction: The density is built from cumulative sums.
status: Exact linear in the cumulative structure.

title: Markov’s Inequality
objects: Positivity of a linear functional.
structure: Follows immediately from monotonicity of expectation applied to 𝑋≥𝑎1𝑋≥𝑎. The matrix version for positive semidefinite random matrices is 𝑃(𝜆max ≥𝑎) ≤tr 𝔼[𝑋]/𝑎.
reduction: The bound is monotonicity of a positive functional.

title: Chebyshev’s Inequality
objects: Markov applied to the quadratic form (𝑋−𝜇)2.
structure: The multivariate version uses the Mahalanobis quadratic form: 𝑃((X −𝜇)⊤Σ−1(X −𝜇) ≥𝑘2) ≤𝑛/𝑘2. Distribution-free, so it is weak but universally valid.
reduction: The bound is Markov applied to a quadratic form.

title: Weak Law of Large Numbers
objects: Averaging as a rank-one projection.
structure: ̄𝑋= 1 𝑛1⊤X, with Var( ̄𝑋) = 1 𝑛2 1⊤Σ1 = 𝜎2/𝑛under independence. The variance shrinks because Σ is diagonal; positive correlation slows or prevents convergence, since 1⊤Σ1 then grows like 𝑛2.
reduction: Averaging becomes a normalised contraction with 1.

title: Strong Law of Large Numbers
objects: Almost-sure rather than in-probability convergence.
structure: Requires only 𝔼|𝑋| < ∞, so it is not a second-order result and the covariance plays no role. Proved by Borel–Cantelli and truncation; no linear-algebraic mechanism.
reduction: Not available beyond the averaging structure.

title: Central Limit Theorem
objects: The covariance matrix as the complete description of the limit.
structure: The limit is determined entirely by Σ — all higher-order structure of the original distribution is erased. In matrix terms, repeated convolution (𝑇𝑛) converges after rescaling to the Gaussian, whose only parameters are a vector and a positive definite matrix. The CLT is the reason second-order linear methods dominate statistics.
reduction: The limiting distribution is specified by a covariance matrix.

title: Lindeberg Condition
objects: No single term dominating the total variance.
structure: Requires the variance vector’s largest entry to be a vanishing fraction of the total — a condition on the spectrum of Σ being spread out. If one eigenvalue dominates, the sum is effectively one-dimensional and the CLT fails.
reduction: The condition is a spectral spread requirement on Σ.

title: Berry–Esseen Theorem
objects: A rate of convergence involving the third moment.
structure: Third moments are rank-3 tensors, so the bound leaves matrix algebra. The 1/√𝑛rate is universal, and only the constant depends on the distribution.
reduction: Third-order data is a tensor, not a matrix.

title: Delta Method
objects: The Jacobian of the transformation.
structure: Error propagation is exactly covariance conjugation by the Jacobian — the first-order Taylor expansion pushed through the quadratic form. It is the workhorse of applied error analysis and is exact when 𝑔is linear.
reduction: The nonlinear transformation is linearised to its Jacobian.

title: Hoeffding’s Inequality
objects: Exponential concentration for bounded variables.
structure: The matrix analogue (Ahlswede–Winter, Tropp) bounds 𝜆max of a sum of independent bounded random matrices with the same exponential form plus a dimension factor 𝑑. Proved via the matrix exponential and Golden–Thompson.
reduction: Scalar concentration extends to eigenvalues of matrix sums.

title: Bernstein Inequality
objects: Variance-aware concentration.
structure: Sharper than Hoeffding when the variance is small. The matrix Bernstein inequality replaces 𝜎2 by ∥∑𝑖𝔼[𝑋2 𝑖]∥— a matrix norm — and is the standard tool for analysing randomised matrix sketching and sampling.
reduction: The variance becomes a matrix norm.

title: McDiarmid’s Bounded Differences Inequality
objects: The vector of bounded-difference constants.
structure: The denominator is ‖c‖2 2, so the bound depends on the Euclidean norm of the sensitivity vector. Proved by a martingale (Doob) decomposition — a sequence of orthogonal increments, which is a projection decomposition in 𝐿2.
reduction: The sensitivity becomes a vector norm.

title: Jensen’s Inequality for Expectations
objects: Convexity against a probability-vector contraction.
structure: Expectation is a convex combination, so Jensen is the definition of convexity applied to it. The matrix version 𝑓(u†𝐴u) ≤u†𝑓(𝐴)u follows by diagonalising 𝐴and applying the scalar case to its eigenvalues.
reduction: Expectation becomes a stochastic contraction.

title: Slutsky’s Theorem
objects: Continuity of linear operations under convergence.
structure: Addition and scalar multiplication are continuous, so limits pass through linear combinations. The matrix version: if 𝐴𝑛→𝐴in probability and X𝑛⇒X then 𝐴𝑛X𝑛⇒𝐴X — the basis of every asymptotic derivation in econometrics.
reduction: The theorem is continuity of matrix–vector multiplication.

title: Markov Property
objects: A single transition matrix 𝑃governing all steps. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 50
structure: Memorylessness is exactly the statement that the process is generated by matrix multiplication: p𝑛+1 = 𝑃⊤p𝑛. Everything about the chain — mixing, recurrence, hitting times, stationarity — is spectral information about 𝑃.
reduction: The process becomes iterated multiplication by a stochastic matrix.

title: Chapman–Kolmogorov Equation
objects: The semigroup property of matrix powers. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 51
structure: Literally associativity of matrix multiplication. In continuous time it becomes 𝑃(𝑡) = 𝑒𝑄𝑡for the generator 𝑄with zero row sums, and the Chapman–Kolmogorov identity is 𝑒𝑄(𝑠+𝑡) = 𝑒𝑄𝑠𝑒𝑄𝑡.
reduction: The equation is matrix multiplication.

title: Stationary Distribution
objects: The left Perron eigenvector with eigenvalue one.
structure: Existence and uniqueness follow from Perron–Frobenius for irreducible 𝑃; convergence 𝑃𝑛→1𝜋⊤ occurs at rate |𝜆2|𝑛. The spectral gap 1 −|𝜆2| is the mixing rate, and PageRank is exactly this computation.
reduction: The stationary distribution is an eigenvector.
status: Exact linear. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 52

title: Detailed Balance
objects: Reversibility, equivalent to self-adjointness in a weighted inner product.
structure: Detailed balance means 𝐷1/2 𝜋𝑃𝐷−1/2 𝜋 is symmetric, so 𝑃is self-adjoint with respect to the 𝜋-weighted inner product. Consequently the eigenvalues are real and the eigenvectors 𝜋-orthogonal — the spectral theorem applies, which is why reversible chains are so much easier to analyse.
reduction: Reversibility becomes symmetrisability by a diagonal similarity.
status: Exact linear. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 53

title: Poisson Process
objects: A continuous-time chain with generator the bidiagonal matrix 𝜆(𝑆−𝐼).
structure: p(𝑡) = 𝑒𝜆(𝑆−𝐼)𝑡e0, a matrix exponential of a shift generator. Independent increments correspond to the semigroup property; the superposition of independent Poisson processes adds generators.
reduction: The process becomes a matrix exponential.

title: Brownian Motion (Wiener Process)
objects: A Gaussian process with covariance matrix 𝐶𝑖𝑗= min(𝑡𝑖, 𝑡𝑗).
structure: Finite-dimensional distributions are multivariate normal with this explicit covariance matrix, which is positive definite. Its Cholesky factor is lower triangular with unit entries — sampling Brownian motion is 𝐿z, that is, a cumulative sum of Gaussians.
reduction: The process becomes a Gaussian vector with a specified covariance matrix.
also_in: Quantitative Finance. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 55

title: Itô’s Lemma
objects: The Hessian contracted with the covariance matrix.
structure: The Itô correction 1 2 tr(Σ𝐻) is a matrix trace — a second-order term surviving because (𝑑𝑊)2 = 𝑑𝑡. It is the reason stochastic calculus differs from ordinary calculus, and it is a linear functional of the Hessian.
reduction: The correction term is a trace of a matrix product.

title: Fokker–Planck Equation
objects: Discretised, a linear generator matrix acting on the density vector.
structure: ̇p = 𝐿⊤p with 𝐿the discretised generator — the density evolves linearly even when the underlying SDE is nonlinear. Stationary densities are null vectors of 𝐿⊤, and relaxation rates are its eigenvalues.
reduction: Density evolution becomes a linear matrix ODE.
status: Exact linear. Nonlinear dynamics, linear density evolution.
also_in: Statistical Mechanics. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 57

title: Martingale Property
objects: Conditional expectation as a projection with eigenvalue one.
structure: Martingales are the fixed points of the conditional expectation projection. Increments are orthogonal in 𝐿2, so variances add: Var(𝑋𝑛) = ∑𝑘Var(Δ𝑘) — a Pythagorean identity for an orthogonal decomposition.
reduction: The property becomes a fixed-point condition for a projection.

title: Optional Stopping Theorem
objects: Invariance of a linear functional under stopping.
structure: The projection structure is preserved under bounded stopping times, so the expectation is unchanged. Applied to hitting times of Markov chains it gives h = 𝑃h on transient states — harmonic vectors, solved as a linear system (𝐼−𝑃trans)h = b.
reduction: Hitting probabilities become a linear system.

title: Floating-Point Representation
objects: A perturbation model; entrywise relative error on a vector.
structure: Rounding a vector is fl(x) = (𝐼+ 𝐷)x with 𝐷diagonal and ‖𝐷‖ ≤𝑢— a diagonal multiplicative perturbation. All rounding error analysis is bookkeeping on products of such matrices.
reduction: Rounding becomes a diagonal perturbation matrix.

title: Machine Epsilon
objects: The unit roundoff, setting the scale of all diagonal perturbations.
structure: The achievable accuracy of any computation is 𝜅(𝐴) 𝑢in relative terms — the condition number multiplies the machine epsilon. This one product governs every numerical result in the compendium.
reduction: The bound is the norm of the perturbation matrix.

title: Rounding Error Model
objects: Accumulated products ∏𝑖(1 + 𝛿𝑖) = 1 + 𝜃𝑛with |𝜃𝑛| ≤𝑛𝑢/(1 −𝑛𝑢).
structure: For matrix operations this gives fl(𝐴𝐵) = 𝐴𝐵+ 𝐸with |𝐸| ≤𝑛𝑢|𝐴||𝐵| entrywise — a componentwise backward error bound. Wilkinson’s analysis is entirely an exercise in bounding such matrices.
reduction: Accumulated rounding becomes a bounded perturbation matrix.

title: Catastrophic Cancellation
objects: The amplification factor as a 1 × 2 condition number.
structure: The condition number of subtraction is (|𝑎| + |𝑏|)/|𝑎−𝑏|, which blows up as 𝑎→𝑏— the scalar case of 𝜅(𝐴) = 𝜎1/𝜎𝑛becoming large as a matrix approaches singularity. Cancellation is ill-conditioning in one dimension.
reduction: Cancellation is a condition number.

title: Backward Error
objects: The smallest perturbation of the data explaining the computed answer.
structure: An algorithm is backward stable when 𝜂= 𝑂(𝑢). Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting, QR by Householder, and the symmetric QR eigenvalue algorithm all are. Backward stability is a statement about a perturbation matrix, not about the answer.
reduction: Stability becomes a bound on a perturbation matrix norm.

title: Forward Error Bound
objects: The condition number as the amplification factor.
structure: The fundamental rule of numerical analysis: forward error ≤condition number × backward error. A stable algorithm gives 𝜂≈𝑢; the accuracy of the result is then limited entirely by 𝜅(𝐴), a property of the problem rather than the method.
reduction: Accuracy becomes a condition number product.

title: Kahan Compensated Summation
objects: Removing the 𝑛dependence from the accumulated perturbation.
structure: Tracking the low-order bits makes the effective perturbation matrix independent of 𝑛. In matrix terms, summation is 1⊤x, and Kahan’s method reduces the condition-number-like factor ∑|𝑥𝑖|/| ∑𝑥𝑖| from being multiplied by 𝑛to being multiplied by 2.
reduction: The bound is on the same perturbation matrix, with a smaller norm.

title: Interval Arithmetic
objects: Componentwise enclosures; matrix intervals for linear systems.
structure: Interval matrix computations give rigorous enclosures but suffer the dependency problem — widths grow multiplicatively. For linear systems the Krawczyk operator gives sharp enclosures, and the width scales with 𝜅(𝐴) as always.
reduction: Enclosures become interval matrices.

title: Horner’s Rule
objects: Evaluation as a product of 2 × 2 aﬀine matrices.
structure: Each step is ( 𝑏 1 ) ↦( 𝑥𝑎𝑘 0 1 )( 𝑏 1 ), so evaluation is a matrix product of length 𝑛. Uses 𝑛multiplications rather than 2𝑛, and is backward stable — the computed value is the exact value of a nearby polynomial.
reduction: Evaluation becomes a product of small matrices.

title: Karatsuba Multiplication
objects: A 3-multiplication bilinear algorithm for 2 × 2-block products.
structure: The tensor rank of the 2 × 2 polynomial product is 3 rather than 4 — the same phenomenon as Strassen. Fast algorithms are low-rank decompositions of the bilinear multiplication tensor.
reduction: The algorithm is a rank-3 tensor decomposition.

title: Schönhage–Strassen Complexity
objects: Multiplication via the FFT.
structure: Integer multiplication is convolution, hence multiplication by a Toeplitz matrix, diagonalised by the DFT. The complexity is the FFT’s, and the modern 𝑂(𝑛log 𝑛) Harvey–van der Hoeven bound is the same idea refined.
reduction: Multiplication becomes a Toeplitz product diagonalised by 𝐹.

title: Strassen Matrix Multiplication
objects: Seven multiplications for a 2 × 2 block product instead of eight.
structure: The bilinear map (𝐴, 𝐵) ↦𝐴𝐵for 2 × 2 matrices is a tensor in ℝ4 ⊗ℝ4 ⊗ℝ4 of rank 7, not 8. All fast matrix multiplication research is the study of that tensor’s rank and border rank. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 13
reduction: The algorithm is a tensor rank decomposition.

title: Extended Euclidean Algorithm
objects: A product of unimodular integer matrices.
structure: The Bézout coeﬀicients are entries of the accumulated matrix product, and unimodularity (det = ±1) is preserved throughout. This is integer Gaussian elimination on a 2 × 𝑛system.
reduction: The algorithm is a unimodular matrix product. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 14

title: Resultant
objects: The determinant of the Sylvester matrix.
structure: Vanishes exactly when 𝑓and 𝑔share a root — that is, when the Sylvester matrix is singular. Common roots become a nontrivial null space, so elimination theory is rank theory for structured matrices.
reduction: The resultant is a determinant.

title: Discriminant
objects: A determinant of the Sylvester matrix of 𝑓and 𝑓′.
structure: Zero exactly when 𝑓has a repeated root, which is when the companion matrix has a nontrivial Jordan block. The discriminant detects non-diagonalisability, and its smallness measures how ill-conditioned the roots are.
reduction: The discriminant is a determinant.

title: Gröbner Basis (Buchberger Criterion)
objects: Linear algebra on the Macaulay matrix, but at doubly exponential degree.
structure: Faugère’s F4 and F5 algorithms compute Gröbner bases by Gaussian elimination on Macaulay matrices — so the computation is linear algebra, but on matrices whose size is doubly exponential in the number of variables. Linear structure exists; tractability does not.
reduction: Reduction becomes row reduction of a Macaulay matrix.
status: Exact linear in structure, intractable in size.

title: S-Polynomial
objects: A designed cancellation of leading terms.
structure: Constructed so the leading terms cancel — exactly the elimination step of Gaussian elimination, choosing a multiplier to zero a pivot. Buchberger’s algorithm is elimination with a monomial order playing the role of pivot selection.
reduction: The 𝑆-polynomial is an elimination step.

title: Risch Decision Procedure Condition
objects: None linear.
structure: A decision procedure in differential algebra; the obstruction to elementary integration is not a rank or spectral condition. Some subproblems reduce to linear systems over function fields, but the procedure as a whole does not.
reduction: Not available.

title: Zeilberger’s Creative Telescoping
objects: Solving for the 𝑎𝑘is a linear system.
structure: The algorithm posits a recurrence with unknown coeﬀicients and solves a linear system for them — the certificate is found by Gaussian elimination over a rational function field. Hypergeometric summation is linear algebra with polynomial entries.
reduction: Certificate finding becomes a linear solve.

title: Cylindrical Algebraic Decomposition Complexity
objects: None linear.
structure: Real quantifier elimination requires repeated resultant computation, and the degree growth is doubly exponential. The individual determinants are linear-algebraic; the combinatorial explosion is not.
reduction: Only at the level of individual resultants.

title: Monte Carlo Integration
objects: A uniform-weight quadrature functional with random nodes.
structure: The same dot product as deterministic quadrature, but with random nodes and equal weights. The 𝑂(𝑁−1/2) rate is dimension-independent, which is why Monte Carlo wins in high dimensions where tensor-product grids fail.
reduction: Integration becomes a dot product with random nodes.

title: Monte Carlo Standard Error
objects: Variance of a normalised sum.
structure: Var( 1 𝑁1⊤f) = 1 𝑁2 1⊤Σ1, which is 𝜎2/𝑁for independent samples. Correlated samples (as in MCMC) inflate this by the integrated autocorrelation time — the ratio 1⊤Σ1/(𝑁𝜎2).
reduction: The error is a quadratic form in the sample covariance.

title: Importance Sampling
objects: A diagonal reweighting matrix.
structure: Changing the sampling distribution is multiplication by diag(w). Variance is minimised when 𝑞∝|𝑓|𝑝, and blows up when 𝑞has lighter tails than 𝑝— the weight vector then has enormous dynamic range, and the effective sample size ‖w‖2 1/‖w‖2 2 collapses.
reduction: Reweighting becomes a diagonal matrix.

title: Control Variates
objects: An optimal coeﬀicient vector from a covariance solve.
structure: The optimal c = Σ−1 𝑌𝑌𝜎𝑋𝑌is exactly the regression coeﬀicient of 𝑋on 𝑌, and the variance reduction factor is 1 −𝑅2. Control variates are least squares applied to variance reduction.
reduction: The optimal coeﬀicients are a linear solve.

title: Antithetic Variates
objects: Inducing negative correlation to shrink 1⊤Σ1.
structure: Variance of the average is 1 2𝜎2(1 + 𝜌), so negative 𝜌helps. Effective for monotone 𝑓, where the antithetic pair is guaranteed negatively correlated. It is a targeted reduction of an off-diagonal covariance entry.
reduction: The gain is a change in one covariance entry.

title: Metropolis–Hastings Acceptance Ratio
objects: Constructs a transition matrix 𝑃with 𝜋as stationary vector.
structure: The acceptance rule is designed to enforce detailed balance 𝜋𝑖𝑃𝑖𝑗= 𝜋𝑗𝑃𝑗𝑖, which makes 𝑃self-adjoint in the 𝜋-weighted inner product and hence gives a real spectrum. Convergence rate is the spectral gap 1 −|𝜆2|.
reduction: The algorithm constructs a reversible stochastic matrix.

title: Gibbs Sampler Update
objects: A product of coordinate-wise transition matrices.
structure: The full sweep is 𝑃= 𝑃1𝑃2 ⋯𝑃𝑛, a product of stochastic matrices each fixing 𝜋. For a Gaussian target the conditionals are given by Schur complements of the precision matrix, and Gibbs sampling is exactly Gauss–Seidel iteration with noise added.
reduction: Sweeps become products of stochastic matrices.

title: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo Leapfrog Step
objects: 𝑀the mass matrix; the integrator is symplectic.
structure: Each step is a symplectic matrix with det = 1, so volume is exactly preserved and the Jacobian factor in the acceptance ratio is one. Choosing 𝑀≈Σ−1 preconditions the sampler, and the eﬀiciency depends on 𝜅(𝑀1/2Σ𝑀1/2) — a condition number.
reduction: The integrator is a product of symplectic matrices.

title: Effective Sample Size
objects: Autocorrelations from the chain’s covariance structure.
structure: The denominator is 1⊤𝑅1/𝑁for the autocorrelation matrix 𝑅— a quadratic form. It relates to the spectral gap: slow mixing means large 𝜌𝑘, which means small ESS.
reduction: ESS becomes a quadratic form in the autocorrelation matrix.

title: Gelman–Rubin Statistic
objects: Between-chain and within-chain variances.
structure: Exactly an ANOVA decomposition: ̂𝑉combines the between-group and within-group sums of squares, which are squared norms of orthogonal projections. Convergence diagnosis is a variance-ratio test.
reduction: The diagnostic is an ANOVA projection decomposition.

title: Quasi-Monte Carlo Error (Koksma–Hlawka)
objects: Discrepancy of the point set; variation of the integrand.
structure: Discrepancy is a supremum over boxes, a combinatorial quantity. The bound gives 𝑂(𝑁−1 log𝑑𝑁), beating Monte Carlo in moderate dimension but degrading with 𝑑. The construction of low-discrepancy sequences uses digital nets over 𝔽2 — generator matrices, so the construction is linear even though the bound is not. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 31
reduction: The construction is linear over 𝔽2; the bound is not.

title: Inverse Transform Sampling
objects: Inversion of the cumulative-sum operator.
structure: Discretely, 𝐹= 𝑆p and sampling is a search in the vector 𝐹— a binary search, 𝑂(log 𝑛). The alias method preprocesses into a table allowing 𝑂(1) sampling, which is a rewriting of the same distribution vector.
reduction: Sampling inverts the cumulative-sum matrix.
status: Exact linear. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 32

title: Box–Muller Transform
objects: Polar coordinates; the pair is a rotation of a radial sample.
structure: Generates a standard bivariate normal, which is rotationally invariant — its covariance is 𝐼, invariant under every orthogonal matrix. Correlated Gaussians follow as 𝜇+ 𝐿z with 𝐿the Cholesky factor of Σ.
reduction: Correlated sampling becomes multiplication by a Cholesky factor.
status: Exact linear for the correlation step.

title: Rejection Sampling
objects: Acceptance probability 1/𝑀; eﬀiciency governed by the envelope ratio.
structure: For Gaussian proposal and target, 𝑀depends on the ratio of covariance determinants, and eﬀiciency degrades exponentially in dimension — 𝑀∼(det Σ𝑞/ det Σ𝑝)1/2 raised to a power in 𝑑. The curse of dimension- ality here is a determinant ratio.
reduction: Eﬀiciency becomes a determinant ratio for Gaussians.
status: Exact linear in the Gaussian case.

title: Linear Congruential Generator
objects: An aﬀine map over ℤ/𝑚.
structure: Iterates lie on at most (𝑑! 𝑚)1/𝑑parallel hyperplanes in 𝑑dimensions — Marsaglia’s theorem, a lattice statement. The spectral test measures the spacing of that lattice, so the quality of an LCG is a lattice determinant question.
reduction: The generator’s output is a lattice.

title: Mersenne Twister Period
objects: A linear recurrence over 𝔽2.
structure: The state update is multiplication by a 19937 × 19937 matrix over 𝔽2, and the period is the order of that matrix — maximal when the characteristic polynomial is primitive. It fails linear complexity tests precisely because it is linear, which is why it is unsuitable for cryptography.
reduction: The generator is a matrix power over 𝔽2.
status: Exact linear — and that is its weakness.

title: Fast Fourier Transform Recursion
objects: A factorisation of the dense DFT matrix into 𝑂(log 𝑁) sparse factors.
structure: Each factor has 𝑂(𝑁) nonzeros, giving 𝑂(𝑁log 𝑁) total. The FFT is nothing but a sparse factorisation of a dense unitary matrix — the paradigm for every fast transform.
reduction: The algorithm is a sparse matrix factorisation.

title: Number Theoretic Transform
objects: The DFT matrix over a finite field.
structure: Identical structure to the complex FFT but with exact arithmetic — no rounding error at all. Requires 𝑁∣𝑝−1. Used for exact polynomial multiplication and in lattice-based cryptography.
reduction: The transform is the DFT matrix over 𝔽𝑝.

title: Fast Multipole Method Complexity
objects: Hierarchical low-rank approximation of the interaction matrix.
structure: Far-field blocks of the kernel matrix are numerically low rank, so each is stored and applied in compressed form. FMM and ℋ-matrices are the same idea: a dense matrix with a hierarchical low-rank block structure, applied in near-linear time.
reduction: The interaction becomes a hierarchically low-rank matrix.

title: Barnes–Hut Opening Criterion
objects: The criterion for a block to be treated as low rank.
structure: A geometric admissibility condition deciding when a matrix block can be replaced by a rank-one (monopole) approximation. It is the block-admissibility condition of ℋ-matrix theory, stated geometrically.
reduction: The criterion is a low-rank admissibility test.

title: Automatic Differentiation (Forward Mode)
objects: Jacobian-vector products.
structure: Propagates one directional derivative per pass, costing 𝑂(𝑛) passes to build the full Jacobian for 𝑛 inputs. Eﬀicient when 𝑛≪𝑚. Implemented with dual numbers, which are the 2×2 matrices ( 𝑎𝑏 0 𝑎) — a nilpotent extension.
reduction: Forward mode computes 𝐽v.

title: Automatic Differentiation (Reverse Mode)
objects: Transposed Jacobian-vector products.
structure: One pass gives the full gradient of a scalar output, costing 𝑂(1) passes regardless of 𝑛— which is why backpropagation makes deep learning feasible. The choice between modes is purely a matter of matrix shape: reverse wins when 𝑚≪𝑛.
reduction: Reverse mode computes 𝐽⊤u.

title: Checkpointing Trade-Off
objects: Recomputation versus storage in the reverse sweep.
structure: Reverse mode must store intermediate states to apply 𝐽⊤; checkpointing recomputes them instead. Revolve gives the optimal schedule, a combinatorial optimisation over a binomial recursion.
reduction: The trade-off is combinatorial, applied to a linear computation.

title: Randomised SVD
objects: Ω a random Gaussian test matrix.
structure: Random projection captures the dominant subspace with high probability; the error is within a modest factor of the Eckart–Young optimum 𝜎𝑘+1. Cost drops from 𝑂(𝑚𝑛2) to 𝑂(𝑚𝑛log 𝑘). Oversampling by 5–10 columns makes the failure probability negligible.
reduction: Already matrix-native; the algorithm is randomised range finding.

title: Johnson–Lindenstrauss Lemma
objects: 𝑅∈ℝ𝑘×𝑑a random projection with 𝑘= 𝑂(𝜖−2 ln 𝑛).
structure: A random linear map preserves all pairwise distances among 𝑛points, with target dimension depending only logarithmically on 𝑛and not at all on 𝑑. Proved by concentration of ‖𝑅x‖2, a quadratic form in a Gaussian matrix.
reduction: Dimension reduction is a random matrix product.

title: Count-Min Sketch Error
objects: A random sparse 0/1 projection matrix.
structure: The sketch is 𝑆f for a random hashing matrix 𝑆with one nonzero per column per row-block, and recovery takes a minimum over rows. Linear in f, so sketches of streams merge by addition — the key property enabling distributed aggregation.
reduction: The sketch is a sparse random matrix product.

title: HyperLogLog Cardinality Estimate
objects: None linear — the estimator uses maxima of leading-zero counts.
structure: Based on order statistics of hash values, not on any linear functional. Merging sketches takes a componentwise maximum, which is idempotent rather than additive — the algebraic reason HyperLogLog handles duplicates and Count-Min does not.
reduction: Not available; the operation is max, not sum.

title: Bloom Filter False Positive Rate
objects: A random sparse 0/1 matrix with OR rather than addition.
structure: Insertion is an OR over the Boolean semiring, not addition over a field, so no cancellation is possible and elements cannot be removed. That algebraic difference — semiring versus field — is exactly the difference between a Bloom filter and an invertible sketch.
reduction: Linear only over the Boolean semiring.
status: Exact linear over the Boolean semiring.

title: Newton–Kantorovich Theorem
objects: Norms of the inverse Jacobian and the residual.
structure: A computable suﬀicient condition for convergence, entirely in terms of matrix norms. It gives a rigorous existence proof for a solution and an enclosing ball — validated numerics from a linear-algebraic bound.
reduction: The condition is a product of matrix norms.

title: Krawczyk Operator
objects: 𝑌an approximate inverse Jacobian; X an interval box.
structure: 𝐾(X) ⊆X proves existence and uniqueness of a root in the box, by the Brouwer fixed-point theorem. The contraction factor is ‖𝐼−𝑌𝐽‖, so the method works exactly when 𝑌is a good enough preconditioner.
reduction: Validation becomes a matrix contraction condition.

title: Sturm Sequence Root Count
objects: Sign changes in a remainder sequence.
structure: For a symmetric tridiagonal matrix the Sturm sequence is the sequence of leading principal minors, and the count of sign agreements gives the number of eigenvalues below a shift — this is exactly the bisection method for symmetric eigenvalues, and it is why 𝐿𝐷𝐿⊤inertia counting works.
reduction: Root counting becomes inertia counting.

title: Descartes’ Rule of Signs
objects: A combinatorial bound on the coeﬀicient vector.
structure: Depends on the sign pattern of the coeﬀicients, not on any rank or spectral property. Combined with bisection it gives real root isolation, but the rule itself is combinatorial.
reduction: Not available.

title: Chebyshev Approximation Error
objects: Optimality of the Chebyshev basis. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 52
structure: The Chebyshev polynomials are the orthogonal basis for the weight (1 −𝑥2)−1/2, and their three-term recurrence is a symmetric tridiagonal matrix whose eigenvalues are the Chebyshev nodes. The Vandermonde matrix in this basis has condition number 𝑂(1) rather than exponential — the basis choice is a conditioning choice.
reduction: The approximation is a projection in a well-conditioned basis.

title: Remez Exchange Equioscillation
objects: Each Remez iteration solves an (𝑛+ 2) × (𝑛+ 2) linear system.
structure: The algorithm alternates between solving a linear system for the coeﬀicients and a nonlinear exchange step relocating the reference points. The characterisation itself is a rank condition — the error must attain its norm with alternating signs at enough points to pin down the polynomial.
reduction: Each iteration is a linear solve. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 53

title: Lattice Reduction for Integer Relations (PSLQ)
objects: Finding a short vector in a lattice.
structure: An integer relation is a null vector of a 1 × 𝑛real matrix, found by LLL or PSLQ — integer Gram– Schmidt with rounding. It discovered the BBP formula and countless closed forms, all as short lattice vectors.
reduction: Relation finding becomes lattice reduction.
also_in: Number Theory. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 54

title: BBP Formula for 𝜋
objects: A specific integer relation, found by PSLQ.
structure: Permits computing the 𝑛-th hexadecimal digit without the preceding ones. Its discovery was a lattice reduction; the formula itself is a convergent series with no matrix content.
reduction: Only its discovery is linear-algebraic.
status: No faithful linear form for the formula itself.

title: Modular Arithmetic Reconstruction (CRT Lifting)
objects: A direct sum decomposition; reconstruction is a linear solve.
structure: Multi-modular algorithms compute a matrix determinant or solve a linear system modulo several primes in parallel, then reconstruct by CRT — a triangular solve. This is how exact integer linear algebra avoids coeﬀicient blowup.
reduction: Reconstruction becomes a triangular linear solve.

title: Hensel Lifting for Factorisation
objects: Newton iteration over ℤ𝑝.
structure: Each lifting step solves a linear system for the correction terms, with the Bézout coeﬀicients as the inverse. Quadratic convergence in the 𝑝-adic valuation, exactly as Newton converges quadratically over ℝ.
reduction: Each lift is a linear solve.

title: Condition Number of Polynomial Roots
objects: Sensitivity of a root to coeﬀicient perturbation.
structure: Equivalently the eigenvalue condition number 1/|w† 𝑖v𝑖| for the companion matrix. Wilkinson’s polyno- mial has 𝜅∼1013 for some roots despite well-separated integer roots — which is why root-finding via coeﬀicients is avoided and eigenvalue methods are used instead.
reduction: Root conditioning becomes eigenvalue conditioning.

title: Complexity of Exact Linear Algebra
objects: The matrix multiplication exponent.
structure: Determinant, inverse, rank, LU, and characteristic polynomial all reduce to matrix multiplication, so they all share the exponent 𝜔. Over ℤthere is the additional cost of coeﬀicient growth, controlled by multi- modular methods. The whole complexity theory of linear algebra collapses to one number.
reduction: Already matrix-native.

title: Convex Set
objects: Closure under convex combination — a constrained linear operation.
structure: Subspaces, aﬀine sets, half-spaces {a⊤x ≤𝑏}, polyhedra {𝐴x ≤b}, and ellipsoids {x⊤𝑃x ≤1} are all convex, and all are defined by linear or quadratic data. Convexity is what remains of linearity when inequalities are allowed.
reduction: Convex combinations are constrained linear combinations.

title: Convex Function
objects: The epigraph is a convex set.
structure: Every convex function is the supremum of the aﬀine functions below it, so convexity is exactly “expressible as a max of linear functions”. Quadratic forms x⊤𝑃x are convex precisely when 𝑃⪰0.
reduction: Convexity becomes a supremum of linear functionals.
status: Exact linear as a supremum of aﬀine forms.

title: First-Order Convexity Condition
objects: The tangent hyperplane as a global underestimator.
structure: The function lies above every tangent plane, which is why a zero gradient certifies a global minimum. The gap 𝑓(y) −𝑓(x) −∇𝑓⊤(y −x) is the Bregman divergence.
reduction: Convexity becomes a linear lower bound.

title: Second-Order Convexity Condition
objects: Positive semidefiniteness of the Hessian.
structure: Convexity is a spectral condition: all Hessian eigenvalues non-negative. Testing it is a Cholesky attempt or an eigenvalue computation. For quadratics the Hessian is constant, so convexity is a single matrix property.
reduction: Convexity becomes a definiteness condition.

title: Strong Convexity
objects: A lower bound on the Hessian spectrum.
structure: Guarantees a unique minimiser and linear convergence of gradient descent. 𝜇= 𝜆min(∇2𝑓), so strong convexity is a bound on the smallest eigenvalue — the curvature floor.
reduction: Strong convexity is a spectral lower bound.

title: Lipschitz Smoothness
objects: An upper bound on the Hessian spectrum.
structure: 𝐿= 𝜆max(∇2𝑓). Together with 𝜇it defines the condition number 𝜅= 𝐿/𝜇, which governs every first-order convergence rate in the field. The safe step size for gradient descent is 1/𝐿.
reduction: Smoothness is a spectral upper bound.

title: First-Order Necessary Condition
objects: A stationary point; for quadratics, a linear system.
structure: For 𝑓= 1 2x⊤𝐴x −b⊤x the condition is exactly 𝐴x = b — minimising a quadratic and solving a linear system are the same problem, which is why conjugate gradients serves both.
reduction: Optimality becomes a linear system for quadratics.

title: Second-Order Suﬀicient Condition
objects: Positive definiteness at the stationary point.
structure: The inertia of the Hessian classifies the point: all-positive gives a minimum, all-negative a maximum, mixed a saddle. In high dimensions saddles dominate, since all 𝑛eigenvalues must agree in sign for an extremum.
reduction: Classification becomes matrix inertia.

title: Subgradient
objects: The subdifferential, a convex set of vectors. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 10
structure: Where the gradient fails to exist the subdifferential is a set rather than a point — for |𝑥| at zero it is [−1, 1]. Optimality is 0 ∈𝜕𝑓, a membership rather than an equation, which is why non-smooth optimisation is harder.
reduction: The gradient becomes a set of supporting linear functionals.

title: Fermat’s Rule (Nonsmooth)
objects: Zero in the subdifferential. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 11
structure: Generalises ∇𝑓= 0. For 𝑓= 𝑔+ ℎwith 𝑔smooth it becomes −∇𝑔∈𝜕ℎ, which is what proximal methods solve at each step. The condition is a containment, not a linear equation.
reduction: Optimality becomes a set membership.

title: Proximal Operator
objects: A generalised projection; for indicator functions, exactly a projection.
structure: Firmly non-expansive, so iterating it converges. When ℎis the indicator of a convex set, prox = 𝑃𝐶, the Euclidean projection — and for a subspace that is the orthogonal projection matrix.
reduction: The operator generalises orthogonal projection. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 12

title: Soft Thresholding
objects: The proximal operator of the ℓ1 norm.
structure: Separable, hence applied componentwise — a diagonal nonlinear map. It is the reason Lasso and ISTA are cheap: the only nonlinearity is a coordinate-wise shrinkage, and everything else is matrix–vector products.
reduction: The operator is diagonal but nonlinear.

title: Standard Constrained Problem
objects: 𝐴the equality constraint matrix.
structure: The feasible set for the equality constraints is an aﬀine subspace x𝑝+ ker 𝐴, of dimension 𝑛−rank 𝐴. Inequality constraints cut it to a polyhedron. Degrees of freedom are a nullity.
reduction: Constraints become a matrix; the feasible set an aﬀine subspace.

title: Lagrangian
objects: Multipliers as a dual vector pairing with the constraints.
structure: The Lagrangian is linear in the multipliers, which is why the dual function is always concave regardless of the primal. Multipliers are the coordinates of a linear functional on the constraint space.
reduction: Constraint penalties become an inner product.

title: Karush–Kuhn–Tucker Conditions
objects: The gradient lies in the span of the constraint gradients.
structure: Stationarity says −∇𝑓0 ∈im[∇f 𝐴⊤] — a column-space membership. For quadratic objectives with linear constraints the whole KKT system is the symmetric indefinite block matrix ( 𝐻𝐴⊤ 𝐴 0 ).
reduction: Optimality becomes a block linear system.

title: Complementary Slackness
objects: A componentwise orthogonality between multipliers and slacks.
structure: 𝜆⊙s = 0 with both non-negative — the supports of the two vectors are disjoint. This combinatorial structure is what makes LP solutions land at vertices and what the simplex method exploits.
reduction: The condition is componentwise orthogonality of two non-negative vectors.

title: Lagrange Dual Function
objects: A pointwise infimum of aﬀine functions of the multipliers.
structure: Concave always, since an infimum of aﬀine functions is concave — the dual problem is convex even when the primal is not. For a quadratic primal the dual is again quadratic, with Hessian 𝐴𝐻−1𝐴⊤.
reduction: The dual is an infimum of linear functionals.

title: Weak Duality
objects: A bound holding without any convexity assumption.
structure: Any dual feasible point certifies a lower bound on the primal optimum — the source of every bound in branch and bound. The gap 𝑝∗−𝑑∗is zero exactly under constraint qualification.
reduction: The bound follows from the inner-product structure of the Lagrangian.

title: Strong Duality (Slater’s Condition)
objects: A relative-interior condition on the feasible set.
structure: Geometrically it is the separating hyperplane theorem applied to the epigraph — the existence of a non-vertical supporting hyperplane. For linear programmes strong duality holds whenever either problem is feasible, with no extra condition.
reduction: Duality becomes hyperplane separation.

title: Fenchel Conjugate
objects: A supremum over linear functionals.
structure: Always convex. For 𝑓= 1 2x⊤𝐴x with 𝐴≻0, 𝑓∗(y) = 1 2y⊤𝐴−1y — conjugation inverts the matrix. Norms conjugate to indicators of dual-norm balls, and 𝑓∗∗= 𝑓for closed convex 𝑓.
reduction: Conjugation becomes matrix inversion for quadratics.

title: Linear Programme (Standard Form)
objects: Everything is a matrix or vector.
structure: Optimal solutions occur at basic feasible solutions — vertices, obtained by choosing 𝑚columns of 𝐴 forming an invertible basis matrix 𝐵and setting x𝐵= 𝐵−1b. There are at most ( 𝑛 𝑚) vertices, and the simplex method walks between them.
reduction: Nothing to reduce; the problem is stated in matrix form.

title: LP Duality
