structure: Pure states are exactly the rank-one 𝜌(tr 𝜌2 = 1); mixed states have higher rank. Purity tr 𝜌2 is a rank-like measure, and the eigenvalues of 𝜌are the mixing probabilities in the optimal decomposition.
reduction: None needed.
status: Exact linear. Purity is a rank statement.

title: Von Neumann Equation
objects: Evolution by commutator — the adjoint action.
structure: 𝜌(𝑡) = 𝑈𝜌𝑈†, a unitary congruence, so the eigenvalues of 𝜌are constant. Von Neumann entropy is therefore conserved under closed-system evolution — irreversibility requires opening the system.
reduction: None needed.

title: Feynman Path Integral
objects: A sum over paths reproducing a matrix element.
structure: Equivalent to the matrix exponential: Trotter splitting 𝑒−𝑖𝐻𝑡/ℏ= lim(𝑒−𝑖𝑉𝑡/𝑁𝑒−𝑖𝑇𝑡/𝑁)𝑁turns the propagator into a product of matrices, and taking the continuum limit gives the path integral. It is a factorisation of a matrix exponential.
reduction: The path integral is a Trotter product of matrices.

title: Infinite Square Well
objects: Eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian on an interval.
structure: Exactly the vibrating string problem with a different constant — the same operator, the same eigen- vectors. Quantisation is discreteness of the spectrum, which comes from the boundary conditions, not from anything quantum.
reduction: None needed.

title: Finite Square Well Bound States
objects: A transcendental eigenvalue condition.
structure: Matching conditions at the boundaries give a 2 × 2 transfer matrix; bound states are where its determinant condition is met. The number of bound states is ⌈2𝑎√2𝑚𝑉0/𝜋ℏ⌉— an eigenvalue count, always at least one in one dimension.
reduction: None needed.

title: Quantum Harmonic Oscillator
objects: An arithmetic spectrum — evenly spaced eigenvalues.
structure: The equal spacing is what makes the oscillator special: it permits the ladder construction, makes coherent states possible, and gives the geometric partition function. In the number basis 𝐻is diagonal and 𝑎is the subdiagonal shift matrix.
reduction: None needed.

title: Ladder Operators
objects: Explicit shift matrices in the number basis.
structure: 𝑎is the subdiagonal with entries √𝑛and 𝑎† its transpose; 𝐻= ℏ𝜔(𝑎†𝑎+ 1 2) is diagonal. The whole spectrum follows from one commutator and the existence of a lowest eigenvector — a purely algebraic construction requiring no differential equations.
reduction: None needed.

title: Coherent State
objects: An eigenvector of the non-Hermitian operator 𝑎.
structure: Since 𝑎is not normal, its eigenvectors are not orthogonal — coherent states form an overcomplete, non-orthogonal frame. They saturate the uncertainty relation and are the closest quantum analogue of a classical state.
reduction: None needed.

title: Quantum Tunnelling Transmission
objects: An entry of the barrier transfer matrix.
structure: The barrier is a 2 × 2 transfer matrix whose off-diagonal entry gives transmission. Inside the barrier the wavevector is imaginary, so the solution decays — evanescence is exactly an eigenvalue leaving the real axis.
reduction: None needed.

title: WKB Tunnelling Integral
objects: The adiabatic approximation to the transfer matrix.
structure: Assumes the local eigenvalue varies slowly, so the transfer matrix is a product of locally diagonal factors. It fails at turning points where the eigenvalues collide, requiring Airy connection formulae.
reduction: WKB is an adiabatic product of local matrices.

title: Hydrogen Atom Energy Levels
objects: The Coulomb Hamiltonian’s discrete spectrum.
structure: The 𝑛2-fold degeneracy is larger than rotational symmetry alone predicts — the extra degeneracy comes from the hidden 𝑆𝑂(4) symmetry generated by the Runge–Lenz vector. Degeneracy is always a symmetry, and here the symmetry is bigger than it looks.
reduction: None needed.

title: Bohr Radius
objects: The length scale from the eigenvalue problem.
structure: Fixed by dimensional analysis of the Hamiltonian’s constants — a null-space computation on the dimensional matrix. It sets the scale of every atomic wavefunction.
reduction: The scale comes from a dimensional null space.

title: Hydrogen Wavefunctions
objects: Eigenvectors, factorised by separation of variables.
structure: Separability reflects the Kronecker sum structure of the Hamiltonian in spherical coordinates, so eigenvectors are products. The angular factors are 𝑆𝑂(3) irreducible representation basis vectors; the radial factors are Laguerre polynomials.
reduction: None needed.

title: Rydberg Formula
objects: Differences of eigenvalues.
structure: Spectral lines are eigenvalue differences, so the observable spectrum is the difference set of the Hamil- tonian’s spectrum. The Ritz combination principle — that line frequencies add — is exactly the statement that they come from differences of a single set.
reduction: Lines are eigenvalue differences.

title: Fine Structure Constant
objects: The dimensionless coupling scaling the perturbation.
structure: Its smallness is why perturbation theory converges quickly in QED — the expansion parameter of the Neumann-like series in the interaction. Relativistic corrections enter at order 𝛼2 relative to the Bohr energies.
reduction: The constant is a perturbation expansion parameter.

title: Fine Structure Splitting
objects: First-order perturbation lifting a degeneracy.
structure: The perturbation is diagonalised within each degenerate eigenspace — degenerate perturbation theory, which is a small eigenproblem inside a larger one. Splitting is the eigenvalue spread of the perturbation restricted to that subspace.
reduction: Splitting is an eigenvalue of a restricted perturbation.

title: Angular Momentum Commutation
objects: The 𝔰𝔲(2) Lie algebra structure constants.
structure: The entire theory of angular momentum follows from these three commutators — the representation theory of 𝔰𝔲(2). The Casimir 𝐽2 commutes with all of them, so it labels irreducible representations.
reduction: None needed.

title: Angular Momentum Eigenvalues
objects: Simultaneous eigenvectors of two commuting operators.
structure: [𝐽2, 𝐽𝑧] = 0 permits a common eigenbasis, and the ladder operators 𝐽± generate the whole (2𝑗+ 1)- dimensional multiplet from any one member. The dimension is the representation’s dimension — degeneracy is representation theory.
reduction: None needed.

title: Spin-1/2 Pauli Matrices
objects: Explicit 2 × 2 Hermitian traceless matrices.
structure: Together with 𝐼they span the Hermitian 2×2 matrices, so every qubit observable is a real combination. 𝜎2 𝑖= 𝐼, 𝜎𝑖𝜎𝑗= 𝑖𝜖𝑖𝑗𝑘𝜎𝑘, and 𝑒−𝑖𝜃̂n⋅𝜎/2 is a rotation with 4𝜋periodicity — the 𝑆𝑈(2) double cover.
reduction: None needed.

title: Spin Magnetic Moment
objects: An operator proportional to the spin vector operator.
structure: Proportionality means the moment shares eigenvectors with the spin, so measuring one measures the other. 𝑔≈2 from the Dirac equation, with QED corrections making it the most precisely tested quantity in physics.
reduction: None needed.

title: Zeeman Effect
objects: A diagonal perturbation in the 𝐽𝑧eigenbasis.
structure: The field breaks rotational symmetry, so the degeneracy of the multiplet lifts — splitting is the eigenvalue spread of a diagonal perturbation. Symmetry breaking is degeneracy lifting, stated spectrally.
reduction: None needed.

title: Landé g-Factor
objects: A projection coeﬀicient from the Wigner–Eckart theorem.
structure: The magnetic moment is not parallel to J, so only its projection onto J survives — the 𝑔-factor is exactly that projection coeﬀicient. It is a matrix element ratio. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 37
reduction: The factor is a projection coeﬀicient.

title: Spin–Orbit Coupling
objects: A bilinear coupling of two vector operators.
structure: L ⋅S = 1 2(𝐽2 −𝐿2 −𝑆2), so it is diagonal in the coupled |𝑗ℓ𝑠⟩basis — the coupling selects which basis diagonalises the Hamiltonian. Changing from uncoupled to coupled basis is a Clebsch–Gordan change of basis.
reduction: None needed.
status: Exact linear. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 38

title: Clebsch–Gordan Addition
objects: A unitary change of basis between two decompositions of a tensor product.
structure: j1 ⊗j2 = ⨁𝐽J — the tensor product of two irreducible representations decomposes into a direct sum. The Clebsch–Gordan coeﬀicients are the entries of the unitary matrix effecting that block-diagonalisation.
reduction: None needed.

title: Wigner–Eckart Theorem
objects: Factorisation of a matrix element into geometry and dynamics.
structure: All 𝑚-dependence is in the Clebsch–Gordan coeﬀicient; the physics is in one reduced matrix element. This is a rank-one factorisation of the matrix of matrix elements — a huge compression forced entirely by symmetry.
reduction: The theorem is a rank-one factorisation.

title: Electric Dipole Selection Rules
objects: Vanishing matrix elements forced by symmetry.
structure: ⟨𝑓| ̂r |𝑖⟩= 0 unless the Clebsch–Gordan coeﬀicient is nonzero — selection rules are a sparsity pattern in the transition matrix imposed by group theory. Most entries are exactly zero, which is why atomic spectra are sparse.
reduction: Selection rules are a symmetry-forced sparsity pattern.

title: Time-Independent Perturbation Theory
objects: Eigenvalue perturbation of a Hermitian matrix.
structure: Exactly the standard first- and second-order eigenvalue perturbation formulas. The energy denomina- tors are eigenvalue gaps, so the expansion fails when levels are close — near-degeneracy is ill-conditioning of the eigenproblem.
reduction: None needed.
status: Exact linear (perturbation of a Hermitian eigenproblem).

title: Degenerate Perturbation Theory
objects: A small eigenproblem within the degenerate eigenspace.
structure: When the gap vanishes, the naive expansion diverges; the fix is to diagonalise 𝐻′ restricted to the degenerate subspace first. This is exactly how one handles a defective or near-defective eigenproblem numerically.
reduction: None needed.

title: Variational Principle
objects: The Rayleigh quotient bound.
structure: Identical to entry 27 of field 05 — the ground state energy is the minimum of the Rayleigh quotient. Second-order accuracy means an 𝑂(𝜖) error in the trial state gives 𝑂(𝜖2) error in the energy, which is why variational methods are so effective.
reduction: None needed.

title: Fermi’s Golden Rule
objects: A squared matrix element times a density of states.
structure: Transition rate is the squared modulus of an off-diagonal matrix element — first-order perturbation theory. The density of states is the spectral density of the final-state Hamiltonian, so the rule is a product of two spectral quantities.
reduction: The rate is a squared matrix element times a spectral density.

title: Rabi Oscillation
objects: Exact solution of a 2 × 2 Hermitian system.
structure: The two-level Hamiltonian ℏ 2( −𝛿Ω Ω 𝛿) has eigenvalue splitting √ Ω2 + 𝛿2, and that splitting is the oscilla- tion frequency. On resonance (𝛿= 0) the transfer is complete because the eigenvectors are equal superpositions — an avoided crossing at its symmetric point.
reduction: None needed.

title: Adiabatic Theorem
objects: Continuous tracking of an eigenvector as the matrix varies.
structure: Valid when the rate of change is small compared with the squared gap: | ⟨𝑚| ̇ 𝐻|𝑛⟩| ≪|𝐸𝑛−𝐸𝑚|2/ℏ. Small gaps break adiabaticity — Landau–Zener transitions occur at avoided crossings, which is exactly eigenvector ill-conditioning.
reduction: The theorem is eigenvector continuity under slow variation.

title: Born Approximation
objects: The scattering amplitude as the Fourier transform of the potential.
structure: First term of the Born (Neumann) series 𝑇= 𝑉+𝑉𝐺0𝑉+⋯— a resolvent expansion, convergent when the potential is weak. The amplitude is a linear transform of the potential, which is why scattering experiments invert to structure.
reduction: The amplitude is a Fourier transform of the potential.

title: Partial Wave Expansion
objects: Decomposition in the angular momentum eigenbasis.
structure: Rotational symmetry block-diagonalises the scattering operator by ℓ, so the S-matrix is diagonal with entries 𝑒2𝑖𝛿ℓ. Unitarity is |𝑆ℓ| = 1 for elastic scattering, and each phase shift is one diagonal entry.
reduction: Symmetry diagonalises the scattering matrix.

title: Optical Theorem
objects: A consequence of unitarity of the S-matrix.
structure: 𝑆†𝑆= 𝐼relates the forward amplitude’s imaginary part to the total cross section — probability removed from the forward beam must reappear elsewhere. It is unitarity written out for one matrix element.
reduction: The theorem is S-matrix unitarity.

title: Scattering Cross Section
objects: The squared modulus of a matrix element.
structure: Amplitudes add; cross sections do not — interference between scattering channels is the cross term. This is the Born rule applied to scattering, so the same quadratic-form structure recurs.
reduction: The cross section is a squared amplitude.

title: Symmetrisation Postulate
objects: Eigenvectors of the exchange operator with eigenvalue ±1.
structure: The exchange operator satisfies ̂𝑃2 = 𝐼, so its eigenvalues are ±1 and the state space splits into symmetric and antisymmetric subspaces. Bosons and fermions are the two eigenspaces of one involution.
reduction: Statistics is an eigenvalue of the exchange operator.

title: Pauli Exclusion Principle
objects: Vanishing of an antisymmetrised product.
structure: The antisymmetriser applied to a repeated state gives zero, because a determinant with two equal columns vanishes. Exclusion is the vanishing of a determinant — the sharpest possible linear-algebraic statement of it.
reduction: Exclusion is a vanishing determinant.

title: Slater Determinant
objects: An antisymmetrised product — literally a determinant.
structure: Spans the antisymmetric subspace of ⨂ 𝑁ℋ, of dimension ( 𝑑 𝑁). Invariant under orthogonal transfor- mations of the occupied orbitals, so only the occupied subspace matters — Hartree–Fock optimises a subspace, not a basis.
reduction: The state is a determinant.

title: Exchange Interaction
objects: An off-diagonal matrix element arising from antisymmetry.
structure: No classical analogue — it comes entirely from the determinant structure of the state. It is what produces ferromagnetism and Hund’s rules, both consequences of a sign in a permutation.
reduction: The interaction is an antisymmetry-induced matrix element.

title: Entangled State (Bell State)
objects: A rank-two matrix in the bipartite coeﬀicient basis.
structure: Writing the state as a coeﬀicient matrix 𝐶, product states are exactly rank 𝐶= 1 and entangled states have higher rank. The Schmidt coeﬀicients are the singular values of 𝐶, and entanglement entropy is the von Neumann entropy of 𝜎2 𝑖. Entanglement is a rank statement, and the SVD is its complete characterisation.
reduction: Entanglement is matrix rank; Schmidt decomposition is the SVD.
status: Exact linear. Possibly the cleanest single insight in the edition.

title: CHSH Bell Inequality
objects: A bound on a bilinear form over local hidden variable models.
structure: Classical models are constrained to a polytope with the CHSH facets; quantum mechanics reaches 2 √ 2 (Tsirelson), the maximum over the larger set of quantum correlations. The quantum bound comes from an SDP relaxation, so the gap between classical and quantum is a polytope-versus-spectrahedron gap.
reduction: The bound separates a polytope from a spectrahedron.

title: No-Cloning Theorem
objects: Impossibility from linearity and unitarity.
structure: The proof is two lines: linearity forces the cloner to act on superpositions term by term, giving |𝜓1⟩|𝜓1⟩+ |𝜓2⟩|𝜓2⟩rather than the product of sums. Cloning would require a nonlinear map, so no-cloning is a consequence of linearity, not an obstruction to it.
reduction: The theorem follows directly from linearity.
status: Exact linear — linearity is the reason for the impossibility.

title: Von Neumann Entropy
objects: A spectral functional of the density matrix.
structure: Zero for pure (rank-one) states, maximal ln 𝑑for the maximally mixed 𝜌= 𝐼/𝑑. Invariant under unitary evolution since the eigenvalues are, so entropy increase requires an open system. Entanglement entropy is 𝑆of a reduced density matrix.
reduction: Entropy is a spectral functional.

title: Decoherence Rate
objects: Exponential decay of off-diagonal density matrix entries.
structure: Decoherence is the density matrix becoming diagonal in the pointer basis — off-diagonals decaying while the diagonal is preserved. It is a rank-reducing, entropy-increasing process, and the pointer basis is selected by the system–environment coupling operator’s eigenvectors.
reduction: Decoherence is off-diagonal decay.

title: Lindblad Master Equation
objects: The most general linear generator preserving trace and positivity.
structure: Linear in 𝜌, so the whole open-system evolution is a linear map on the 𝑑2-dimensional space of density matrices — vectorised, it is a 𝑑2 × 𝑑2 matrix. Complete positivity is the structural constraint, and the steady state is a null vector of that superoperator. Even dissipation and measurement remain exactly linear.
reduction: Open evolution is a linear superoperator.
status: Exact linear. The chapter closes as it began: nothing here is anything but linear algebra.

title: Membrane Equation
objects: A linear ODE with a sum of current terms.
structure: Exactly Kirchhoff’s current law on a capacitor, so the passive membrane is a first-order linear system with a single pole. All the nonlinearity of neural excitability enters through the conductances in the current terms.
reduction: The membrane is a linear RC circuit.

title: Ohmic Ionic Current
objects: A conductance acting aﬀinely on the voltage.
structure: Aﬀine in 𝑉, so a sum of ohmic currents gives an effective conductance and an effective reversal potential — the weighted average ∑𝑔𝑖𝐸𝑖/ ∑𝑔𝑖. That averaging is a normalised inner product, and it is why shunting inhibition works by changing the denominator.
reduction: Parallel conductances combine as a weighted average.

title: Hodgkin–Huxley Equations
objects: A four-dimensional system, linear in 𝑉given the gating variables.
structure: The system is linear in each variable separately — the nonlinearity is entirely in the products 𝑚3ℎ and 𝑛4 multiplying 𝑉. Linearising about rest gives a Jacobian whose eigenvalues predict the threshold and the resonance frequency exactly.
reduction: The equations are multilinear; excitability is a Jacobian eigenvalue phenomenon.

title: Gating Variable Kinetics
objects: A first-order linear relaxation with voltage-dependent coeﬀicients.
structure: Linear in 𝑚at fixed voltage, so each gate is a one-pole low-pass filter whose time constant depends on 𝑉. The separation of 𝜏𝑚from 𝜏𝑛and 𝜏ℎis the time-scale structure that generates the spike.
reduction: Each gate is a linear filter with a state-dependent time constant.

title: Boltzmann Activation Curve
objects: A logistic function — linear in the logit.
structure: The logit of activation is exactly linear in voltage with slope 1/𝑘, which is why activation curves are fitted on a logit scale. The slope reflects the gating charge moved across the membrane field.
reduction: Activation is linear in the logit.

title: Goldman–Hodgkin–Katz Current Equation
objects: A rectifying current–voltage relation.
structure: Nonlinear in voltage — the rectification comes from asymmetric concentrations — but linear in the permeability. It reduces to the ohmic form when concentrations are symmetric, which is the linear special case.
reduction: The relation is linear in permeability, nonlinear in voltage.

title: Cable Equation
objects: A linear PDE — the diffusion equation with a decay term.
structure: Fully linear, so dendritic responses superpose exactly and Green’s functions can be computed. Rall’s equivalent cylinder is a change of variables collapsing a branched tree to a single cable — a dimensional reduction of the operator.
reduction: Passive dendrites are a linear PDE; Rall’s reduction is a change of basis.

title: Length Constant
objects: The spatial decay eigenvalue of the cable operator.
structure: The reciprocal of the operator’s spatial eigenvalue, so voltage decays as 𝑒−𝑥/𝜆in an infinite cable. Its square-root dependence on diameter is why thick dendrites conduct further.
reduction: The constant is a reciprocal spatial eigenvalue.

title: Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Model
objects: A linear ODE with a reset — a hybrid system.
structure: Between spikes the dynamics are exactly linear with a single eigenvalue −1/𝜏; the entire nonlinearity is the threshold-and-reset map. That separation is why the model is both analytically tractable and genuinely spiking.
reduction: Linear subthreshold dynamics plus a discrete reset map.

title: LIF Firing Rate
objects: A reciprocal of an integration time computed from the linear solution.
structure: Obtained by integrating the linear ODE between reset and threshold, so the f–I curve follows in closed form. It has a hard rheobase — the current below which the exponential never reaches threshold.
reduction: The rate follows from integrating the linear subthreshold equation.

title: Exponential Integrate-and-Fire
objects: A linear term plus an exponential spike-generating term.
structure: The exponential is a fitted approximation to the sodium activation near threshold, so the model is linear plus one nonlinear term. It reproduces real neurons’ f–I curves far better than the pure LIF for a single extra parameter.
reduction: The model is linear plus one exponential term.

title: Adaptive Exponential Model
objects: A second linear state variable providing adaptation.
structure: Adding a slow linear variable makes the system 2 × 2, and the resulting complex eigenvalues produce resonance and bursting. Different firing patterns correspond to different regions of the two-dimensional parameter space — a spectral classification.
reduction: Adaptation adds a second linear state; patterns are eigenvalue regimes.

title: Izhikevich Model
objects: A quadratic plus a linear equation — a minimal two-dimensional system.
structure: The quadratic is the normal form of a saddle-node bifurcation, so the model is the simplest system with a genuine spike-generating fold. Its four parameters place the system in different bifurcation regimes, which is how it reproduces twenty firing patterns.
reduction: The quadratic is a bifurcation normal form; the second equation is linear.

title: Morris–Lecar Model
objects: A planar system whose phase plane can be drawn.
structure: Two dimensions means nullclines and a 2 × 2 Jacobian, so every bifurcation can be classified by trace and determinant. It is the standard vehicle for teaching excitability precisely because the linear analysis is complete.
reduction: Excitability is classified by a 2 × 2 Jacobian’s trace and determinant.

title: Type I and Type II Excitability
objects: Two different bifurcations at the onset of repetitive firing.
structure: Type I arises from a real eigenvalue passing through zero (arbitrarily low firing rates); Type II from a complex pair crossing the imaginary axis (a jump to finite frequency). The entire behavioural distinction is which eigenvalue crosses — one of the cleanest cases where the spectrum determines the phenomenology.
reduction: The classification is by which eigenvalue crosses the imaginary axis.

title: Phase Response Curve
objects: A linear response function on the limit cycle.
structure: 𝑍(𝜙) is the gradient of the phase with respect to the state — the adjoint eigenfunction of the linearised dynamics around the cycle. It is exactly first-order perturbation theory applied to a periodic orbit, and it predicts synchronisation properties.
reduction: The PRC is the adjoint linearisation of a limit cycle.

title: Synaptic Conductance Kinetics
objects: An alpha function — the impulse response of a two-stage linear filter.
structure: Exactly the response of two cascaded first-order filters, so synaptic input is a linear convolution of the spike train with this kernel. Summation across synapses is therefore exact superposition.
reduction: Synaptic input is convolution with a linear kernel.

title: NMDA Magnesium Block
objects: A voltage-dependent gate multiplying a conductance.
structure: The multiplication of presynaptic activity by postsynaptic depolarisation makes the NMDA receptor a coincidence detector — a product, not a sum. That product is the biophysical basis of Hebbian learning, and it is precisely the nonlinearity a purely linear synapse would lack.
reduction: The block makes the synapse multiplicative rather than additive.

title: Quantal Synaptic Release
objects: A product of three parameters — a binomial mean.
structure: Mean and variance together identify the parameters, since Var = 𝑛𝑝𝑞(1 −𝑝) — two equations giving two of the three unknowns. Variance–mean analysis is exactly this moment-matching solve. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 20
reduction: Quantal analysis is a moment-matching linear solve.

title: Short-Term Depression
objects: A linear recovery punctuated by multiplicative decrements.
structure: Recovery is a first-order linear relaxation; each spike multiplies the resource by (1 −𝑢). The steady- state release becomes inversely proportional to rate, so the synapse transmits changes rather than levels — a high-pass filter implemented biophysically. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 21
reduction: Linear recovery plus multiplicative depletion gives a high-pass filter.

title: Short-Term Facilitation
objects: The complementary linear relaxation with incremental jumps.
structure: Same structure as depression with the opposite sign, and the two together make the synapse a band- pass filter whose peak frequency is set by the two time constants. Filtering properties are read directly off the two eigenvalues. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 22
reduction: Two relaxation time constants give a band-pass response.

title: Hebbian Learning Rule
objects: An outer product update — a rank-one matrix increment.
structure: Δ𝑊= 𝜂xx⊤, so repeated application accumulates the input correlation matrix. The weight vector therefore converges toward the leading eigenvector of the correlation matrix — Hebbian learning is power iteration, and without normalisation it diverges.
reduction: Hebbian learning is power iteration on the input covariance. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 23

title: Oja’s Rule
objects: Hebbian learning with a normalising decay term.
structure: The subtracted term constrains ‖w‖ →1, so the rule converges exactly to the principal eigenvector of the input covariance. It is online principal component analysis implemented in one line of local update.
reduction: Oja’s rule is online PCA — convergence to a leading eigenvector.
status: Exact linear. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 24

title: BCM Rule
objects: A Hebbian rule with a sliding threshold set by a second moment.
structure: The threshold’s dependence on the output’s mean square makes the rule stable and selective — it drives the weight vector toward directions producing sparse, high-variance responses. It is a nonlinear modification of power iteration that selects for kurtosis rather than variance.
reduction: The sliding threshold makes it a projection-pursuit rather than a PCA rule.

title: Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity
objects: A temporally asymmetric learning kernel.
structure: Weight change is the correlation of pre- and postsynaptic trains with this kernel — a cross-correlation, hence a linear functional of the joint spike statistics. The asymmetry makes it sensitive to causal order, so it learns temporal sequences rather than instantaneous correlations.
reduction: STDP is a cross-correlation with an asymmetric kernel.

title: Calcium Control Hypothesis
objects: A threshold function of a single scalar signal.
structure: A piecewise map from calcium concentration to weight change, unifying rate-based and timing-based rules under one variable. It is a dimensional reduction: many induction protocols collapse onto one scalar.
reduction: Multiple protocols collapse onto one scalar variable.

title: Synaptic Scaling
objects: A multiplicative rescaling of the whole weight vector.
structure: Multiplicative scaling preserves relative weights exactly — it is a scalar multiple of the vector, so it changes the norm without changing the direction. That is precisely why it can stabilise firing rates without erasing learned structure.
reduction: Scaling is a scalar multiple preserving direction.

title: Rate Model
objects: A recurrent weight matrix inside a pointwise nonlinearity.
structure: Linearising gives 𝜏 ̇𝛿r = (−𝐼+ 𝐹′𝑊)𝛿r, so stability and dynamics are governed by the eigenvalues of 𝑊scaled by the gain. Every network computation in this section is a statement about that spectrum.
reduction: Network dynamics are governed by the connectivity matrix’s spectrum.

title: Wilson–Cowan Equations
objects: A 2 × 2 system with a sign-structured weight matrix.
structure: The matrix has positive and negative columns (excitation and inhibition), which makes complex eigenvalues possible — hence oscillation. Trace and determinant of the 2 × 2 Jacobian classify every regime the model can produce.
reduction: Regimes are classified by a 2 × 2 Jacobian.

title: Balanced Network Condition
objects: A near-cancellation of two large terms.
structure: Mean excitatory and inhibitory inputs cancel to leading order, leaving fluctuations of order √ 𝐾— the network operates in the null space of the mean input. This is why cortical neurons fire irregularly despite thousands of inputs, and it is a precisely linear cancellation.
reduction: Balance is a cancellation leaving the system driven by fluctuations.

title: Diffusion Approximation for Input
objects: The first two moments of the summed synaptic input.
structure: Many small independent inputs sum to a Gaussian by the central limit theorem — the mean is a signed inner product and the variance an unsigned one. That sign difference is why balance cancels the mean but not the variance.
reduction: Mean and variance are two inner products with different sign patterns.

title: Siegert Formula
objects: A first-passage time for an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process.
structure: The mean first passage time solves a linear second-order ODE with boundary conditions, so the transfer function is exact for the diffusion-approximated LIF. It is the network’s f–I curve, and mean-field theories are built by composing it with entry 31.
reduction: The rate solves a linear first-passage boundary value problem.

title: Hopfield Network Energy
objects: A quadratic form with a symmetric weight matrix.
structure: Symmetry of 𝑊guarantees the dynamics descend an energy function, so there are no limit cycles — the network always converges to a fixed point. Asymmetric weights destroy the Lyapunov function and permit oscillation, which is exactly why the symmetry assumption matters.
reduction: The energy is a quadratic form; symmetry guarantees convergence.

title: Hopfield Storage Capacity
objects: A capacity limit from crosstalk between stored outer products.
structure: Weights are a sum of pattern outer products ∑𝜇𝜉𝜇𝜉𝜇⊤, and interference between them grows as √𝑝/𝑁. Capacity is where interference overwhelms signal — a signal-to-noise condition on a sum of rank-one matrices.
reduction: Capacity is where rank-one interference swamps the signal.

title: Ring Attractor Dynamics
objects: A circulant connectivity matrix.
structure: Translation-invariant connectivity is circulant, so it is diagonalised exactly by the Fourier basis and its eigenvalues are the Fourier coeﬀicients 𝑊0, 𝑊1, …. A bump forms when the 𝑊1 eigenvalue exceeds the threshold — pattern formation as a single Fourier mode going unstable.
reduction: Ring networks are circulant; bumps are unstable Fourier modes.

title: Line Attractor for Integration
objects: A marginally stable direction — an eigenvalue precisely at one.
structure: Perfect integration requires an eigenvalue of exactly one, so the state persists along that direction while decaying in all others. The fine tuning required is the theory’s central problem: any mismatch makes memory leak or run away exponentially.
reduction: Integration is an eigenvalue tuned exactly to one.
status: Exact linear. The fine-tuning problem is a spectral one.

title: Oscillation Frequency from Delayed Inhibition
objects: A frequency set by loop delay.
structure: The characteristic equation of a delayed feedback loop is transcendental, and oscillation occurs where the phase around the loop reaches 180°. Gamma frequency emerges from the inhibitory time constants — a phase condition on a linear loop.
reduction: The frequency is a phase condition on a delayed linear loop.

title: Kuramoto Synchronisation of Neurons
objects: A mean-field coupled phase model.
structure: The order parameter 𝑟𝑒𝑖𝜓= 1 𝑁∑𝑒𝑖𝜃𝑗reduces the all-to-all coupling to a single complex number — a rank-one reduction of an 𝑁× 𝑁interaction. Synchronisation onset at 𝐾𝑐is a bifurcation in that scalar.
reduction: Mean-field coupling is a rank-one reduction to one complex order parameter.
also_in: Complexity Science. Neural Coding and Analysis

title: Poisson Spike Model
objects: A counting process with independent increments.
structure: Independence makes counts additive across intervals, so the process is fully specified by its rate function. It is the null model against which all spike-train structure is measured.
reduction: Independent increments make counts additive.

title: Fano Factor of Spike Counts
objects: A normalised variance.
structure: One for Poisson, so deviation quantifies structure — refractoriness lowers it, bursting raises it. Cortical values near one are what motivated the balanced network of entry 30.
reduction: The factor is a ratio of two moments.

title: Coeﬀicient of Variation of Intervals
objects: A normalised interval dispersion.
structure: Complementary to the Fano factor — one describes intervals, the other counts, and for a renewal process 𝐹= CV2 asymptotically. The relation between them diagnoses non-renewal structure.
reduction: The two dispersion measures are linked for renewal processes.

title: Spike-Triggered Average
objects: An average of stimulus vectors preceding spikes.
structure: For white noise stimuli the STA is an unbiased estimate of the linear filter — exactly a reverse correlation, which is a cross-correlation. For correlated stimuli it must be whitened by 𝐶−1 STA, a linear solve against the stimulus covariance.
reduction: The STA is a cross-correlation; correlated stimuli require a covariance inverse.

title: Linear–Nonlinear–Poisson Model
objects: A linear filter followed by a static nonlinearity.
structure: The filter k is a single direction in stimulus space — a rank-one projection — and everything the model sees is that one-dimensional projection. Spike-triggered covariance extends it to multiple filters by finding the eigenvectors of the spike-triggered covariance that differ from the prior.
reduction: The model is a projection; multi-filter extensions are eigenvector problems.

title: Generalised Linear Model for Spikes
objects: A Poisson GLM with a log link.
structure: Exactly a linear predictor exponentiated, and the log-likelihood is concave — so fitting has a unique global optimum. The history term captures refractoriness and bursting within the same linear framework, which is why the GLM displaced ad hoc spike models.
reduction: The model is linear in log rate with a concave likelihood.

title: Mutual Information of a Neural Code
objects: A divergence between a joint distribution and its rank-one approximation.
structure: Mutual information measures exactly how far the joint distribution is from the outer product of its marginals — the same rank-one comparison as in every independence test here. It is zero precisely when the joint matrix has rank one.
reduction: Mutual information measures departure from rank one.

title: Direct Method Information Rate
objects: A difference of two entropies.
structure: Exactly a linear contrast between the response entropy and the conditional entropy, both estimated from word distributions. Finite-sample bias in entropy estimation is severe and is corrected by extrapolation in 1/𝑁— a linear extrapolation.
reduction: The rate is an entropy difference with a linear bias correction.

title: Fisher Information for Neural Populations
objects: A sum of squared tuning-curve slopes — a Gram-like quantity.
structure: Information comes from tuning-curve slopes, not peaks, so the most informative neurons about a stimulus are those tuned to its flank. With correlated noise, 𝐽= f′⊤Σ−1f′ — a quadratic form with the inverse noise covariance, and correlations can either help or hurt depending on their alignment with f′.
reduction: Fisher information is a quadratic form with an inverse covariance.

title: Population Vector Decoding
objects: A normalised weighted sum of preferred direction vectors. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 48
structure: Exactly a weighted average — an inner product with the firing rate vector as weights. It is optimal only when tuning is cosine and preferred directions are uniformly distributed; otherwise it is a biased linear estimator.
reduction: Population vector decoding is a weighted vector sum.

title: Maximum Likelihood Decoding
objects: A maximisation of a log-likelihood linear in the spike counts.
structure: Linear in r for fixed 𝜃, so the log-likelihood surface is an inner product of the rate vector with a 𝜃-dependent template — matched filtering across templates. It attains the Cramér–Rao bound asymptotically, which is entry 47.
reduction: Decoding is matched filtering across a template family. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 49

title: Signal Detection d-Prime
objects: A standardised mean difference.
structure: Exactly the projection of the mean difference onto the optimal discriminant direction, normalised by noise — Fisher’s linear discriminant in one dimension. In the multivariate case 𝑑′2 = Δ𝜇⊤Σ−1Δ𝜇, a Mahalanobis distance.
reduction: 𝑑′ is a Mahalanobis distance along a discriminant direction.

title: Neurometric–Psychometric Comparison
objects: A comparison of two discriminability measures.
structure: The surprising near-equality implies that pooling many neurons yields little improvement, which happens when noise is correlated along the discriminant direction — information-limiting correlations. It is a statement about the alignment of Σ with Δ𝜇.
reduction: The result reflects noise correlations aligned with the signal direction.

title: Eﬀicient Coding Principle
objects: An information maximisation over a linear encoding.
structure: For Gaussian signals the optimal linear code whitens the input — decorrelating and equalising variance, which is exactly PCA followed by scaling. Retinal centre-surround receptive fields are the whitening filter for natural image statistics.
reduction: Eﬀicient coding is whitening — a linear transform of the covariance.

title: Predictive Coding Error
objects: A residual after subtracting a prediction.
structure: Exactly a projection residual: the prediction is a linear map of context, and only the orthogonal component is transmitted. This decorrelates the signal, which is the same whitening objective as entry 52 arrived at from a different direction.
reduction: Predictive coding transmits a projection residual.

title: Free Energy Principle
objects: A variational bound — a KL divergence plus a log evidence.
structure: Under Gaussian assumptions the whole scheme reduces to precision-weighted prediction error minimi- sation, which is generalised least squares with the precision matrix as the weight. That Gaussian case is where the principle makes contact with everything else in this chapter.
reduction: The Gaussian case is precision-weighted least squares.

title: Reinforcement Learning Prediction Error
objects: A temporal difference — a linear contrast of value estimates.
structure: With linear function approximation 𝑉= w⊤𝜙, the TD update is a stochastic linear iteration whose fixed point solves a linear system. Dopamine’s correspondence to 𝛿is the field’s most cited link between an algorithm and a signal.
reduction: TD learning with linear features is a stochastic linear iteration.

title: BOLD Haemodynamic Response Function
objects: A convolution kernel — the impulse response of the vascular system.
structure: The BOLD signal is the neural activity convolved with ℎ, so the whole forward model is a linear time-invariant filter. Its low-pass character is why fMRI has poor temporal resolution regardless of sampling rate.
reduction: BOLD is a linear convolution.

title: General Linear Model for fMRI
objects: A design matrix built by convolving the task regressors with the HRF.
structure: Literally ordinary (or generalised) least squares, fitted independently at every voxel — hundreds of thousands of identical linear solves. Contrasts c⊤̂𝛽test hypotheses, and design eﬀiciency is the conditioning of 𝑋⊤𝑋.
reduction: fMRI analysis is mass-univariate least squares.

title: Random Field Theory Correction
objects: An expected Euler characteristic of a thresholded field.
structure: Accounts for spatial smoothness so the correction is far less severe than Bonferroni — the effective number of independent tests is the resel count, which is a smoothness-derived rank. It is a geometric rather than combinatorial correction.
reduction: The correction replaces test count with an effective smoothness-derived rank.

title: Dynamic Causal Modelling
objects: A bilinear state-space model with three parameter matrices.
structure: 𝐴is the intrinsic connectivity, 𝐵𝑗the modulation by input 𝑗, 𝐶the direct input effect — bilin- ear because inputs multiply states. Model comparison is Bayesian, and the estimated 𝐴is directed effective connectivity.
reduction: DCM is a bilinear state-space model.

title: Granger Causality
objects: A log ratio of residual variances from two nested regressions.
structure: Both models are vector autoregressions — linear predictors of the present from the past — and the statistic compares their residual variances. It measures predictive improvement, not causation, and its interpretation degrades badly with unobserved common inputs or differential filtering.
reduction: Granger causality is a nested VAR variance comparison.

title: Asymptotic Notation
objects: An equivalence-class construction on growth rates.
structure: The set of functions of a given order forms a cone closed under addition and positive scaling — so 𝑂(⋅) classes are closed under the operations a vector space would need, but the ordering is a preorder, not a norm. It is a quotient by scaling, not a linear structure.
reduction: Growth classes form a cone under a preorder.

title: Master Theorem
objects: A divide-and-conquer recurrence with three regimes.
structure: The comparison is between 𝑛log𝑏𝑎and 𝑓(𝑛) — a comparison of two exponents, hence linear in the logs. The three cases correspond to which term dominates the geometric series of the recursion tree.
reduction: The cases compare exponents, which is linear in logs.

title: Akra–Bazzi Theorem
objects: A generalisation handling unequal subproblem sizes.
structure: The exponent 𝑝solves ∑𝑎𝑖𝑏𝑝 𝑖= 1 — a single scalar equation, and the integral accumulates the non-recursive work weighted by depth. It is a weighted linear accumulation over the recursion tree.
reduction: The solution is a weighted integral with an exponent from a scalar equation.

title: Merge Sort Recurrence
objects: A balanced recursion tree with equal work per level.
structure: Each of the log 𝑛levels does 𝑂(𝑛) work, so the total is a sum of equal terms — a uniform linear accumulation over depth. The optimality follows from entry 5.
reduction: The cost is a uniform sum over log 𝑛levels.

title: Comparison Sort Lower Bound
objects: A counting bound — a decision tree must have 𝑛! leaves.
structure: A binary tree with 𝑛! leaves has depth at least log2 𝑛! ≈𝑛log 𝑛by Stirling. It is an information- theoretic counting argument, and its content is combinatorial rather than linear.
reduction: The bound is a leaf-counting argument on a binary tree.

title: Quicksort Expected Time
objects: An expectation over random pivot choices.
structure: Computed by linearity of expectation over indicator variables for each pair comparison — the sum ∑𝑖<𝑗2/(𝑗−𝑖+ 1) is a harmonic sum. Linearity of expectation is the one genuinely linear tool doing the work here.
reduction: The analysis uses linearity of expectation over pair indicators.

title: Binary Search
objects: Repeated halving of an interval.
structure: Each step is a contraction by a factor of two, so the number of steps is a logarithm — the reciprocal of a contraction rate. It is the same structure as any geometric convergence.
reduction: Search is geometric contraction; cost is a log.

title: Amortised Analysis (Aggregate Method)
objects: An average over a sequence — a linear functional of the cost vector.
structure: Exactly a mean, so expensive operations are paid for by cheap ones. Its validity depends only on summing, which makes it a linear accounting identity.
reduction: Amortisation is an average of a cost vector.

title: Potential Method
objects: A telescoping sum with a potential function.
structure: The potential differences telescope exactly, so the total amortised cost differs from the actual by only the endpoint potentials. It is the discrete analogue of a conservative field — path independence from an exact difference.
reduction: The method is a telescoping (exact-difference) argument.

title: Union-Find Complexity
objects: An inverse Ackermann bound — effectively constant.
structure: Path compression flattens the forest, and the analysis assigns ranks and charges operations against them. It is a combinatorial amortised argument with no linear content.
reduction: The bound is combinatorial amortisation.

title: Fibonacci Heap Bounds
objects: Amortised bounds from a two-term potential function.
structure: The potential counts trees plus twice the marked nodes — a linear functional of the structure’s state. Cascading cuts are paid for by the potential drop.
reduction: The potential is a linear functional of structural counts.

title: Hash Table Load Factor
objects: A geometric series in the load factor.
structure: The expected probe count is a Neumann series ∑𝛼𝑘, diverging as 𝛼→1. That divergence is why tables resize at a load factor well below one. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 13
reduction: Probe count is a geometric series.

title: Universal Hashing
objects: A family of hash functions with a pairwise independence guarantee.
structure: The standard construction ℎ(𝑥) = ((𝑎𝑥+ 𝑏) mod 𝑝) mod 𝑚is an aﬀine map over a finite field, so universality is a property of aﬀine maps over 𝔽𝑝. Linear algebra over finite fields is doing the real work.
reduction: Universal hash families are aﬀine maps over a finite field. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 14

title: Birthday Bound
objects: A collision probability from pairwise counting.
structure: The expected number of colliding pairs is (𝑛 2)/𝑚— linearity of expectation over pair indicators again. Collisions become likely at 𝑛≈√𝑚, which sets every hash length in cryptography.
reduction: The bound follows from linearity of expectation over pairs.

title: Balanced Tree Height
objects: A logarithmic depth from bounded branching.
structure: A tree with branching factor 𝑏and 𝑛nodes has depth log𝑏𝑛— the same reciprocal-of-contraction structure as binary search. Rebalancing rotations preserve the invariant that keeps this bound.
reduction: Depth is a log of node count.

title: B-Tree Height
objects: Depth with a large branching factor.
structure: Increasing 𝑏from 2 to hundreds divides the depth by log2 𝑏— a linear rescaling of the logarithm. That rescaling is why disk-based indexes use wide nodes.
reduction: Branching factor rescales the log linearly.

title: Skip List Expected Height
objects: An expected maximum of geometric random variables.
structure: Each element’s level is geometric, and the maximum of 𝑛such variables concentrates around log1/𝑝𝑛. The analysis is probabilistic rather than linear, achieving balanced-tree behaviour without rotations.
reduction: The height is a maximum of geometric variables.

title: Cache-Oblivious Complexity
objects: A memory transfer count in a two-level model.
structure: The bound is optimal without knowing 𝐵or 𝑀, achieved by recursive divide-and-conquer that is self-similar at all scales. Its optimality is a statement about the recursion matching the memory hierarchy’s geometric structure.
reduction: Optimality follows from scale-invariant recursion.

title: Complexity Class P
objects: A union of time-bounded classes.
structure: Closed under composition and complement, which makes it robust across machine models. Closure properties are set-theoretic rather than linear.
reduction: Class definitions are set-theoretic.

title: Complexity Class NP
objects: An existential quantifier over polynomial-length certificates.
structure: The asymmetry between existential and universal quantification is the whole content — co-NP swaps the quantifier. Quantifier structure is logical, not linear.
reduction: The class is defined by quantifier structure.

title: Polynomial-Time Reduction
objects: A transitive preorder on problems.
structure: Composition of reductions is transitive, so the reduction relation is a preorder — completeness means being maximal in it. Composition of maps is the only algebra present, and it lacks additive structure.
reduction: Reductions compose; the structure is a preorder, not a vector space.

title: Cook–Levin Theorem
objects: An encoding of computation as a Boolean formula.
structure: The proof builds a formula whose satisfying assignments are exactly accepting computation tableaux — a combinatorial encoding. Over 𝔽2, XOR-SAT is linear algebra and is solvable in polynomial time by Gaussian elimination; the hardness comes precisely from allowing OR, which breaks linearity. That contrast is the sharpest available statement of what linearity buys.
reduction: Linear (XOR) constraints are easy; the theorem’s hardness needs nonlinearity.
status: No faithful linear form — and the reason is instructive.

title: Space Hierarchy and Savitch’s Theorem
objects: A recursive reachability argument on a configuration graph.
structure: Savitch’s proof is repeated squaring of the reachability relation — which over the Boolean semiring is exactly matrix squaring on the configuration graph’s adjacency matrix. Reachability in 2𝑘steps is the 2𝑘th Boolean matrix power.
reduction: Savitch’s argument is Boolean matrix squaring.

title: Time Hierarchy Theorem
objects: A diagonalisation argument.
structure: Constructs a machine differing from every machine in the smaller class — Cantor’s diagonal argument applied to computations. Diagonalisation is a self-reference construction with no linear analogue.
reduction: Diagonalisation has no linear counterpart.

title: Halting Problem Undecidability
objects: A self-referential contradiction.
structure: The proof assumes a decider and builds a machine that contradicts it on its own description. Self- reference is the mechanism, and no matrix formulation captures it — attempting one would misrepresent the argument entirely.
reduction: Self-reference resists linear formulation. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 25

title: Rice’s Theorem
objects: A sweeping generalisation of entry 25.
structure: Reduces the halting problem to any non-trivial semantic property, so the undecidability is inherited by reduction. The obstruction is the same self-reference.
reduction: The theorem inherits the halting problem’s obstruction.

title: Kolmogorov Complexity
objects: A minimum description length — an uncomputable functional.
structure: It is subadditive, 𝐾(𝑥𝑦) ≤𝐾(𝑥) + 𝐾(𝑦) + 𝑂(log), which is the closest thing to linearity available. Its uncomputability follows from the same self-reference as the halting problem.
reduction: Only subadditivity survives; the quantity is uncomputable.

title: Invariance Theorem
objects: Machine-independence up to an additive constant.
structure: Different universal machines differ by a bounded additive term — an equivalence up to translation. That additive structure is what makes the quantity meaningful at all.
reduction: Invariance is an additive-constant equivalence.

title: Approximation Ratio
objects: A worst-case ratio over instances.
structure: Many approximation algorithms are analysed by LP relaxation and rounding — solving a linear program over a polytope, then rounding to an integer point. The integrality gap is the ratio between the LP and integer optima, so approximability is bounded by a linear program’s slack.
reduction: Approximation bounds often come from LP relaxations and integrality gaps.

title: PCP Theorem
objects: A probabilistically checkable proof system.
structure: The proof uses low-degree polynomial encodings and linearity testing — checking whether a function is close to linear over 𝔽2 with 𝑂(1) queries. Linearity testing is literally at the heart of the theorem, which makes it the most linear-algebraic result in complexity theory.
reduction: The proof relies on linearity testing over finite fields.

title: Randomised Complexity Classes
objects: Classes defined by acceptance probability thresholds.
structure: Amplification by repetition uses Chernoff bounds — concentration of a sum of independent indicators, which is linearity of expectation plus a tail bound. The gap between 1/3 and 2/3 is arbitrary precisely because amplification is so effective.
reduction: Amplification rests on concentration of linear sums.

title: Quantum Complexity BQP
objects: A class defined by unitary circuits on a Hilbert space.
structure: Quantum computation is linear algebra: states are unit vectors, gates are unitary matrices, and a computation is a product of unitaries applied to a vector. Measurement is the only non-unitary step, and it is a projection followed by renormalisation.
reduction: Quantum computation is a product of unitary matrices.
status: Exact linear. The most literally linear model of computation.

title: Grover Search Speedup
objects: A product of two reflection operators.
structure: The Grover iterate is the composition of a reflection about the marked state and a reflection about the uniform superposition — and the product of two reflections is a rotation. The state rotates by a fixed angle per step in a two-dimensional invariant subspace, so 𝜋/4 √ 𝑁steps reach the target. The quadratic speedup is a statement about angles in a plane.
reduction: Grover’s algorithm is a rotation built from two reflections.

title: Shor Factoring Complexity
objects: Period finding via the quantum Fourier transform.
structure: The QFT is a unitary matrix — the discrete Fourier transform — implemented in 𝑂(𝑛2) gates, and it converts period finding into a peak-detection problem. Factoring reduces to finding an eigenvalue phase of a modular multiplication operator, so the whole algorithm is phase estimation.
reduction: Shor’s algorithm is eigenvalue phase estimation via a unitary Fourier transform.

title: Graph Traversal Complexity
objects: A sweep over the adjacency structure.
structure: Cost is linear in the size of the adjacency matrix’s sparse representation — one visit per nonzero entry. BFS layers are exactly the sets reached by successive Boolean matrix powers.
reduction: Traversal touches each nonzero of the adjacency matrix once.

title: Dijkstra’s Algorithm
objects: A greedy relaxation over edge weights.
structure: Each relaxation is 𝑑𝑣←min(𝑑𝑣, 𝑑𝑢+ 𝑤𝑢𝑣) — exactly a min-plus inner product. The algorithm’s correctness requires non-negative weights, which is the condition that the min-plus operator is monotone in the right way.
reduction: Relaxation is a min-plus operation.

title: Bellman–Ford Complexity
objects: 𝑉−1 rounds of full relaxation.
structure: Each round is a min-plus matrix–vector product d ←𝑊⊗d, so the algorithm computes 𝑊⊗(𝑉−1) applied to the source indicator. Negative cycles are detected because the iteration fails to converge — a spectral- radius condition in the tropical semiring.
reduction: Bellman–Ford is repeated min-plus matrix–vector multiplication.

title: Floyd–Warshall All-Pairs
objects: A min-plus matrix “cube” computed in place.
structure: The algorithm computes the min-plus closure 𝑊∗= 𝐼⊕𝑊⊕𝑊⊗2 ⊕⋯, and its triple loop is exactly the structure of matrix multiplication. The 𝑂(𝑉3) cost is the cost of one matrix multiply, which is why the two problems have the same complexity signature.
reduction: All-pairs shortest paths is min-plus matrix closure.

title: A* Search Admissibility
objects: A lower-bound condition on a heuristic.
structure: Consistency, ℎ(𝑛) ≤𝑐(𝑛, 𝑛′)+ℎ(𝑛′), is a triangle inequality — so a consistent heuristic is a metric-like potential. A* with a consistent heuristic is Dijkstra on reweighted edges 𝑤′ = 𝑤+ℎ(𝑛′)−ℎ(𝑛), an exact potential transformation.
reduction: A* is Dijkstra with a potential-transformed weight matrix.

title: Minimum Spanning Tree Cut Property
objects: A matroid exchange property.
structure: Spanning trees form the bases of a graphic matroid, and greedy optimality is equivalent to the matroid structure. Matroids generalise linear independence — the graphic matroid’s independent sets are exactly the linearly independent columns of the incidence matrix over 𝔽2.
reduction: MSTs are matroid bases; the matroid is linear independence over 𝔽2.

title: Max-Flow Min-Cut
objects: A pair of linear programs in duality.
structure: Exactly LP duality: the max-flow LP’s dual is the min-cut LP, and strong duality gives equality. Integrality follows because the constraint matrix is totally unimodular, so the LP optimum is automatically integral — one of the cleanest matrix-theoretic explanations of a combinatorial theorem.
reduction: The theorem is LP duality plus total unimodularity.

title: Edmonds–Karp Complexity
objects: BFS-based augmenting path selection.
structure: Choosing shortest augmenting paths bounds the number of augmentations, giving a strongly polyno- mial bound. The residual graph is the constraint matrix’s current slack, so each augmentation is a pivot-like step.
reduction: Augmentation is a pivot on the flow polytope.

title: Graph Colouring Bound
objects: Bounds on the chromatic number.
structure: The Hoffman bound 𝜒≥1 −𝜆max/𝜆min comes directly from the adjacency matrix’s spectrum, and the Lovász theta function sits between the clique and chromatic numbers as a semidefinite program. Spectral and SDP relaxations are the standard route to bounds here.
reduction: Colouring bounds come from the adjacency spectrum and SDP relaxations.

title: Strongly Connected Components
objects: A block decomposition of the adjacency matrix. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 43
structure: Ordering vertices by component makes the adjacency matrix block triangular, and the components are the diagonal blocks — exactly the Frobenius normal form of a non-negative matrix. Irreducibility of a matrix is strong connectivity of its graph, which is what Perron–Frobenius requires.
reduction: SCCs are the diagonal blocks of the Frobenius normal form.

title: RSA Encryption
objects: Exponentiation in a multiplicative group.
structure: The group (ℤ/𝑛)∗is abelian, so exponentiation is a group endomorphism — linear in the exponent’s additive structure, since 𝑒and 𝑑are inverses mod 𝜙(𝑛). Security rests on factoring being hard, which is not a linear-algebraic obstruction.
reduction: Exponentiation is linear in the exponent group.

title: Diﬀie–Hellman Key Exchange
objects: Commutativity of exponentiation. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 45
structure: The scheme works because exponents commute — the map is bilinear in the exponent pair. That bilinearity is exactly what pairing-based cryptography exploits further.
reduction: The exchange is bilinear in the exponents.

title: Elliptic Curve Discrete Log
objects: Scalar multiplication in an abelian group.
structure: The group law makes 𝑘𝑃a module action of ℤon the curve’s point group — linear in 𝑘. Smaller keys suﬀice because no sub-exponential algorithm is known, not because of any structural difference in the linearity. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 46
reduction: Scalar multiplication is a module action.

title: Security Level in Bits
objects: A logarithmic measure of work.
structure: Comparing key sizes across schemes is comparing logs of work factors, so security level is a linear scale in log space. Doubling key length does not double security for schemes with sub-exponential attacks — the map is not linear in key length.
reduction: Security level is linear in log work. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 47

title: Structure: XOR is exactly vector addition over 𝔽2, and a uniform key makes the ciphertext uniform regardless
structure: XOR is exactly vector addition over 𝔽2, and a uniform key makes the ciphertext uniform regardless of the message — the translation acts transitively on the space. Perfect secrecy is a statement about a group acting simply transitively, which is as linear as cryptography gets.
reduction: The pad is translation in 𝔽𝑛 2 by a uniform element.
status: Exact linear. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 48

title: Hash Function Properties
objects: Three increasingly strong one-wayness requirements.
structure: A linear hash function would be trivially breakable — collisions are found by solving a linear system. Cryptographic hashes must therefore be deliberately far from linear, which makes this one of the few entries where linearity is the enemy.
reduction: Linearity would destroy the security property.
status: No faithful linear form, by design.

title: Merkle Tree Proof Size
objects: A path from a leaf to the root of a binary tree.
structure: Verification recomputes hashes along a path, so proof size is the tree depth. It is the same logarithmic- depth structure as every balanced tree here.
reduction: Proof size is tree depth.

title: Amdahl’s Law
objects: A speedup bounded by the serial fraction.
structure: Total time is a sum of a fixed serial part and a divisible parallel part — a linear decomposition of the work vector. The bound 𝑆≤1/(1 −𝑝) is the limit as the parallel term vanishes.
reduction: The law is a linear work decomposition.

title: Gustafson’s Law
objects: Speedup under a fixed time rather than fixed problem size.
structure: Exactly linear in 𝑁, because the problem grows with the machine. The contrast with Amdahl is a contrast between two different linear models of what is held fixed.
reduction: Scaled speedup is aﬀine in processor count.

title: Average Memory Access Time
objects: An aﬀine combination of hit and miss costs.
structure: Exactly a weighted average, and multi-level hierarchies nest the same formula recursively — a chain of aﬀine maps. Each level’s miss rate weights the next level’s cost.
reduction: AMAT is a nested aﬀine combination.

title: Cache Miss Categories
objects: An additive decomposition of miss counts.
structure: Approximately additive, measured by comparing against idealised caches — a difference-based attri- bution. The decomposition is not orthogonal, so the categories overlap somewhat.
reduction: The categories are a difference-based additive attribution.

title: Instruction Pipeline Speedup
objects: A throughput ratio approaching the pipeline depth.
structure: Fill and drain costs are an additive overhead, so speedup approaches 𝑘as 𝑛grows — an aﬀine correction to an ideal linear scaling. Hazards add further additive stall terms.
reduction: Pipelining is ideal scaling with an additive overhead.

title: CPU Performance Equation
objects: A product of three factors — additive in logs.
structure: Exactly multiplicative, so improvements in different factors compound. It separates the compiler’s, architecture’s, and technology’s contributions into independent multiplicands.
reduction: Performance is multiplicative, hence log-additive.

title: Little’s Law for Systems
objects: A stock–flow identity.
structure: Exactly linear and distribution-free — it requires only that the system be stable, with no assumptions about arrival or service distributions. That generality is why it holds across queueing, epidemiology, and inventory alike.
reduction: The law is a linear stock–flow identity.

title: Roofline Model
objects: A minimum of two linear bounds.
structure: Performance is capped by the lower of a compute ceiling and a bandwidth-limited ramp, so the model is piecewise linear with a single kink. The kink’s location — the machine balance point — determines whether an algorithm is compute- or memory-bound.
reduction: The model is a minimum of two linear functions.

title: Shannon Entropy for Compression
objects: The expected code length lower bound.
structure: Entropy is a linear functional of the surprisal vector, and the source coding theorem says no lossless code beats it on average. Huffman and arithmetic coding approach it, and the gap is at most one bit per symbol.
reduction: Entropy is a linear functional of surprisal.

title: Sample Moments
objects: A mean is a projection; a variance is a squared residual norm.
structure: The mean is the projection of x onto the all-ones vector, ̄𝑥1 = 11⊤ 𝑛x, and the variance is the squared norm of the residual. The 𝑛−1 arises because that projection consumes one dimension — degrees of freedom is a rank statement.
reduction: Mean and variance are a projection and its residual norm.

title: Skewness and Kurtosis
objects: Standardised third and fourth moments.
structure: Higher moments are linear functionals of the distribution but nonlinear in the data, and standardising makes them scale-invariant. Their sample versions have high variance, which is why they are unreliable in small samples.
reduction: Moments are linear functionals of the distribution.

title: Quantile Definition
objects: A generalised inverse of a monotone function.
structure: Sorting is a permutation matrix, and the quantile picks an entry of the permuted vector — so the operation is a permutation followed by a selection. Quantiles are equivariant under monotone transforms, which moments are not.
reduction: Quantiles are permutation-plus-selection.

title: Interquartile Range and Outlier Fence
objects: A linear contrast of two order statistics.
structure: Exactly a difference and an aﬀine extension, so both are linear in the sorted vector. The 1.5 factor corresponds to about 0.7% tail mass under normality.
reduction: The fences are aﬀine in order statistics.

title: Median Absolute Deviation
objects: A robust scale estimate — a median of an ℓ1 residual.
structure: The constant makes it consistent for the normal standard deviation, so it is a rescaled robust norm. It replaces the ℓ2 residual norm of the standard deviation with a median, trading eﬀiciency for a 50% breakdown point.
reduction: MAD replaces an ℓ2 norm with a median of absolute residuals.

title: Winsorised and Trimmed Mean
objects: A weighted mean with a truncated weight vector.
structure: Exactly an inner product of the sorted vector with a weight vector that is zero at the ends — an L-estimator. The whole family of trimmed and Winsorised estimators is a family of weight vectors.
reduction: Trimmed means are inner products with truncated weight vectors.

title: Breakdown Point
objects: A robustness threshold.
structure: The mean has breakdown zero because a single point moves it without bound — the weight vector is uniform and unbounded in influence. The median has breakdown 1/2, the maximum possible, because its weight vector concentrates on the centre.
reduction: Breakdown reflects the weight vector’s concentration.

title: Influence Function
objects: A Gâteaux derivative of a statistical functional.
structure: Exactly a directional derivative in the space of distributions, so it is the linearisation of an estimator. Bounded influence means the linearisation stays bounded, which is precisely what robustness requires.
reduction: The influence function is a functional derivative — a linearisation.

title: Empirical CDF and Kolmogorov–Smirnov Distance
objects: A sup-norm distance between two functions.
structure: An ℓ∞distance in function space, so it is a norm — and its distribution-free null distribution comes from the Brownian bridge. The empirical CDF itself is a normalised sum of indicators, hence linear in the data.
reduction: The statistic is a sup-norm between two linear functionals.

title: Population Stability Index
objects: A symmetrised KL-type divergence between two histograms.
structure: A sum over bins of a product of a difference and a log ratio — linear in the bin contributions. It measures drift by comparing two probability vectors, and the binning choice is a projection onto a coarse basis.
reduction: PSI is an additive divergence over a binned basis.

title: Minkowski Distance
objects: The ℓ𝑝norm of a difference vector.
structure: A genuine norm for 𝑝≥1 (the unit ball is convex), failing the triangle inequality below one. 𝑝= 1 gives Manhattan, 𝑝= 2 Euclidean, 𝑝→∞Chebyshev — a family of unit balls interpolating from a cross-polytope to a cube.
reduction: The distance is an ℓ𝑝norm of a difference.

title: Mahalanobis Distance
objects: A quadratic form with the inverse covariance as metric.
structure: Exactly a Euclidean distance after whitening by Σ−1/2 — a change of basis that makes correlated data isotropic. It is the natural distance whenever the data have a covariance structure, and it appears in discriminant analysis, outlier detection, and 𝑑′ alike.
reduction: Mahalanobis distance is Euclidean distance in whitened coordinates.

title: Cosine Similarity
objects: A normalised inner product. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 14
structure: Exactly the inner product on the unit sphere, so it measures angle and ignores magnitude. On centred data it equals the Pearson correlation — the same object under a different name.
reduction: Cosine similarity is a normalised inner product.

title: Jaccard Index
objects: A normalised inner product of binary vectors.
structure: The intersection is a⊤b and the union is ‖a‖1 + ‖b‖1 −a⊤b, so the index is a ratio of linear forms. MinHash estimates it by sampling, preserving the ratio in expectation.
reduction: The index is a ratio of inner products and ℓ1 norms. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 15

title: Edit (Levenshtein) Distance
objects: A dynamic programming matrix in the min-plus semiring.
structure: The same tropical recursion as sequence alignment, and it satisfies the triangle inequality — so it is a genuine metric on strings. The metric property is what allows metric-tree indexing.
reduction: Edit distance is a min-plus recursion and a metric.

title: Earth Mover’s (Wasserstein) Distance
objects: An optimal transport linear program.
structure: Exactly a transportation LP with marginal constraints, and its dual is the Kantorovich–Rubinstein formulation over 1-Lipschitz functions. The constraint matrix is totally unimodular, so the optimum is achieved at a vertex with integral structure.
reduction: Wasserstein distance is a linear program with a totally unimodular constraint matrix.

title: Kullback–Leibler Divergence
objects: An expectation of a log ratio — linear in 𝑃.
structure: Linear in the first argument given the log-ratio vector, but not symmetric and not a metric. Its asymmetry is exactly why forward and reverse KL give different variational approximations — mode-covering versus mode-seeking.
reduction: KL is a linear functional of 𝑃against a log-ratio vector.

title: Jensen–Shannon Divergence
objects: A symmetrised divergence about the midpoint distribution.
structure: The midpoint is a convex combination — a linear average — and the symmetrisation makes √ JSD a true metric. It is bounded by log 2, which makes it comparable across problems.
reduction: Symmetrisation about a linear midpoint yields a metric.

title: Locality-Sensitive Hashing
objects: A random projection followed by quantisation.
structure: For cosine similarity the hash is sign(r⊤x) with r random Gaussian — a random hyperplane, so the collision probability is 1 −𝜃/𝜋. The whole scheme is a random linear map plus a sign, which is why it preserves angles.
reduction: LSH is a random linear projection plus quantisation.

title: Curse of Dimensionality
objects: Concentration of distances in high dimension.
structure: Distances concentrate because the sum of 𝑝independent contributions has relative fluctuation 𝑂(1/√𝑝) — a central limit statement. Nearest neighbours become meaningless, which is why every method in the next section reduces dimension first.
reduction: Distance concentration follows from summing many independent terms.

title: Principal Component Analysis
objects: The eigendecomposition of the covariance matrix.
structure: Literally an eigenvalue problem: the components are eigenvectors, ordered by eigenvalue, and they are orthogonal because Σ is symmetric. Each successive component maximises a Rayleigh quotient subject to orthogonality with the previous ones.
reduction: PCA is the covariance matrix’s eigendecomposition.

title: Explained Variance Ratio
objects: A normalised eigenvalue.
structure: The trace of Σ is the total variance, so the eigenvalues partition it exactly — a spectral decomposition of variance. The cumulative sum’s shape is the scree plot.
reduction: Eigenvalues partition the trace.

title: PCA via SVD
objects: The singular value decomposition of the centred data matrix.
structure: 𝑉’s columns are the principal directions and 𝜎2 𝑖/(𝑛−1) are the eigenvalues, so the SVD gives PCA without forming the covariance — which squares the condition number. Eckart–Young says the rank-𝑘truncation is the best rank-𝑘approximation in Frobenius norm, which is the whole justification for truncating.
reduction: PCA is the SVD; truncation is optimal by Eckart–Young.

title: Kernel PCA
objects: An eigendecomposition of the centred Gram matrix.
structure: PCA in a feature space accessed only through inner products, so the computation is an 𝑛× 𝑛eigen- problem rather than a 𝑝×𝑝one. The kernel trick works precisely because PCA depends on the data only through inner products.
reduction: Kernel PCA is PCA on the Gram matrix.

title: Multidimensional Scaling
objects: A double-centred squared distance matrix, then eigendecomposed.
structure: Double centring converts squared distances into inner products exactly, so classical MDS is PCA on the recovered Gram matrix. If 𝐷is Euclidean, 𝐵is positive semidefinite and the embedding is exact — negative eigenvalues measure non-Euclideanness.
reduction: MDS is an eigendecomposition of a double-centred distance matrix.

title: Isomap Geodesic Distance
objects: MDS applied to graph shortest-path distances.
structure: The shortest paths are computed by min-plus matrix closure, then classical MDS eigendecomposes the result — a tropical computation feeding a spectral one. It unfolds a manifold exactly when the neighbourhood graph approximates geodesics well.
reduction: Isomap composes a min-plus closure with an eigendecomposition.

title: t-SNE Objective
objects: A KL divergence between two neighbour distributions.
structure: Minimised by gradient descent over embedding coordinates, so there is no closed form and no eigen- decomposition. The heavy-tailed low-dimensional kernel breaks any linear correspondence — distances between clusters in a t-SNE plot are not interpretable, which is a direct consequence of the objective being purely local.
reduction: The embedding is a nonconvex optimisation with no linear structure.
status: No faithful linear form. Global geometry is not preserved.

title: UMAP Cross-Entropy Objective
objects: A fuzzy set cross-entropy between two graph representations.
structure: Better global structure than t-SNE because the repulsive term penalises distant points that should be distant, but still a nonconvex graph layout problem. Its spectral initialisation is a Laplacian eigenmap, so the linear part is only the starting point.
reduction: Only the spectral initialisation is linear.
status: No faithful linear form (except the initialisation).

title: Random Projection Bound
objects: The Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma.
structure: A random linear map into 𝑘dimensions preserves all pairwise distances within (1 ± 𝜀) with high probability, and 𝑘is independent of the original dimension. It is a purely linear-algebraic result — a random matrix acts as a near-isometry on any fixed finite set.
reduction: A random linear map is a near-isometry on finite sets.

title: Non-Negative Matrix Factorisation
objects: A constrained low-rank matrix factorisation.
structure: Non-negativity forces a parts-based rather than a cancelling representation, and it makes the problem nonconvex — though convex in 𝑊and 𝐻separately, which is why alternating least squares works. Unlike the SVD the factorisation is not unique, so interpretation requires care.
reduction: NMF is a biconvex low-rank factorisation.

title: K-Means Objective
objects: A total within-cluster scatter — a trace.
structure: Minimising 𝐽is equivalent to maximising the between-cluster scatter, since the total is fixed — an exact trace decomposition, tr(𝑆𝑇) = tr(𝑆𝑊) + tr(𝑆𝐵). Relaxing the cluster indicator matrix to be orthonormal turns k-means into a PCA-like eigenproblem, which is the link to spectral methods.
reduction: K-means is a trace decomposition; its relaxation is an eigenproblem.

title: Silhouette Coeﬀicient
objects: A normalised contrast between within- and between-cluster distances.
structure: Exactly a difference of two averages over the distance matrix, normalised — a linear functional per point. Averaging over points gives a single quality score.
reduction: The coeﬀicient is a normalised distance contrast.

title: Elbow and Gap Statistic
objects: A comparison of within-cluster dispersion against a null reference.
structure: Exactly a contrast in log space between observed and reference dispersion, with the reference generated from a uniform null. It formalises the elbow by giving it a baseline.
reduction: The statistic is a log-space contrast against a null.

title: Gaussian Mixture Model
objects: A convex combination of Gaussian densities.
structure: Linear in the mixture weights, and each component’s covariance matrix defines a Mahalanobis metric — so the model is a set of ellipsoids. K-means is its limit as all covariances become 𝜀𝐼.
reduction: The mixture is a linear combination of densities.

title: EM Algorithm Steps
objects: An alternation between a responsibility matrix and weighted estimates.
structure: The E-step normalises rows of a weight matrix; the M-step computes weighted means and covariances — both linear operations. Monotone likelihood increase follows from a variational bound, and convergence is to a local optimum.
reduction: EM alternates two linear estimation steps.

title: DBSCAN Density Criterion
objects: A thresholded row sum of the 𝜀-neighbourhood adjacency matrix.
structure: Core points are those whose adjacency row sum exceeds the threshold, and clusters are connected components of the core-point subgraph. It is a graph connectivity computation on a thresholded distance matrix.
reduction: DBSCAN thresholds an adjacency matrix and finds components.

title: Hierarchical Linkage Criteria
objects: Different reduction operators on the distance matrix.
