structure: The Lance–Williams formula expresses every linkage as a linear recurrence on the merged distances, with different coeﬀicients per method. That single recurrence unifies all of them as one parametrised linear update. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 37
reduction: All linkages are one linear recurrence with different coeﬀicients.

title: Spectral Clustering
objects: The graph Laplacian’s smallest eigenvectors.
structure: 𝐿is symmetric positive semidefinite, and the multiplicity of eigenvalue zero equals the number of connected components — an exact rank statement. The Fiedler vector (second smallest) gives the optimal relaxed bipartition, so spectral clustering is a relaxation of a combinatorial cut problem into an eigenproblem.
reduction: Spectral clustering is an eigendecomposition of the Laplacian. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 38

title: Adjusted Rand Index
objects: A chance-corrected agreement on a contingency table.
structure: Built from pair counts in the contingency table between two clusterings, so it is a quadratic functional of the table. The chance correction subtracts the expectation under fixed margins — the rank-one baseline again.
reduction: ARI compares a table against a rank-one chance model.

title: Normalised Mutual Information
objects: A normalised divergence from the rank-one joint.
structure: Mutual information measures departure of the joint contingency table from the outer product of its margins, normalised to [0, 1]. It is invariant to label permutation because permutations act on both margins consistently.
reduction: NMI is a normalised rank-one departure measure.

title: Autocorrelation Function
objects: The normalised diagonals of a Toeplitz covariance matrix.
structure: Stationarity makes the covariance matrix Toeplitz — constant along diagonals — so the whole matrix is determined by one vector. Toeplitz systems are solved in 𝑂(𝑛2) by Levinson–Durbin rather than 𝑂(𝑛3), which is the structural payoff.
reduction: Stationary covariance is Toeplitz; the ACF is its first row.

title: Stationarity Conditions
objects: An eigenvalue containment condition.
structure: Writing the AR process in companion-matrix form, stationarity is exactly the requirement that the companion matrix’s spectral radius is below one. It is the same condition as stability of a linear dynamical system.
reduction: Stationarity is a spectral radius condition on the companion matrix.

title: ARIMA Model
objects: A ratio of two polynomial operators in the lag operator.
structure: The backshift operator 𝐵is a shift matrix, and the polynomials in it are banded Toeplitz operators — so the model is a rational filter. Differencing (1 −𝐵)𝑑removes unit roots by cancelling eigenvalues at one.
reduction: ARIMA is a rational filter built from shift operators.

title: Exponential Smoothing
objects: A first-order linear recursion — an IIR filter.
structure: Expanding gives geometrically decaying weights on past observations, so it is an inner product with an exponential weight vector. It is equivalent to an ARIMA(0,1,1) model, which is why it works well on trending series.
reduction: Smoothing is an exponentially weighted inner product.

title: STL Decomposition
objects: An additive decomposition into three components.
structure: Each component is extracted by local regression (LOESS), which is a linear smoother — so the whole decomposition is a sum of three linear operators applied to the series. The operators are near-projections onto trend, seasonal, and residual subspaces.
reduction: STL applies three linear smoothers summing to the identity.

title: Dynamic Time Warping
objects: A min-plus dynamic programming matrix.
structure: The same tropical recursion as edit distance and sequence alignment, computing an optimal monotone alignment path. It violates the triangle inequality, so it is not a metric — which complicates indexing.
reduction: DTW is a min-plus recursion.

title: CUSUM Change Detection
objects: A rectified cumulative sum.
structure: Cumulative summation is a triangular linear operator, and the rectifier resets it — so the statistic is a linear accumulation with a floor. It is optimal for detecting a step change in mean by the sequential probability ratio argument.
reduction: CUSUM is a rectified triangular accumulation.

title: EWMA Control Chart
objects: The same exponential filter as entry 44, with control limits.
structure: The variance of 𝑧𝑡converges to 𝜎2𝜆/(2−𝜆), computable exactly because the filter is linear. The limits widen to their asymptote as the filter reaches steady state.
reduction: The chart is a linear filter with a closed-form variance.

title: Isolation Forest Anomaly Score
objects: A score from expected path lengths in random trees.
structure: Anomalies are isolated by fewer random axis-aligned splits, so the score is a normalised expected depth. The random splits are axis-aligned, which means the method is sensitive to rotation — a genuine limitation of using coordinate-wise cuts on correlated data.
reduction: The score is a normalised expected depth; axis alignment breaks rotation invariance.

title: Local Outlier Factor
objects: A ratio of local densities averaged over neighbours.
structure: Local reachability density is a reciprocal of an average distance, so LOF is a ratio of two linear functionals of the distance matrix. It detects outliers relative to local density rather than globally.
reduction: LOF is a ratio of averaged distance functionals.

title: A/B Test Sample Size
objects: An inverse-square relation between sample and effect size.
structure: The same Fisher information inversion as in trial design — required information scales as the inverse squared effect. Detecting a 1% lift needs roughly a hundred times the sample of a 10% lift.
reduction: Sample size inverts an information requirement.

title: CUPED Variance Reduction
objects: A regression adjustment using a pre-experiment covariate.
structure: Exactly the least squares coeﬀicient, so the adjustment projects out the component of 𝑌explained by 𝑋— the residual has variance (1 −𝜌2)Var(𝑌). It is ANCOVA, and the variance reduction is the regression 𝑅2.
reduction: CUPED is a regression projection; variance reduction is 𝑅2.

title: Sequential Testing Always-Valid p-Value
objects: A reciprocal of a running likelihood ratio.
structure: The likelihood ratio is a non-negative martingale, so Ville’s inequality bounds the probability it ever exceeds 1/𝛼— validity at all stopping times follows from one martingale inequality. Log-likelihood ratios add over observations, which is what makes the running product tractable.
reduction: Validity follows from a martingale bound on an additive log-likelihood.

title: Sample Ratio Mismatch Test
objects: A quadratic form in the observed-minus-expected vector.
structure: Exactly a weighted squared norm of the residual, with weights 1/𝐸𝑖. A significant result invalidates the randomisation, so it is a check on the orthogonality that the experiment depends on.
reduction: The test is a weighted squared residual norm.

title: Simpson’s Paradox
objects: A failure of ratio comparisons to survive aggregation.
structure: Ratios are not linear functionals, so their ordering is not preserved under addition of numerators and denominators — the mediant of two fractions need not lie in the same order. The paradox is precisely a demonstration that ratios do not add.
reduction: Ratios are not linear; aggregation does not preserve their order.
status: No faithful linear form. The paradox is the failure of linearity.

title: Precision, Recall, and F1
objects: Row and column normalisations of a confusion matrix, and their harmonic mean. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 55
structure: Precision normalises by the predicted column, recall by the actual row — the same transposition structure as PPV and sensitivity. The harmonic mean penalises imbalance, which is why 𝐹1 is low unless both are high.
reduction: The metrics are row and column normalisations of one matrix.

title: Precision–Recall AUC
objects: A Riemann sum — a linear functional of the curve. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 56
structure: Exactly a weighted sum of precisions with recall increments as weights. Unlike ROC AUC it depends on class balance, since the baseline is the positive rate rather than 0.5.
reduction: Average precision is a weighted sum along the curve.

title: Normalised Discounted Cumulative Gain
objects: An inner product of gains with a positional discount vector.
structure: Exactly a weighted sum where the weight vector is a fixed logarithmic discount, normalised by the ideal ordering. Sorting is a permutation, so nDCG measures how close the achieved permutation is to the optimal one under a fixed weight vector. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 57
reduction: nDCG is a normalised inner product with a discount vector.

title: Bootstrap Confidence Interval
objects: Quantiles of a resampling distribution.
structure: Resampling multiplies the data by a multinomial weight vector, so each bootstrap replicate is a reweighted statistic. For linear statistics the bootstrap distribution has an exact mean and variance, which is why it works so well for means and so poorly for extremes.
reduction: Bootstrapping is random reweighting.

title: Benford’s Law
objects: A scale-invariant distribution over leading digits.
structure: The only distribution invariant under multiplication by any constant, because taking logs turns scaling into translation and the uniform distribution on the circle is translation-invariant. It is a Haar measure argument, and its use in fraud detection is a goodness-of-fit test against this fixed vector.
reduction: Benford’s law is translation invariance in log space.

title: Empirical Risk Minimisation
objects: An average loss over a hypothesis class.
structure: The empirical risk is a linear functional of the per-example loss vector, so the objective is a mean — and its concentration around the true risk is the whole content of generalisation theory. For linear 𝑓and convex 𝐿the problem is convex.
reduction: Empirical risk is a mean of a loss vector.

title: Bias–Variance Decomposition
objects: An orthogonal decomposition of squared error.
structure: The cross terms vanish exactly because the bias is the deviation of the mean and the variance is the deviation from it — Pythagoras in the space of random variables. It is the same orthogonal split as in ANOVA and in the Brier score.
reduction: The decomposition is an orthogonal projection identity.

title: Double Descent
objects: A conditioning catastrophe at 𝑝= 𝑛.
structure: When parameters equal samples the design matrix is square and typically ill-conditioned, so the minimum-norm solution has enormous norm — the smallest singular value approaches zero. Beyond the threshold, extra parameters give the pseudoinverse more room and the minimum-norm solution becomes better behaved. Double descent is a statement about the smallest singular value of 𝑋.
reduction: The peak is where 𝑋’s smallest singular value is worst.

title: Squared Error Loss
objects: A quadratic form in the residual.
structure: Its minimiser is the conditional mean, and for linear models the solution is a projection onto the column space — the normal equations. Quadratic loss is the unique loss whose optimum is the mean.
reduction: Squared loss gives a projection solution.

title: Absolute and Huber Loss
objects: A piecewise objective, quadratic near zero and linear in the tails.
structure: Absolute loss gives the conditional median rather than the mean, and Huber interpolates — bounded influence in the tails, so outliers pull with constant rather than growing force. It is exactly a bounded influence function.
reduction: Huber bounds the influence function; the quadratic region stays linear.

title: Cross-Entropy Loss
objects: An inner product of a one-hot vector with a log-probability vector.
structure: Exactly a linear functional of the log-probabilities, so gradients with respect to the logits are simply ̂p −y — remarkably clean, and the reason softmax and cross-entropy are always paired.
reduction: Cross-entropy is an inner product in log space; its logit gradient is a difference.

title: Softmax Function
objects: A normalised exponential — a map from logits to the simplex.
structure: Shift-invariant, so the logits have one redundant dimension — the map’s Jacobian diag(p) −pp⊤is singular with 1 in its null space. It is the same normalised weight vector as every partition function in this compendium.
reduction: Softmax is a normalised weight vector with a rank-deficient Jacobian.

title: Hinge Loss
objects: A rectified linear function of the margin.
structure: Piecewise linear with a kink at margin one, so the subgradient is either zero or −𝑦x — only misclassified and margin points contribute. That sparsity in the gradient is what produces support vectors.
reduction: Hinge loss is a rectified linear function; its subgradient is sparse.

title: Focal Loss
objects: Cross-entropy with a confidence-dependent reweighting.
structure: The modulating factor down-weights easy examples, so it is a diagonal reweighting of the per-example loss vector that depends on the current prediction. It is an adaptive weight, not a change of the loss’s structure.
reduction: Focal loss is cross-entropy with an adaptive diagonal weight.

title: Regularised Objective
objects: A sum of a data term and a penalty term.
structure: Exactly additive, so the penalty shifts the optimum along a regularisation path parametrised by 𝜆. The Lagrangian view makes it a constrained problem — the penalty is the dual of a norm ball constraint.
reduction: Regularisation adds a penalty; the path is a parametrised family of solutions.

title: Ridge and Lasso Penalties
objects: Two norms whose unit balls have different geometry. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 12
structure: Ridge has a closed form ̂𝜃= (𝑋⊤𝑋+ 𝜆𝐼)−1𝑋⊤y — the penalty shifts every eigenvalue of 𝑋⊤𝑋up by 𝜆, which is exactly why it fixes ill-conditioning. Lasso’s corners on the ℓ1 ball make the solution sparse, since the optimum lands on a face where coordinates are exactly zero.
reduction: Ridge shifts the spectrum; lasso’s ball geometry produces sparsity.

title: Elastic Net
objects: A convex combination of two norms.
structure: The ℓ2 term makes the objective strictly convex, so correlated predictors are selected together rather than arbitrarily — the grouping effect. It is a linear interpolation between two penalty geometries.
reduction: Elastic net linearly interpolates two norm balls.
status: Exact linear. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 13

title: Generalisation Gap
objects: A deviation between a population and an empirical mean.
structure: Bounding it uniformly over the hypothesis class is the core problem, and the bounds are concentration inequalities on sums of independent terms. Linearity of expectation plus a tail bound does all the work.
reduction: The gap is a concentration statement about a mean.
status: Exact linear. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 14

title: VC Dimension Bound
objects: A capacity measure counting realisable labellings.
structure: For linear classifiers in ℝ𝑝the VC dimension is exactly 𝑝+ 1 — the number of free parameters of a hyperplane. That equality is the cleanest link between a combinatorial capacity and a dimension.
reduction: For hyperplanes, VC dimension equals the parameter count.
status: Exact linear (linear classifiers). The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 15

title: Rademacher Complexity
objects: An expected supremum of a random inner product.
structure: Exactly the expected maximum correlation with random signs — an inner product of the function’s values with a random ±1 vector. For linear classes bounded in norm it evaluates in closed form via Cauchy– Schwarz, giving ℜ𝑛≤𝐵𝑅/√𝑛.
reduction: Rademacher complexity is an expected supremum of inner products.

title: PAC Learning Sample Complexity
objects: A sample requirement scaling with capacity.
structure: Linear in the dimension and inverse-square in accuracy, which is the same information-theoretic scaling as everywhere else. Doubling accuracy needs four times the data.
reduction: Sample complexity is linear in capacity, inverse-square in accuracy.

title: Margin Bound
objects: A bound depending on the margin rather than the dimension.
structure: The complexity term involves ‖w‖ 2 𝑅2 rather than 𝑝, so it is dimension-free — which explains why SVMs and kernel methods work in infinite-dimensional spaces. Norm control replaces dimension control.
reduction: Norm-based capacity replaces dimension-based capacity.

title: Bayes Error Rate
objects: An irreducible error from class overlap.
structure: A linear functional of the posterior, and no classifier can beat it. It is the analogue of the noise floor in every other estimation problem here.
reduction: The Bayes rate is a linear functional of the posterior.

title: No Free Lunch for Learning
objects: A symmetry argument over the space of target functions.
structure: Averaging over a symmetric set of problems makes every algorithm’s expected performance identical — a group-invariance statement. It says inductive bias is necessary, not that any particular bias is good.
reduction: The theorem is a symmetry (invariance) argument.

title: Cross-Validation Estimate
objects: An average over held-out folds.
structure: Exactly a mean of 𝐾estimates, though the folds are dependent — so the variance of the estimate is not the naive one. For linear models with squared loss, leave-one-out has the closed form ∑(𝑟𝑖/(1 −ℎ𝑖𝑖))2 where ℎ𝑖𝑖are the hat matrix’s diagonal entries, so no refitting is needed at all.
reduction: LOOCV for linear models is a closed form in the hat matrix’s diagonal.

title: SVM Primal Problem
objects: A quadratic program with linear constraints.
structure: Convex with a unique optimum, and maximising the margin is minimising the norm — the geometric margin is 2/ ‖w‖. It is a quadratic objective over a polyhedron.
reduction: The SVM is a quadratic program.

title: SVM Dual Problem
objects: A quadratic form in the dual variables built from a Gram matrix.
structure: The data appear only through inner products, which is precisely what makes the kernel trick possible. Complementary slackness makes most 𝛼𝑖zero — the support vectors are the active constraints.
reduction: The dual is a quadratic form in the Gram matrix.

title: Kernel Trick
objects: An inner product in an implicit feature space.
structure: Mercer’s theorem says any positive semidefinite kernel corresponds to some feature map, so the Gram matrix’s positive semidefiniteness is the condition for a valid kernel. Computation in the feature space never happens — only the 𝑛× 𝑛matrix is formed.
reduction: Kernels are inner products; validity is positive semidefiniteness.

title: Common Kernels
objects: Three positive semidefinite kernels with different feature spaces.
structure: The RBF kernel’s feature space is infinite-dimensional, yet the Gram matrix is finite — which is the whole point. Sums and products of kernels are kernels, so the valid kernels form a cone closed under those operations.
reduction: Kernels form a closed cone; the RBF’s feature space is infinite-dimensional.

title: Representer Theorem
objects: A finite expansion in kernel functions at the data points.
structure: The optimum of any norm-regularised objective lies in the span of the training kernels — the component orthogonal to that span only increases the norm without changing the fit. It is a projection argument, and it reduces an infinite-dimensional optimisation to 𝑛coeﬀicients.
reduction: The theorem is an orthogonal projection argument.

title: Gaussian Process Posterior
objects: A linear solve against a regularised kernel matrix.
structure: The posterior mean is exactly kernel ridge regression, and the posterior covariance 𝐾∗∗−𝐾∗(𝐾+ 𝜎2𝐼)−1𝐾⊤ ∗is a Schur complement. The 𝑂(𝑛3) cost is the Cholesky factorisation, which is what limits GPs to moderate 𝑛.
reduction: GP regression is a linear solve; the variance is a Schur complement.

title: Bagging Variance Reduction
objects: The variance of an average of correlated estimators.
structure: Averaging 𝐵correlated predictors leaves an irreducible 𝜌𝜎2 floor, so the benefit is capped by the correlation. This formula is the entire justification for the next entry.
reduction: The variance of a mean of correlated variables has a correlation floor.

title: Random Forest Feature Subsampling
objects: A device for lowering 𝜌in entry 27.
structure: Restricting each split to a random feature subset decorrelates the trees, pushing 𝜌down so averaging helps more. It trades a small increase in individual tree bias for a large drop in the correlation floor.
reduction: Subsampling reduces the correlation term of the variance formula.

title: Out-of-Bag Error
objects: A built-in held-out estimate.
structure: The probability a sample is omitted from a bootstrap draw is (1−1/𝑛)𝑛→𝑒−1, so about 37% of trees never saw each point. That gives cross-validation for free — an exact consequence of the resampling distribution.
reduction: The 𝑒−1 fraction follows from the bootstrap’s inclusion probability.

title: AdaBoost Weight Update
objects: A multiplicative reweighting of the sample distribution.
structure: Multiplicative in weights means additive in log weights, and AdaBoost is exactly coordinate descent on the exponential loss. The learner weight 𝛼𝑡= 1 2 ln 1−𝜀𝑡 𝜀𝑡 is a log-odds — the same object as in every log-linear model here.
reduction: AdaBoost is coordinate descent on exponential loss; weights are log-additive.

title: Gradient Boosting
objects: A functional gradient descent — an additive expansion.
structure: The model is a sum of weak learners, each fitted to the negative gradient — so boosting is gradient descent in function space with a shrinkage step size 𝜈. Additivity is what makes the ensemble a linear combination of basis functions.
reduction: Boosting is gradient descent in function space; the model is an additive expansion.

title: XGBoost Regularised Objective
objects: A second-order Taylor expansion of the loss plus a penalty.
structure: Using both gradient and Hessian gives the optimal leaf weight in closed form, −𝐺𝑗/(𝐻𝑗+ 𝜆) — a Newton step on a diagonal Hessian. The split gain is the resulting objective improvement, which is a difference of such quadratic terms.
reduction: XGBoost takes Newton steps with a diagonal Hessian.

title: Feedforward Layer
objects: An aﬀine map followed by a pointwise nonlinearity.
structure: The aﬀine part is the entire learned content; without 𝜎a deep network collapses to a single matrix product, since the composition of aﬀine maps is aﬀine. Depth is only meaningful because of the nonlinearity — this is the single most important fact about neural networks stated in linear-algebraic terms.
reduction: A layer is an aﬀine map plus a nonlinearity; without the latter, depth is vacuous.

title: Universal Approximation Theorem
objects: A density statement about a span of ridge functions.
structure: The span of {𝜎(w⊤x + 𝑏)} is dense in continuous functions on compacts — a statement about a spanning set, not about how many elements are needed. The required width may be exponential, which is why the theorem justifies expressiveness but not practice.
reduction: The theorem is a density statement about a span.

title: Backpropagation
objects: A product of Jacobians, evaluated right to left.
structure: The chain rule gives 𝜕𝐿/𝜕x = 𝐽⊤ 1 𝐽⊤ 2 ⋯𝐽⊤ 𝐿∇𝐿, and reverse-mode evaluation is cheap because a matrix– vector product costs far less than a matrix–matrix one. Each weight gradient is a rank-one outer product, which is why the update is eﬀicient. Backpropagation is an associativity choice in a matrix product.
reduction: Backpropagation is a Jacobian product, associated right to left.

title: Activation Functions
objects: The pointwise nonlinearities that make depth meaningful.
structure: ReLU is piecewise linear, so a ReLU network is a piecewise linear function whose pieces are polyhedral regions — the network partitions input space into cells and is aﬀine on each. Counting those regions bounds expressivity.
reduction: ReLU networks are piecewise aﬀine on a polyhedral partition.

title: Vanishing and Exploding Gradients
objects: A product of many Jacobians.
structure: The gradient norm is governed by the product of the Jacobians’ singular values, so anything other than a product near one is exponentially bad in depth. It is exactly the Lyapunov exponent of a matrix product — the same object as in random matrix products elsewhere in this compendium.
reduction: The problem is the Lyapunov exponent of a Jacobian product.

title: Xavier and He Initialisation
objects: A variance scaling chosen to keep Jacobian singular values near one.
structure: The scaling preserves activation variance layer to layer, which keeps the Jacobian product’s spectral norm near unity. It is a direct engineering fix for entry 37, derived by a variance propagation calculation.
reduction: Initialisation tunes the Jacobian spectrum to preserve scale.

title: Batch Normalisation
objects: A per-feature standardisation followed by an aﬀine map. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 39
structure: Centring and scaling is a diagonal whitening of the activations, which improves the loss landscape’s conditioning — it makes the Hessian’s eigenvalues more uniform. The learned 𝛾, 𝛽restore representational capacity that the normalisation would otherwise remove.
reduction: Batch norm is a diagonal whitening plus an aﬀine map.

title: Layer Normalisation
objects: The same whitening along the other axis.
structure: Normalising per example makes the operation batch-independent, which is why transformers use it. It is the transpose of the batch norm operation in terms of which axis is reduced. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 40
reduction: Layer norm whitens along the transposed axis.

title: Dropout
objects: A random diagonal mask applied to activations.
structure: Exactly multiplication by a random diagonal matrix, and its expectation is a scalar multiple — which is why inference simply scales. For linear regression, dropout is provably equivalent to ℓ2 regularisation with a data-dependent scaling.
reduction: Dropout is a random diagonal matrix; in expectation it is ridge-like.
status: Exact linear. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 41

title: Residual Connection
objects: An identity plus a learned perturbation.
structure: The Jacobian becomes 𝐼+ 𝜕𝐹/𝜕𝑥, so gradients flow through the identity path regardless of what 𝐹 does — the product of Jacobians is bounded away from zero. It is the cleanest fix to entry 37, and it works by adding an identity matrix.
reduction: Residuals add an identity to each Jacobian.

title: Convolution Operation
objects: A Toeplitz (or block-circulant) matrix acting on the input.
structure: Convolution is a linear map with tied, sparse weights — the same matrix structure as any translation- invariant operator, diagonalised by the Fourier transform. Weight sharing is exactly the constraint that the matrix be Toeplitz, and that constraint is where the parameter savings come from.
reduction: Convolution is multiplication by a Toeplitz matrix.

title: Convolution Output Size
objects: The output dimension of the Toeplitz operator.
structure: Padding and stride determine the matrix’s shape, so the formula is a dimension count. Stride subsam- ples the rows, which is a selection matrix composed with the convolution.
reduction: The formula counts the operator’s output dimension.

title: Receptive Field Growth
objects: The support of a composed sequence of local operators.
structure: Composing banded matrices widens the band additively for stride one and multiplicatively with striding — the support of the product grows as the sum of the supports. Dilated convolutions widen the band without adding parameters.
reduction: The receptive field is the support of a product of banded matrices.

title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
objects: Three linear projections, a Gram matrix, a softmax, and a weighted sum.
structure: 𝑄= 𝑋𝑊𝑄, 𝐾= 𝑋𝑊𝐾, 𝑉= 𝑋𝑊𝑉are all linear; 𝑄𝐾⊤is a similarity Gram matrix; the softmax makes it row-stochastic; multiplying by 𝑉is a convex combination of value vectors. The scaling by √𝑑𝑘keeps the logits’ variance constant so the softmax does not saturate. Everything but one softmax is matrix multiplication.
reduction: Attention is a data-dependent row-stochastic matrix applied to a linear projection.
status: Exact linear apart from the softmax.

title: Multi-Head Attention
objects: A block-diagonal collection of low-rank projections, recombined linearly.
structure: Each head projects to 𝑑/ℎdimensions, so each is a rank-limited attention operation, and concatenation plus 𝑊𝑂is a linear recombination. The total parameter count matches single-head attention at full width — heads buy diversity of subspaces, not capacity.
reduction: Multi-head attention is a block-structured low-rank decomposition.
status: Exact linear apart from the softmaxes.

title: Positional Encoding
objects: A fixed Fourier basis added to the embeddings.
structure: Because relative positions correspond to rotations in each frequency’s two-dimensional subspace, a shift is a linear map on the encoding — which is what lets attention learn relative offsets. Rotary embeddings make this explicit by applying the rotation directly to 𝑄and 𝐾.
reduction: Positional encoding is a Fourier basis; shifts act as rotations.

title: Transformer Parameter Count
objects: A count dominated by the four 𝑑× 𝑑weight matrices per layer.
structure: Attention contributes 4𝑑2 (Q, K, V, O) and the feedforward block 8𝑑2 at the usual 4× width — so parameters scale quadratically in width and linearly in depth. Every parameter is an entry of a matrix.
reduction: The count is the total size of the layer matrices.

title: Neural Scaling Law
objects: A power law — linear in log–log.
structure: Loss falls as a power of parameters, data, or compute, so fitting the exponents is a linear regression in log space. The predictability across many orders of magnitude is what makes large-scale training plannable.
reduction: Scaling laws are linear in logs.

title: Compute-Optimal Allocation
objects: A constrained optimisation of a log-linear loss surface.
structure: Minimising loss subject to a compute budget 𝐶≈6𝑁𝐷is a Lagrange problem on a log-linear surface, so the solution is a fixed ratio of exponents. The Chinchilla result — roughly 20 tokens per parameter — is the solution of that two-variable optimisation.
reduction: The allocation solves a Lagrange condition on a log-linear surface.

title: Autoencoder Reconstruction
objects: A composition of an encoder and a decoder.
structure: With linear 𝑓and 𝑔and squared loss, the optimal autoencoder spans exactly the same subspace as PCA — the solution is the leading singular subspace, though not necessarily the individual components. Nonlinearity is what lets it beat PCA.
reduction: A linear autoencoder recovers the PCA subspace.

title: Variational Autoencoder ELBO
objects: A reconstruction term minus a divergence term.
structure: For Gaussian 𝑞and 𝑝the KL term has a closed form in the means and log-variances — a sum of simple scalar expressions per dimension, since the covariances are diagonal. The bound is exactly the log evidence minus the posterior approximation gap.
reduction: The Gaussian KL is a closed-form sum over diagonal components.

title: Reparametrisation Trick
objects: An aﬀine map of a fixed noise variable.
structure: Writing the sample as an aﬀine function of parameter-free noise makes the gradient pass through — the randomness is moved outside the differentiated path. It is precisely the linearity of the location–scale family that makes this work.
reduction: The trick exploits the aﬀine structure of location–scale families.

title: GAN Minimax Objective
objects: A two-player zero-sum game.
structure: At the optimal discriminator the objective reduces to the Jensen–Shannon divergence, but the game dynamics are a nonconvex-nonconcave saddle point problem. Linearising the joint dynamics gives a Jacobian with imaginary eigenvalues — which is exactly why training oscillates rather than converges.
reduction: Training instability is imaginary eigenvalues of the game’s Jacobian.

title: Wasserstein GAN
objects: A supremum of a linear functional over a Lipschitz ball.
structure: Exactly the Kantorovich–Rubinstein dual of the transport LP — linear in the measures, with the constraint set being a norm ball in function space. The gradient penalty enforces the Lipschitz constraint approximately.
reduction: The objective is a linear program’s dual over a Lipschitz ball.

title: Diffusion Forward Process
objects: An aﬀine interpolation between data and noise.
structure: The forward process is exactly linear — a scalar times the data plus a scalar times Gaussian noise — with a closed form at every 𝑡because Gaussians are closed under aﬀine maps. All the learning happens in the reverse process.
reduction: The forward process is an aﬀine map with a closed form.

title: Diffusion Training Objective
objects: A squared error on the noise vector.
structure: Predicting the noise is equivalent to predicting the score up to a scalar, so this simple regression objective secretly learns the gradient of the log density. The whole training procedure is least squares on a linear target.
reduction: Training is least squares on an aﬀine-transformed target.

title: Score Function and Langevin Sampling
objects: A gradient step plus noise — a discretised Langevin diffusion.
structure: For a Gaussian target the score is exactly linear, −Σ−1(x −𝜇), so sampling is an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process whose convergence rate is Σ’s smallest eigenvalue. Ill-conditioned targets mix slowly for exactly the reason ill-conditioned linear systems converge slowly.
reduction: For Gaussian targets Langevin sampling is a linear OU process.

title: Contrastive Learning (InfoNCE)
objects: A softmax over inner products with a temperature.
structure: The similarities are inner products of normalised embeddings — a Gram matrix — and the loss is cross-entropy over its rows. It lower-bounds the mutual information between views, and the temperature rescales the Gram matrix before the softmax.
reduction: InfoNCE is cross-entropy over a scaled Gram matrix.
status: Exact linear apart from the softmax.

title: Uninformed Search Complexity
objects: An exponential count over a branching tree.
structure: The frontier size grows geometrically, so the cost is a geometric series dominated by its last term. It is counting rather than linear algebra, though the geometric growth is the same structure as a single-eigenvalue expansion.
reduction: Growth is geometric; the analysis is counting.

title: Iterative Deepening
objects: Repeated bounded searches whose costs form a geometric series.
structure: Re-expanding shallow nodes costs only a constant factor because ∑𝑖≤𝑑𝑏𝑖≈𝑏𝑑⋅ 𝑏 𝑏−1 — the geometric series’ sum is dominated by its last term. Trading time for space is free up to that factor.
reduction: The overhead is a geometric series ratio.

title: A* Evaluation Function
objects: A sum of a path cost and a heuristic estimate.
structure: Exactly additive, and the addition is what makes the priority queue ordering meaningful. With ℎa potential function, A* is Dijkstra on reweighted edges — a linear transformation of the weight matrix.
reduction: A* is Dijkstra under a potential transformation.

title: Admissibility and Consistency
objects: A lower bound and a triangle inequality.
structure: Consistency is exactly the triangle inequality, making ℎbehave like a metric potential — which guarantees the reweighted edge costs stay non-negative. Admissibility alone guarantees optimality but permits re-expansion.
reduction: Consistency is a triangle inequality on a potential.

title: Heuristic Dominance
objects: A partial order on heuristics.
structure: Pointwise domination gives a pointwise ordering of expanded node sets — a monotone relation. The maximum of two admissible heuristics is admissible, so admissible heuristics form a lattice under max.
reduction: Heuristics form a lattice under pointwise max.

title: Effective Branching Factor
objects: The root of a geometric series matching the observed node count.
structure: Solving for 𝑏∗inverts a geometric sum — a one-dimensional monotone solve. It is the standard summary of a heuristic’s practical quality.
reduction: The factor inverts a geometric series.

title: Pattern Database Heuristic
objects: A combination of abstraction-based lower bounds.
structure: Disjoint patterns allow addition because their costs partition the problem — an additive decomposition valid exactly when the abstractions do not share cost. Otherwise only the max is admissible.
reduction: Disjointness licenses addition; otherwise only max is safe.

title: Minimax Value
objects: An alternating max-min recursion — a tropical recursion with two operators.
structure: Alternating max and min over a game tree is a recursion in a semiring with two operations, so it does not reduce to a single tropical semiring. The alternation is what makes game trees fundamentally different from shortest-path problems.
reduction: Alternating max-min is not a single semiring recursion. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 9

title: Alpha–Beta Pruning Complexity
objects: An effective halving of the exponent.
structure: Perfect move ordering halves the depth exponent, which is equivalent to a square root of the search space — the same quadratic improvement as Grover’s algorithm, though achieved by pruning rather than inter- ference. Move ordering quality determines where between 𝑏𝑑and 𝑏𝑑/2 the true cost falls.
reduction: Pruning halves the exponent.

title: Monte Carlo Tree Search UCT
objects: An exploitation term plus an exploration bonus.
structure: Exactly the UCB1 formula, where the bonus is a confidence radius from Hoeffding’s inequality — a concentration bound on a sample mean. The sum is a linear combination of an estimate and its uncertainty.
reduction: UCT adds a mean and a concentration-derived radius.

title: PUCT with a Policy Prior
objects: A prior-weighted exploration term.
structure: The network’s policy prior multiplies the exploration bonus, so search effort is allocated proportionally to prior probability — a reweighting of the visit distribution. AlphaZero’s strength comes from this coupling of a learned vector with a search rule.
reduction: The prior is a multiplicative weight on the exploration term.

title: Constraint Satisfaction Arc Consistency
objects: A fixed-point computation on domain sets.
structure: Repeatedly pruning domains is a monotone decreasing operator on a lattice, so it converges to a greatest fixed point. Over the Boolean semiring the constraint propagation is a matrix operation on the constraint incidence structure.
reduction: Propagation is a monotone fixed point on a lattice.

title: STRIPS Planning Representation
objects: State vectors over propositions with additive and subtractive updates.
structure: States are binary vectors, and actions add and remove entries — an update s′ = (s∨a+)∧¬a−, which is linear over the Boolean semiring. Planning is reachability in that space, and it is PSPACE-complete.
reduction: State updates are Boolean-semiring linear operations.

title: Relaxed Plan Heuristic
objects: A relaxation removing the subtractive part of the update.
structure: Dropping deletes makes the state monotonically increasing, so reachability becomes a simple closure computation — the relaxation converts a hard problem into a monotone one. That monotonicity is exactly why the relaxed problem is polynomial.
reduction: Dropping deletes makes the update monotone.

title: Propositional Entailment
objects: A semantic consequence relation.
structure: Entailment reduces to unsatisfiability, which is NP-complete in general. Over 𝔽2, XOR clauses are solved by Gaussian elimination — the linear fragment is easy, and general SAT’s hardness comes precisely from leaving it.
reduction: The linear (XOR) fragment is Gaussian elimination; general SAT is not.

title: Resolution Rule
objects: An inference rule that is complete for refutation.
structure: Resolution is a combinatorial closure operation on clause sets, and the resolution proof’s length can be exponential. It is a symbolic rule with no additive structure.
reduction: Resolution is a symbolic closure with no linear form.

title: DPLL Unit Propagation
objects: A constraint propagation with backtracking.
structure: Unit propagation is a monotone closure on partial assignments — the same lattice fixed point as arc consistency. Backtracking is the non-monotone part and is where the exponential lives.
reduction: Propagation is a monotone closure; backtracking is not linear.

title: Conflict-Driven Clause Learning
objects: A cut in an implication graph producing a new constraint.
structure: The learned clause comes from a cut separating the conflict from the decisions — a graph cut, which is the primal side of a max-flow problem. That graph-theoretic step is what turned SAT solvers into industrial tools.
reduction: Clause learning is a cut in an implication graph.

title: First-Order Unification
objects: A most general substitution — a term-level solve.
structure: Unification is solving equations in a free term algebra, computable in near-linear time. It is a solve, but over a non-linear algebraic structure — substitution does not distribute like a linear map.
reduction: Unification solves equations in a free algebra, not a vector space.

title: Description Logic Subsumption
objects: A partial order on concepts.
structure: Concepts form a lattice under subsumption with meet and join given by conjunction and disjunction — the same lattice structure as subspaces under inclusion. That analogy is the closest linear correspondence available.
reduction: Concepts form a lattice, analogous to subspace inclusion.

title: Default Logic Extension
objects: A non-monotonic inference rule.
structure: Adding information can retract conclusions, so the consequence operator is non-monotone — the opposite of every closure operator above. Non-monotonicity is fundamentally incompatible with a linear (hence monotone in the relevant sense) formulation.
reduction: Non-monotonicity has no linear counterpart.

title: Bayesian Network Factorisation
objects: A tensor factorised into low-order conditional tables.
structure: The joint is a huge tensor, and the factorisation expresses it as a product of small ones — exactly a tensor network. The parameter count drops from exponential to the sum of the local table sizes, which is the whole point.
reduction: A Bayesian network is a tensor factorisation.

title: D-Separation
objects: A graphical criterion for factorisation of the joint.
structure: Conditional independence means the corresponding conditional joint has rank one when viewed as a matrix over the two variable sets. D-separation reads off which such rank-one factorisations hold from the graph alone.
reduction: Conditional independence is a rank-one factorisation of a conditional. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 23

title: Variable Elimination
objects: A tensor contraction — summing out an index.
structure: Each elimination step multiplies factors (an outer product) and sums an index (a contraction), so the whole algorithm is a sequence of tensor contractions. The cost is exponential in the largest intermediate factor’s size, which is the induced width of the elimination order — choosing the order is exactly the tensor-network contraction ordering problem. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 24
reduction: Inference is tensor contraction; cost is the contraction width.

title: Belief Propagation
objects: Message passing — repeated matrix–vector products along edges.
structure: Each message is a matrix–vector product with the pairwise potential matrix, followed by normalisation. On trees it converges exactly in two sweeps; on loopy graphs it may not converge, and its fixed points are stationary points of the Bethe free energy.
reduction: Message passing is matrix–vector multiplication along edges.
status: Exact linear. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 25

title: Junction Tree Complexity
objects: A cost exponential in the treewidth.
structure: Treewidth measures how far the graph is from a tree, and it is exactly the largest clique in a chordal completion — the maximal intermediate tensor’s order. It is the single parameter determining whether exact inference is feasible.
reduction: Treewidth is the maximum contraction rank.

title: Markov Random Field
objects: An undirected factorisation over cliques.
structure: For Gaussian MRFs the precision matrix’s sparsity pattern is the graph — a zero in Σ−1 means conditional independence. That equivalence between graph structure and matrix sparsity is the cleanest statement in graphical models.
reduction: For Gaussians, the graph is the precision matrix’s sparsity pattern.

title: Conditional Random Field
objects: A log-linear model over structured outputs.
structure: Exactly linear in the feature functions on the log scale, so the model is a softmax over an exponentially large output space. The forward–backward algorithm computes 𝑍by matrix products over the chain, making inference tractable.
reduction: CRFs are log-linear; inference is a matrix product over the chain.

title: Particle Filter Weight Update
objects: A multiplicative reweighting of a discrete measure.
structure: The posterior is represented by a weighted point mass vector, and each update multiplies entrywise by the likelihood and renormalises — a diagonal operator on the weight vector. It is the sampled version of the master equation’s linear update.
reduction: The update is a diagonal reweighting of a discrete measure.

title: Effective Sample Size for Particles
objects: The reciprocal squared norm of the weight vector.
structure: Exactly 1/ ‖w‖ 2 2 for normalised weights, equalling 𝑁when uniform and one when degenerate. Weight degeneracy is the weight vector collapsing onto a single coordinate — a rank-one collapse.
reduction: ESS is a reciprocal squared norm.

title: Variational Inference Objective
objects: A lower bound whose gap is a KL divergence.
structure: Maximising the ELBO is minimising 𝐷𝐾𝐿(𝑞‖𝑝) — the projection of the true posterior onto a tractable family in KL geometry. For mean-field families, coordinate ascent updates each factor in closed form, a sequence of linear-in-log updates.
reduction: Variational inference is a projection in KL geometry.

title: Dempster–Shafer Combination
objects: A convolution over the subset lattice.
structure: The combination rule is a Möbius-transform convolution on the lattice of subsets, computable by fast transforms analogous to the FFT. Its normalisation by conflict 𝐾produces counterintuitive results when the sources strongly disagree.
reduction: Combination is a lattice convolution with a fast transform.

title: Markov Decision Process
objects: A transition tensor 𝑃(𝑠′ ∣𝑠, 𝑎) and a reward vector.
structure: For a fixed policy, 𝑃𝜋is a stochastic matrix and the problem becomes a linear system — the whole of policy evaluation. The action dimension is what makes optimisation nonlinear, via the max.
reduction: An MDP is a stochastic tensor plus a reward vector.

title: Bellman Expectation Equation
objects: A linear system in the value vector.
structure: Exactly v = (𝐼−𝛾𝑃𝜋)−1r, and the inverse exists because 𝛾< 1 makes 𝛾𝑃𝜋a contraction with spectral radius below one. Policy evaluation is literally a matrix inversion, and the Neumann series ∑𝛾𝑘(𝑃𝜋)𝑘is the discounted return.
reduction: Policy evaluation is a linear solve; the return is a Neumann series.
status: Exact linear. The field’s central matrix equation.

title: Bellman Optimality Equation
objects: A fixed point of a max-aﬀine operator.
structure: The max makes it nonlinear, but the operator is still a 𝛾-contraction in the sup norm — so a unique fixed point exists by Banach. Each policy’s evaluation is linear; the max over policies is what is not.
reduction: The operator is max-aﬀine: linear per policy, nonlinear across them.

title: Q-Function
objects: A value matrix indexed by state and action.
structure: 𝑄is a matrix where 𝑉is a vector — the extra action index is what makes greedy improvement possible without a model. Its low-rank structure in many problems is what value factorisation methods exploit.
reduction: 𝑄is the state–action value matrix.

title: Value Iteration Contraction
objects: A contraction mapping with modulus 𝛾.
structure: Convergence is geometric at rate 𝛾, so the number of iterations for accuracy 𝜀is log 𝜀/ log 𝛾— the same reciprocal-log structure as any linear iterative solver. The discount factor is exactly the convergence rate.
reduction: Value iteration is a contraction; 𝛾is its rate.

title: Q-Learning Update
objects: A stochastic approximation step toward a Bellman target.
structure: Exactly Robbins–Monro stochastic approximation on the optimality operator, converging under the usual step-size conditions. With linear function approximation the update becomes a stochastic linear iteration, and off-policy sampling can make its expected update matrix unstable — the deadly triad is a spectral radius problem.
reduction: Q-learning is stochastic approximation; instability is a spectral radius issue.

title: SARSA Update
objects: The on-policy counterpart, without the max.
structure: Removing the max makes the expected update exactly linear in 𝑄, which is why SARSA with linear approximation has convergence guarantees that Q-learning lacks. The difference between the two algorithms is precisely the difference between a linear and a max-aﬀine operator.
reduction: SARSA’s expected update is linear; Q-learning’s is not.

title: TD(𝜆) Eligibility Traces
objects: An exponentially weighted accumulation of gradients.
structure: The trace is a geometric filter applied to the gradient sequence — a linear recursion. The forward view shows TD(𝜆) is a geometrically weighted average of 𝑛-step returns, so 𝜆interpolates linearly between TD(0) and Monte Carlo.
reduction: Traces are a geometric filter; 𝜆is a linear interpolation weight.

title: Policy Gradient Theorem
objects: An expectation of a score function times a value.
structure: The gradient of the objective involves no derivative of the state distribution — that term cancels exactly, which is the theorem’s content. The remaining expression is a linear functional of 𝑄weighted by the score.
reduction: The theorem is an exact cancellation leaving a linear functional.

title: Advantage Function and Baseline
objects: A centring of the value matrix by its row means. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 41
structure: Subtracting any state-dependent baseline leaves the gradient unbiased, because the score function has zero mean under the policy — an orthogonality condition. The variance-minimising baseline is a weighted mean, and 𝑉is a good approximation to it.
reduction: Baselines exploit an orthogonality; centring reduces variance.

title: Generalised Advantage Estimation
objects: A geometrically weighted sum of TD errors.
structure: Exactly a geometric filter applied to the TD error sequence, so 𝜆trades bias against variance along a one-parameter family. It is the same exponential weighting as eligibility traces, seen from the forward direction.
reduction: GAE is a geometric filter on TD errors. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 42

title: Trust Region Policy Constraint
objects: A quadratic constraint given by the Fisher information matrix.
structure: To second order the KL divergence is 1 2Δ𝜃⊤𝐹Δ𝜃, so the trust region is an ellipsoid in the Fisher metric. The natural gradient 𝐹−1∇𝐽is the steepest ascent direction in that metric — a linear solve against the Fisher matrix.
reduction: The trust region is a Fisher-metric ellipsoid; the natural gradient is a linear solve.

title: PPO Clipped Objective
objects: A piecewise linear surrogate in the probability ratio.
structure: The clip makes the objective piecewise linear in 𝑟𝑡with zero gradient outside the trust band — a rectifier that removes the incentive to move too far. It approximates the trust region constraint without the Fisher matrix solve.
reduction: Clipping is a rectifier producing a piecewise linear objective.

title: Soft Actor-Critic Objective
objects: A reward objective plus an entropy bonus.
structure: The optimal policy becomes a Boltzmann distribution over Q-values with temperature 𝛼— a softmax, the same normalised weight vector as everywhere else. Entropy regularisation smooths the max into a log-sum- exp, which is the soft Bellman operator.
reduction: Entropy regularisation replaces max with log-sum-exp; the policy is a softmax.
status: Exact linear apart from the softmax.

title: POMDP Belief Update
objects: A matrix–vector product followed by a diagonal reweighting.
structure: Exactly the forward algorithm of an HMM: propagate by the transition matrix, reweight by the observation likelihood, renormalise. The belief is a probability vector and the update is linear before normalisation, so a POMDP is an MDP on the belief simplex.
reduction: Belief update is a linear operator plus a normalisation.

title: Value of Information
objects: A difference of two expectations with max and expectation interchanged.
structure: Non-negative by Jensen’s inequality, since the max of an expectation is at most the expectation of a max — information cannot hurt a rational agent. The gap is exactly the Jensen slack, hence a curvature quantity.
reduction: VOI is a Jensen gap between max and expectation.

title: Nash Equilibrium in Multi-Agent RL
objects: A fixed point of the best-response correspondence.
structure: For two-player zero-sum games the equilibrium is the value of a linear program, and the minimax theorem is LP duality. For general-sum games it is a complementarity problem — no longer linear, and computing it is PPAD-complete.
reduction: Zero-sum equilibria are linear programs; general-sum ones are not.

title: Fictitious Self-Play
objects: An averaging iteration on the strategy simplex.
structure: The empirical average is a running mean — a linear accumulation — and in zero-sum games the averages converge to equilibrium. Convergence follows from the same argument as no-regret learning.
reduction: Self-play averages strategies; convergence is a no-regret result.

title: Counterfactual Regret Minimisation
objects: A rectified regret vector, normalised into a strategy.
structure: Regret matching normalises the positive part of the cumulative regret vector — a rectifier plus an ℓ1 normalisation. Average regret falls as 1/ √ 𝑇, and in zero-sum games that gives convergence to equilibrium.
reduction: The strategy is a normalised rectified regret vector.

title: Shapley Value for Credit Assignment
objects: A weighted average of marginal contributions.
structure: Exactly a linear functional of the characteristic function — the unique one satisfying eﬀiciency, sym- metry, linearity, and the null player axiom. Linearity in 𝑣is literally one of the defining axioms, which makes this the most explicitly linear entry in the chapter.
reduction: The Shapley value is the unique linear functional satisfying four axioms.

title: Language Model Objective
objects: A sum of log conditional probabilities.
structure: The chain rule of probability makes the joint log-likelihood exactly additive over positions — a sum, which is why autoregressive training parallelises across positions with causal masking. That masking is a triangular matrix.
reduction: The objective is additive in logs; causal masking is a triangular matrix.

title: Perplexity
objects: The exponential of the mean negative log-likelihood.
structure: Exactly the geometric mean of the inverse probabilities, so it is a linear quantity in log space. It is interpretable as an effective branching factor — the size of a uniform distribution with the same entropy.
reduction: Perplexity is exponentiated mean surprisal.

title: Temperature Sampling
objects: A scalar rescaling of the logit vector.
structure: Dividing logits by 𝑇is a linear map before the softmax, so temperature interpolates between the argmax (𝑇→0) and the uniform distribution (𝑇→∞). It is a one-parameter family of reweightings.
reduction: Temperature is a scalar scaling of the logits.

title: Nucleus (Top-p) Sampling
objects: A truncation of the sorted probability vector.
structure: Sorting is a permutation and truncation is a masking, so the operation is a permutation, a cumulative sum, and a threshold — all linear except the threshold. It adapts the support size to the distribution’s shape, unlike top-k.
reduction: Nucleus sampling is a permutation, cumulative sum, and mask.

title: Beam Search
objects: A bounded-width search maximising an additive score.
structure: Scores accumulate additively in log space, so beam search is an approximate max over paths in a lattice — a truncated tropical computation. Length normalisation is a division that corrects the bias toward short sequences.
reduction: Beam search is truncated max-plus path search.

title: RLHF Reward Model
objects: A Bradley–Terry model — logistic in a score difference.
structure: The log odds of a preference are exactly the difference of two scalar scores, so the reward model is identified only up to an additive constant. Fitting it is logistic regression on pairwise contrasts.
reduction: Preference learning is logistic regression on score differences.

title: KL-Regularised Policy Objective
objects: A reward maximisation penalised by divergence from a reference.
structure: The closed-form optimum is 𝜋∗∝𝜋ref exp(𝑟/𝛽) — an exponential tilting of the reference, which is a diagonal reweighting followed by normalisation. That closed form is the basis of the next entry.
reduction: The optimum is an exponential tilting of the reference policy.

title: Direct Preference Optimisation
objects: A logistic loss on a difference of log-ratio terms.
structure: Inverting entry 59’s closed form expresses the implicit reward as a log ratio, so the reward model is eliminated algebraically and preference learning becomes direct supervised training. The whole derivation is a change of variables in log space — one of the cleaner algebraic simplifications in recent machine learning.
reduction: DPO substitutes the closed-form optimum, turning RL into logistic regression on log ratios.

title: Homogeneous Transformation
objects: A 4 × 4 matrix combining rotation and translation.
structure: Composition of transforms is matrix multiplication, and inversion is 𝑇−1 = ( 𝑅⊤−𝑅⊤p 0⊤ 1 ) — closed form, no numerical inversion needed. Embedding translation into a linear map on homogeneous coordinates is the trick that makes aﬀine motion linear.
reduction: Rigid motion is matrix multiplication in homogeneous coordinates.

title: Rotation Matrix Properties
objects: The special orthogonal group 𝑆𝑂(3).
structure: Orthogonality means the columns are an orthonormal frame, so 𝑅−1 = 𝑅⊤and rotations preserve lengths and angles exactly. The constraint surface is a three-dimensional manifold inside nine-dimensional matrix space — six constraints, three degrees of freedom.
reduction: Rotations are orthogonal matrices; the group is a constraint manifold.

title: Euler Angles and Gimbal Lock
objects: A product of three elementary rotation matrices.
structure: Gimbal lock occurs when the parametrisation’s Jacobian loses rank — two axes align and a degree of freedom is lost. It is a chart singularity, not a physical one, and it exists because no three-parameter chart covers 𝑆𝑂(3) globally.
reduction: Gimbal lock is a rank deficiency of the parametrisation Jacobian.
status: Exact linear, with a chart singularity.

title: Axis–Angle and Rodrigues Formula
objects: The exponential map from a skew-symmetric matrix.
structure: 𝑅= 𝑒𝜃[ ̂𝜔]× — the exponential of a skew matrix is orthogonal, which is the Lie algebra to Lie group map. Rodrigues’ formula is the closed form because [ ̂𝜔]3 × = −[ ̂𝜔]× truncates the series.
reduction: Rotation is the matrix exponential of a skew matrix.

title: Unit Quaternion Rotation
objects: A conjugation in the quaternion algebra.
structure: Quaternions double-cover 𝑆𝑂(3), so 𝑞and −𝑞give the same rotation — the group 𝑆3 maps two-to-one onto 𝑆𝑂(3). They avoid gimbal lock because 𝑆3 is a global chart, and composition is a bilinear product.
reduction: Quaternion multiplication is bilinear; the map to 𝑆𝑂(3) is two-to-one.

title: Twist and Screw Motion
objects: An element of the Lie algebra 𝔰𝔢(3) — a six-vector.
structure: Twists form a vector space, so they can be added and scaled, unlike the group elements themselves. Chasles’ theorem says every rigid motion is a screw — a rotation about an axis with translation along it, which is the twist’s canonical decomposition.
reduction: Twists live in a six-dimensional Lie algebra — a genuine vector space.

title: Denavit–Hartenberg Transform
objects: A product of four elementary transforms per joint.
structure: The convention reduces six pose parameters to four by aligning frames with the joint axes — a canonical form removing two redundant degrees of freedom. It is a basis choice that minimises parameters.
reduction: DH is a canonical parametrisation reducing six parameters to four.

title: Forward Kinematics
objects: An ordered product of joint transforms.
structure: Exactly a matrix product, evaluated in 𝑂(𝑛) — the map from joint angles to end-effector pose. It is a smooth but nonlinear map from the joint torus to 𝑆𝐸(3); the linearity is in the composition, not in the dependence on q.
reduction: Forward kinematics is a matrix product, nonlinear in the joint angles.

title: Manipulator Jacobian
objects: A 6 × 𝑛matrix mapping joint rates to end-effector twist.
structure: The central object of manipulator analysis: its column space is the set of achievable twists, its null space is the internal motions that do not move the tool, and its singular values are the gains in each direction. Force maps transpose: 𝜏= 𝐽⊤ℱ, an exact duality.
reduction: The Jacobian is a linear map; kinematics and statics are dual through it.

title: Inverse Kinematics via Pseudoinverse
objects: A minimum-norm solution plus a null space projection.
structure: 𝐽+ gives the least-norm solution; (𝐼−𝐽+𝐽) projects onto ker 𝐽, so redundant arms can pursue secondary objectives without disturbing the tool. This single equation is the reason redundancy is useful, and it is pure pseudoinverse algebra.
reduction: IK is a pseudoinverse solve plus a null space projection.

title: Damped Least Squares
objects: A Tikhonov-regularised inverse.
structure: Adding 𝜆2𝐼shifts every singular value away from zero, so the solution stays bounded near singularities — exactly ridge regression applied to a kinematic solve. The damping trades tracking accuracy for conditioning.
reduction: Damping is Tikhonov regularisation of the Jacobian inverse.

title: Manipulability Measure
objects: The product of the Jacobian’s singular values. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 13
structure: The volume of the manipulability ellipsoid, whose axes are the singular vectors scaled by the singular values. It vanishes exactly at singularities, so maximising it is a conditioning objective.
reduction: Manipulability is the product of singular values.

title: Kinematic Singularity
objects: A rank deficiency of the Jacobian. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 14
structure: At a singularity some direction becomes unreachable and the required joint velocities blow up — the smallest singular value hits zero, so the condition number diverges. Every singularity in robotics is this one linear-algebraic event.
reduction: Singularity is Jacobian rank loss.

title: Differential Drive Kinematics
objects: A 2 × 2 linear map from wheel speeds to body twist.
structure: Exactly invertible, so wheel commands follow from a desired twist by a matrix inverse. The sum and difference structure means it is a change of basis to symmetric and antisymmetric modes. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 15
reduction: The map is an invertible 2 × 2 matrix.

title: Ackermann Steering
objects: A geometric constraint for slip-free turning.
structure: Both wheels must be tangent to circles about a common centre, which is a linear condition on the cotangents. The bicycle model linearises this to a single steering angle, which is the standard control abstraction.
reduction: The constraint is linear in the cotangents.

title: Nonholonomic Constraint
objects: A linear constraint on velocities that is not integrable.
structure: Linear in ̇q but not derivable from a positional constraint, so the reachable configuration space remains full-dimensional even though instantaneous motions are restricted. Chow’s theorem: the Lie brackets of the allowed vector fields span everything — a car can reach any pose by parallel parking, and the bracket is the algebraic reason.
reduction: The constraint is linear in velocity; controllability comes from Lie brackets.
status: Exact linear (the constraint), with a non-integrable structure.

title: Manipulator Equation of Motion
objects: A configuration-dependent mass matrix and a velocity coupling matrix.
structure: 𝑀is symmetric positive definite, so it defines a metric on the configuration space — the kinetic energy is a quadratic form in ̇q. Linear in ̈q, which is why forward dynamics is a linear solve at each instant.
reduction: The dynamics are linear in acceleration with a positive definite mass matrix.

title: Skew-Symmetry Property
objects: A structural identity linking the mass and Coriolis matrices.
structure: Skew-symmetry means ̇q⊤( ̇ 𝑀−2𝐶) ̇q = 0, so the Coriolis terms do no net work — energy conservation, expressible entirely as a matrix property. It is what makes passivity-based control provably stable.
reduction: Energy conservation is a skew-symmetry of a matrix combination.

title: Recursive Newton–Euler Algorithm
objects: A forward and backward sweep along the kinematic chain.
structure: The chain structure makes the system matrices banded, so the sweeps are exactly forward and backward substitution on a bidiagonal system. Linear cost instead of cubic is the payoff of that structure.
reduction: The algorithm is forward–backward substitution on a banded system.

title: Composite Rigid Body Inertia
objects: An assembly of the mass matrix from link inertias.
structure: Each entry is an inner product of motion subspaces with accumulated inertias, so the matrix is built column by column. Its symmetry halves the work.
reduction: The mass matrix is assembled from inner products.

title: Articulated Body Algorithm
objects: A propagation of articulated inertias down the chain.
structure: Avoids forming and inverting 𝑀by propagating Schur complements along the chain — each joint’s elimination is a rank-one update to the downstream inertia. It is exactly banded Gaussian elimination in physical clothing.
reduction: The algorithm is banded elimination via Schur complements.

title: Operational Space Formulation
objects: The task-space inertia — a congruence transform of the joint-space one.
structure: Λ is the inverse of the projected inverse inertia, which is exactly a Schur complement structure. It lets control be specified in task coordinates while null-space motions are handled separately by the dynamically consistent pseudoinverse.
reduction: Task-space inertia is a congruence transform and Schur complement.

title: Contact Wrench Cone
objects: A second-order cone constraint on contact forces.
structure: The friction cone is convex, so feasibility problems over it are second-order cone programs. Polyhedral approximation replaces it with a set of linear inequalities, which is why most solvers use a linearised friction pyramid.
reduction: The cone is convex; linearising gives a polyhedron.

title: Zero Moment Point
objects: A weighted average of link positions — a generalised centre of pressure.
structure: Exactly a normalised inner product of positions with force weights, so the ZMP is a point in the convex hull of contact points when balanced. Stability is the linear condition that it lies inside the support polygon.
reduction: The ZMP is a weighted average; stability is a convex containment.

title: Linear Inverted Pendulum Model
objects: A linear second-order system with eigenvalues ±√𝑔/𝑧𝑐.
structure: Constraining the centre of mass to a horizontal plane makes the dynamics exactly linear, which is the whole reason the model dominates walking control. One eigenvalue is unstable and one stable — the unstable one is what capture point control cancels.
reduction: The constrained pendulum is an exactly linear system.

title: Capture Point
objects: A projection onto the unstable eigenvector.
structure: The capture point is exactly the coordinate along the unstable eigendirection — stepping to it cancels the divergent mode and brings the robot to rest. It is one of the cleanest applications of eigenvector decomposition in engineering practice.
reduction: The capture point is the unstable modal coordinate.

title: Configuration Space
objects: A manifold, not a vector space.
structure: For a revolute arm 𝒞= 𝑇𝑛, a torus — which is locally like ℝ𝑛but globally is not, so straight-line interpolation is not well defined without care. That topological difference is why planning is not simply a linear problem.
reduction: 𝒞is a manifold; only local charts are linear.

title: Minkowski Sum Obstacle Growth
objects: A set-valued sum.
structure: For convex sets the Minkowski sum’s support function is the sum of the support functions — an exactly linear operation on the support function representation. That linearity is what makes convex collision checking eﬀicient.
reduction: Minkowski sums add support functions linearly.

title: Probabilistic Roadmap Coverage
objects: An exponential coverage guarantee.
structure: Each sample independently covers a region, so the failure probability decays exponentially in sample count — a product of independent complements. The roadmap itself is a graph, and querying it is a shortest path computation.
reduction: Coverage is exponential in samples; queries are graph searches.

title: RRT Growth
objects: A tree growing by nearest-neighbour extension.
structure: A uniformly sampled point is most likely to fall in the largest Voronoi cell, so growth is automatically biased toward frontiers. The Voronoi diagram is a partition induced by a distance metric — the geometry does the exploration.
reduction: Growth bias follows from Voronoi cell volumes under a metric.

title: RRT* Rewiring Radius
objects: A shrinking connection radius ensuring asymptotic optimality.
structure: The radius must shrink slowly enough to keep the random geometric graph connected — the same log 𝑛/𝑛threshold as in percolation on random graphs. The 1/𝑑exponent is where dimensionality bites.
reduction: The radius is a random geometric graph connectivity threshold.

title: Artificial Potential Field
objects: A sum of gradient fields.
structure: Forces superpose exactly because gradients add, so composing behaviours is linear. Local minima are where the gradients cancel — the method’s well-known failure mode, and it is a statement about the potential’s critical points.
reduction: Potentials add; failures are critical points of the sum.

title: Dynamic Window Approach
objects: A weighted sum of objectives over an admissible velocity set.
structure: Exactly a linear scalarisation of a multi-objective problem, evaluated over a box of dynamically feasible velocities. Weight choice determines the trade-off — a point on the Pareto frontier.
reduction: The objective is a linear scalarisation over a feasible box.

title: Velocity Obstacle
objects: A cone in velocity space.
structure: The set of colliding relative velocities is a cone, and avoiding it is a constraint set complement. Reciprocal velocity obstacles split the avoidance effort by a linear half-and-half rule, which makes the cone constraint a half-plane.
reduction: Collision avoidance is a cone constraint; the reciprocal version is a half-plane. The LKVexa Compendium — Calculus Edition 34

title: Trajectory Optimisation Objective
objects: A quadratic control cost plus a nonconvex obstacle term.
structure: Without obstacles it is a linear-quadratic problem with a closed-form solution; obstacles make it nonconvex, so solvers sequentially convexify — solving a sequence of quadratic programs. That sequence is the workhorse of modern trajectory optimisation.
reduction: The problem is solved as a sequence of quadratic programs.

title: Minimum Jerk Trajectory
objects: A quintic polynomial fitted to six boundary conditions.
structure: Six conditions and six coeﬀicients give a square linear system with a Vandermonde matrix, solved exactly. The minimum-jerk objective’s Euler–Lagrange equation is 𝑥(6) = 0, whose solutions are exactly quintics.
reduction: The trajectory solves a Vandermonde linear system.

title: Dubins Path
objects: A finite set of candidate path types.
structure: The optimal path is always one of six combinations of arcs and straight segments, so optimisation reduces to enumerating six closed-form candidates and taking the minimum. It is a discrete selection over analytically solved pieces, not a linear optimisation.
reduction: Optimisation reduces to a finite enumeration.

title: Kalman Filter Prediction
objects: A linear state propagation and a congruence transform of the covariance.
structure: The state map is linear and the covariance transforms by congruence — exactly how a quadratic form transforms under a change of variables. Adding 𝑄is the process noise injection.
reduction: Prediction is a linear map plus a congruence transform.

title: Kalman Filter Update
objects: The optimal linear gain — a weighted least squares solution.
structure: The gain weights prediction against measurement by their relative precisions, and the result is simul- taneously the BLUE, the MAP estimate under Gaussian assumptions, and the recursive least squares solution. The updated covariance (𝐼−𝐾𝐻)𝑃−is a Schur complement.
reduction: The update is a weighted least squares solve; the covariance is a Schur complement.

title: Extended Kalman Filter Linearisation
objects: A Jacobian evaluated at the current estimate.
structure: The EKF applies the exactly-linear Kalman machinery to a first-order approximation, so its optimality guarantees are lost. Divergence occurs when the linearisation point drifts far from the truth — the error of the approximation feeds back into the estimate.
reduction: The EKF linearises then applies the linear filter.

title: Unscented Transform
objects: A deterministic quadrature capturing two moments.
structure: The sigma points are chosen so their weighted mean and covariance match exactly, and propagating them captures the transformed distribution to higher order than a Jacobian does. The point placement uses a matrix square root of the covariance — a Cholesky factor.
reduction: Sigma points come from a covariance matrix square root.

title: Mahalanobis Gating
objects: A quadratic form in the innovation with the innovation covariance as metric.
structure: Exactly a whitened distance, chi-square distributed under correct association. Data association is thresholding this quadratic form, which is why the innovation covariance must be right.
reduction: Gating is a whitened quadratic form.

title: Monte Carlo Localisation
objects: A weighted particle approximation to a pose distribution.
structure: Motion propagates particles through the (nonlinear) kinematics and observations reweight them di- agonally — the same linear-then-normalise structure as any particle filter. It handles multimodality, which the Kalman filter’s single Gaussian cannot.
reduction: Reweighting is diagonal; the representation handles multimodality.

title: SLAM Posterior
objects: A joint distribution over trajectory and map.
structure: The correlations between landmarks are what make SLAM hard and also what make it work — the covariance matrix is dense even though each observation touches few variables. Its inverse, the information matrix, is sparse, which is the key exploited by entry 46.
reduction: The covariance is dense; the information matrix is sparse.

title: Graph SLAM Objective
objects: A weighted nonlinear least squares problem.
structure: Solved by Gauss–Newton, each iteration is a linear system 𝐻Δx = −b with 𝐻= ∑𝐽⊤Ω𝐽— a sum of rank-limited contributions. Each edge adds a small block, so 𝐻has exactly the graph’s sparsity pattern.
reduction: Each iteration is a sparse linear solve with graph-structured 𝐻.

title: Information Matrix Sparsity
objects: The inverse covariance, whose zeros encode conditional independence.
structure: A zero entry means the two variables are conditionally independent given the rest, and in SLAM each measurement couples only a few variables — so Ω is sparse where Σ is dense. Exploiting this sparsity with sparse Cholesky is what made large-scale SLAM tractable.
reduction: Sparsity of the information matrix is conditional independence.

title: Bundle Adjustment
objects: A large sparse nonlinear least squares problem.
structure: The Hessian has a bipartite block structure (cameras and points), and the Schur complement trick eliminates the points block — which is block-diagonal and trivially invertible — leaving a much smaller camera system. That Schur complement is what makes bundle adjustment feasible on millions of points.
reduction: The Schur complement exploits the bipartite Hessian structure.

title: Pinhole Camera Projection
objects: A 3 × 4 projection matrix acting on homogeneous coordinates.
structure: Projection is exactly a linear map in homogeneous coordinates followed by a division — so it is linear projectively but not aﬀinely. That projective linearity is what makes the entire structure-from-motion machinery algebraic.
reduction: Projection is a linear map in projective coordinates.

title: Epipolar Constraint
objects: A bilinear form with a rank-two matrix.
structure: The fundamental matrix has rank exactly two (det 𝐹= 0), and its null vectors are the epipoles. Estimating it from correspondences is a linear system solved by SVD, then projected back to rank two by zeroing the smallest singular value — a textbook Eckart–Young truncation.
reduction: 𝐹is a rank-two matrix estimated by SVD and rank-truncated.

title: RANSAC Iteration Count
objects: A required sample count from a geometric distribution.
structure: Each trial independently succeeds with probability 𝑤𝑠, so the count follows from a geometric tail — linear in logs. Sensitivity to the minimal sample size 𝑠is exponential, which is why minimal solvers matter.
reduction: The count inverts a geometric probability.

title: Computed Torque Control
objects: An exact feedback linearisation of the manipulator dynamics.
structure: Cancelling the nonlinear terms makes the closed-loop error dynamics exactly ̈e + 𝐾𝐷̇e + 𝐾𝑃e = 0 — a linear second-order system with placeable poles. It converts a nonlinear plant into a linear one by exact cancellation, and its weakness is that the cancellation requires a perfect model.
reduction: Feedback linearisation makes the error dynamics exactly linear.

title: PD Plus Gravity Compensation
objects: A linear feedback law with one nonlinear correction.
structure: Global asymptotic stability follows from a Lyapunov argument using the skew-symmetry property of entry 18 — no exact model of 𝑀or 𝐶is needed. That robustness is why it is preferred when the model is uncertain.
